hardJudge.note: 정답 B(evoke) 검산 완료: "rather than describe"와 "appears only through scattered images"를 연결해야 하며, A(conceal)는 '직접 말하지 않음'과 부분 부합하나 "appears"와 충돌, C(embellish)는 시적 장식과 연관되나 대조 구조와 충돌, D(dismiss)도 문장 성립. 말라르메의 명명 관련 주장, 얼음에 갇힌 백조(Le vierge, le vivace...), 부채(Éventail) 소재 모두 사실에 부합. 한국어·영어 해설 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 원문 지문은 자체 작성으로 보이며 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 말라르메의 'nommer un objet... suggérer' 발언과 백조·부채 시편에 관한 사실 서술이 정확함. conceal이 강한 오답 유인이고, 'rather than describe'와 'appears' 단서를 연결해야 풀 수 있어 medium에 맞음.

Each actor typically played a single stock character, such as the miserly merchant Pantalone or the scheming servant Arlecchino, for an entire career, memorizing a repertoire of jokes, speeches, and comic routines suited to that role. When a scene called for invention, performers drew on this stored material rather than creating lines from nothing, so their apparent improvisation was in fact ______ by years of preparation.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Although commedia dell'arte troupes of sixteenth-century Italy were celebrated for improvising their performances, their spontaneity was less unrestrained than audiences may have assumed. Each actor typically played a single stock character, such as the miserly merchant Pantalone or the scheming servant Arlecchino, for an entire career, memorizing a repertoire of jokes, speeches, and comic routines suited to that role. When a scene called for invention, performers drew on this stored material rather than creating lines from nothing, so their apparent improvisation was in fact ______ by years of preparation.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 배우들이 즉흥처럼 보이는 연기를 할 때 오랜 기간 외워 둔 자료에 기댔다고 설명하므로, 즉흥 연기가 준비에 의해 '뒷받침되었다'는 뜻의 C(underpinned)가 가장 적절하다. A(undermined)는 준비가 즉흥을 약화했다는 뜻이 되어, 준비가 즉흥을 가능하게 했다는 지문 논리와 반대된다. B(concealed)는 관객이 즉흥이라고 여겼다는 점과 일부 맞아 보이지만, 즉흥이 준비를 숨긴 것이지 준비가 즉흥을 숨긴 것이 아니므로 관계가 뒤집혀 있다. D(complicated)는 즉흥이 생각보다 단순하지 않았다는 첫 문장과 얼핏 맞아 보이지만, 준비가 즉흥을 더 어렵게 만들었다는 근거는 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage explains that when actors seemed to improvise, they were actually drawing on material they had memorized over many years, so their improvisation was supported by, or "underpinned" by, that preparation. That makes C correct. A, "undermined," would mean the preparation weakened the improvisation, which is the opposite of the passage's point that preparation made it possible. B, "concealed," might seem to fit because audiences thought the acting was spontaneous, but it gets the relationship backward: the improvisation hid the preparation, not the other way around. D, "complicated," seems to echo the first sentence's idea that improvisation was less simple than it looked, but nothing in the passage says preparation made improvising harder.

In his late self-portraits, he lets deep shadow swallow much of the clothing and background, allowing light to fall chiefly on the furrowed brow and tired eyes. Art historians argue that this selective illumination is not mere technical display: by withholding detail elsewhere, Rembrandt ______ the viewer's attention on the face, so that the sitter's inner weariness, rather than his status or wealth, becomes the subject of the painting.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 렘브란트가 다른 곳의 세부를 감추어 얼굴로 관람자의 시선을 모은다고 말하므로, 주의를 한곳에 '집중시킨다'는 D가 가장 정확하다. A는 주의를 흩뜨린다는 뜻이라 지문의 논리와 정반대이다. B는 빛이라는 주제와 연결되어 그럴듯하지만, 빛을 비추는 대상은 얼굴이지 관람자의 '주의'가 아니므로 'attention on the face'와 맞지 않는다. C도 빛과 관련된 단어이지만 주의를 반사한다는 것은 시선을 한곳에 모은다는 의미를 전달하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says that by withholding detail elsewhere, Rembrandt draws the viewer's attention onto the face, so D, "concentrates," is the most precise choice: it means gathering attention in one spot. A means scattering attention, which is the opposite of what the passage describes. B sounds tempting because the passage is about light, but what gets lit is the face, not the viewer's "attention," so it doesn't fit "attention on the face." C is also a light-related word, but "reflecting" attention doesn't mean pulling it into one place.

A means "foreshadowed," but his work came out in the 1920s alongside the Art Deco movement, not before it. C means "hid," which is the opposite of the work making the commitment visible. Which finding, if true, would most directly support Demir's claim?
problem.stimulus: In many medieval Islamic manuscripts of the Qur'an, the pages that open a volume are covered with dense geometric interlace framing a few lines of script. Some art historians have treated these frontispieces as mainly decorative, a show of the workshop's skill meant to impress wealthy patrons. Art historian Leyla Demir argues for a different reading: the geometric ornament, she claims, worked as a visual sign of the sacred status of the text itself, so illuminators set aside their most elaborate patterns for passages that held special religious weight, not for whatever pages were most visible to a buyer.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Demir's claim?
options: In manuscripts made for the wealthiest patrons, the opening pages carry more intricate geometric interlace than the opening pages of manuscripts made for less wealthy buyers.
In the manuscripts studied, the most intricate geometric interlace is found on opening pages, which buyers commonly examined first when judging a workshop's work.

In the manuscripts studied, the most intricate geometric interlace frames the Throne Verse and the opening chapter even when those passages fall deep inside a volume, and pages of comparable visibility nearby carry plain borders.
In the manuscripts studied, geometric interlace patterns closely resemble those found on palace tilework produced in the same cities during the same period.
problem.explanation: 데미르의 주장은 가장 정교한 문양이 가장 눈에 띄는 페이지가 아니라 종교적으로 중요한 구절에 쓰였다는 것이다. C는 권 중간의 눈에 덜 띄는 위치에서도 중요한 구절에만 정교한 문양이 있고, 비슷하게 보이는 주변 페이지는 소박하다고 하므로 두 설명을 구별해 데미르를 지지한다. A는 문양의 정교함이 후원자의 부와 함께 달라진다는 것이어서 오히려 장식·과시 해석에 맞는다. B는 정교한 문양이 구매자가 먼저 보는 첫 페이지에 몰려 있다는 것이므로 경쟁 해석과 일치한다. D는 궁전 타일과의 유사성만 보여 줄 뿐, 문양이 신성한 구절을 표시했는지와는 관계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Demir claims that the most elaborate patterns marked passages of special religious weight, not the pages most visible to buyers. C supports this because the intricate interlace follows the important passages even deep inside a volume, while nearby pages that are just as visible get plain borders, so it separates her reading from the display explanation. A ties how intricate the ornament is to how wealthy the patron was, which fits the decorative, impress-the-patron view instead. B puts the finest work on the opening pages buyers looked at first, which is exactly what the rival view would predict. D shows only that the patterns look like palace tilework, which tells you nothing about whether the ornament marked sacred passages.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Qur'anic Arabic calligraphy and Islamic geometric pattern sacred text artistic veneration religious visual tradition

hardJudge.note: 정답 C는 '종교적 중요 구절 vs. 가시성 높은 페이지'라는 두 설명을 직접 구별하는 조건(권 내부 깊숙한 위치 + 비슷한 가시성의 인접 페이지는 소박)을 모두 담아 데미르 주장을 가장 직접 지지함. A·B는 경쟁(장식·과시) 해석을 뒷받침하는 그럴듯한 오답, D는 무관한 유사성 자료로 적절히 배제됨. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 결론 동일, 한글 혼입 없음. 사소한 점: '개경장(opening chapter)'은 실제로 권의 첫머리에 놓이는 것이 보통이라 'even when those passages fall deep inside a volume'이 왕좌의 구절(2:255)에는 자연스럽지만 개경장에는 다소 어색함—다만 'even when'이라는 조건부 표현이고 문항의 논리나 정답 판별에 영향이 없어 사실 오류로 판정하지 않음. 난이도는 표준 SAT medium 수준에 부합.

advisory.note: C는 종교적 중요성과 눈에 띄는 정도를 분리해 데미르의 주장을 직접 지지한다. A와 B는 지문에 나온 경쟁 해석을 그럴듯하게 담은 오답이고, D는 관련성이 없다. 다만 C의 '비교 가능한 가시성' 조건이 다소 노골적이어서 medium 하단에 가깝다.

problem.passage:
Many medieval manuscripts are palimpsests: parchment whose original text was scraped away so the leaves could be reused for a new text. Using ultraviolet and multispectral imaging, conservators have recovered faint traces of these erased layers. One such codex, now held in a monastery library, contains a twelfth-century prayer book written over an older Greek mathematical treatise. Historian Lena Marwick argues that the scribe who erased the treatise did not choose it at random. She thinks the scribe deliberately chose a text that no one in the community could read anymore, since by the twelfth century the monastery's members no longer understood technical Greek, and so the treatise had become useless parchment to them.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marwick's claim?
problem.stimulus: Many medieval manuscripts are palimpsests: parchment whose original text was scraped away so the leaves could be reused for a new text. Using ultraviolet and multispectral imaging, conservators have recovered faint traces of these erased layers. One such codex, now held in a monastery library, contains a twelfth-century prayer book written over an older Greek mathematical treatise. Historian Lena Marwick argues that the scribe who erased the treatise did not choose it at random. She thinks the scribe deliberately chose a text that no one in the community could read anymore, since by the twelfth century the monastery's members no longer understood technical Greek, and so the treatise had become useless parchment to them.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marwick's claim?
options: Other twelfth-century codices from the same monastery were written over erased Greek technical works, while the monastery's Latin texts from the same period were copied and kept whole.
Ultraviolet imaging shows that the erased Greek treatise in the codex contained diagrams and calculations that are not found in any other surviving copy.
Records show that the monastery's twelfth-century scribes often scraped and reused parchment because new animal skins were expensive and hard to obtain.
Multispectral analysis shows that the treatise was erased more thoroughly in some parts of the codex than in others, which suggests that more than one scribe did the scraping.
problem.explanation: Marwick의 주장은 필경사가 공동체에서 더 이상 읽히지 않는 그리스 기술 문헌을 일부러 골라 지웠다는 것이다. A는 같은 수도원에서 그리스 기술 문헌은 계속 지워진 반면 읽을 수 있는 라틴어 문헌은 보존되었음을 보여 주므로, 의도적이고 이해 가능성에 따른 선택이었다는 주장을 직접 뒷받침한다. B는 이 논문의 희귀성을 보여 줄 뿐, 필경사가 왜 이것을 골랐는지는 설명하지 못한다. C는 양피지를 재사용한 이유(비용)를 설명하지만, 어떤 문헌을 지울지 고른 기준은 다루지 않으며 오히려 우연한 선택으로도 해석될 수 있다. D는 지우는 작업을 누가 어떻게 했는지에 관한 것이어서 선택의 동기와는 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Marwick claims the scribe deliberately picked a Greek technical text because the community could no longer read it. A shows a pattern: at the same monastery, Greek technical works kept getting erased while readable Latin texts were preserved, so it directly supports a deliberate selection based on what people could understand. B only shows that the treatise is rare. It doesn't explain why the scribe chose it. C explains why parchment was reused at all (cost), but it says nothing about how the scribe picked which text to erase, and it fits random reuse just as well. D is about how the scraping was done and by whom, so it doesn't tell us why this text was chosen.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Palimpsest erased manuscript recovery and medieval textual archaeology ultraviolet imaging hidden layer restoration

hardJudge.note: Marwick의 주장(읽을 수 없게 된 그리스 기술 문헌을 의도적으로 선택)을 A의 선택적 패턴(그리스 기술서는 지우고 라틴어 문헌은 보존)이 직접 뒷받침함을 검산으로 확인. B(희귀성)·D(지운 방식/인원)는 동기와 무관, C(비용)는 재사용 일반 이유로 선택 기준을 다루지 않아 배제 가능. C가 그럴듯한 부분 근거를 가진 오답으로 기능하며 B도 지문 소재와 연결되어 비교가 필요하므로 medium에 적합. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 팔림프세스트·UV/다중분광 영상 관련 서술은 사실에 부합하며, 역사가는 가공 인물로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: A는 선택적 삭제 패턴(그리스 기술서는 지움, 라틴어는 보존)을 보여 의도적·가독성 기반 선택을 직접 지지함. C는 재사용 동기라 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능하고, B·D는 관련은 있으나 선택 기준과 무관함. medium 수준에 적합.

problem.passage:
Literary historians long treated the lyrics of twelfth-century troubadours in southern France as a kind of rulebook: in poem after poem, a knight pledges humble service to a married noblewoman, praises her from a distance, and suffers patiently, and scholars assembled these recurring gestures into a fixed code of fin'amor, or courtly love. Historian Simone Arnaud argues, however, that this reading ______ how often the poets mocked those very conventions, as when Guilhem IX boasts of his devotion in one stanza and parodies it in the next.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Literary historians long treated the lyrics of twelfth-century troubadours in southern France as a kind of rulebook: in poem after poem, a knight pledges humble service to a married noblewoman, praises her from a distance, and suffers patiently, and scholars assembled these recurring gestures into a fixed code of fin'amor, or courtly love. Historian Simone Arnaud argues, however, that this reading ______ how often the poets mocked those very conventions, as when Guilhem IX boasts of his devotion in one stanza and parodies it in the next.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation:
정답 D(overlooks): 지문 첫 부분은 학자들이 반복되는 표현을 고정된 규범으로 정리했다는 기존 견해를 소개하고, 'however' 뒤에서 Arnaud가 반박한다. 그 해석이 시인들이 관습을 조롱한 사실을 '간과한다'고 지적해야 Guilhem IX 예시와 논리가 맞는다.
A(codifies): 첫 단계(학자들이 규범을 체계화함)에는 어울리지만, 반박 단계에서 '조롱을 체계화한다'는 말은 비판이 되지 못한다.
B(concerns): 중립적인 단어라 '이 해석이 조롱에 관한 것이다'가 되어 반박의 기능이 없고, 오히려 기존 해석이 조롱을 다룬다는 뜻이 되어 지문과 반대된다.
C(neglectful of): 뜻은 '간과하다'와 비슷하지만 형용사구라서 동사가 들어가야 할 자리(this reading ___ how...)에 문법적으로 들어갈 수 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer D (overlooks): The first part of the text lays out the traditional view that scholars turned recurring gestures into a fixed code. After "however," Arnaud pushes back by saying this reading misses how often the poets mocked those conventions. The Guilhem IX example supports exactly that criticism.
A (codifies) fits the first part, where scholars organize the conventions into a code. But saying the reading "codifies" the mockery doesn't work as a criticism.
B (concerns) is neutral. It would mean the traditional reading is about the mockery, which doesn't rebut anything and actually contradicts the text.
C (neglectful of) means roughly the same thing, but it's an adjective phrase. The sentence needs a verb after "this reading," so it's grammatically wrong.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 '기존 학계 해석(규범화) → however 이후 Arnaud의 반박' 두 단계로 명확히 구분되고, 빈칸은 반박 단계 시작부에 위치한다. 'overlooks'는 반박 기능(기존 해석이 조롱을 놓쳤다)에 정확히 부합하며 Guilhem IX 예시와 논리적으로 연결된다. A 'codifies'는 첫 단계('assembled... into a fixed code')에 어울리는 유인 오답, C 'neglectful of'는 의미는 유사하나 형용사구로 동사 자리에 부적합한 품사 오답, B는 중립어로 반박 기능 부재. 사실 관계(Guilhem IX의 궁정연애 찬양과 패러디 병존, fin'amor 용어, 12세기 남프랑스 트루바두르) 문제 없음. Simone Arnaud는 가상 인물로 보이나 문항 성립에 지장 없음. 정답 도출 자체는 'however'+'mocked' 단서로 비교적 직접적이어서 hard 중에서는 난도가 낮은 편이나, 두 서술 단계 구조화와 관계 역전 추론을 요구하므로 medium 초과로 판정.

advisory.note: 기존 견해 다음에 'however'로 반박하는 전형적인 구조라서 'overlooks'가 곧바로 떠오른다. C는 품사가 맞지 않아 문법만으로 지울 수 있고, B는 중립어라 반박 기능이 없어 쉽게 걸러진다. 남는 매력적인 오답은 A뿐이며, 어려움은 대부분 troubadour 배경 서술의 길이에서 나온다. 역전 관계 추론이나 다중 단서 종합을 실제로 요구하지 않으므로 전형적인 medium 수준이다.

problem.passage:
Under Justinian I, the sixth-century builders of Hagia Sophia covered its vaults with gold-glass tesserae, small cubes in which gold leaf was sealed between layers of glass. Instead of setting the cubes flat, craftsmen pressed them into the wet plaster at slightly different angles, which took more labor and left the surface visibly uneven. To modern viewers used to smooth, polished finishes, the result can look careless. ______ the irregularity was intentional: the tilted cubes scattered light from windows and lamps, so the golden vaults seemed to shimmer and shift as worshippers moved beneath them.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Under Justinian I, the sixth-century builders of Hagia Sophia covered its vaults with gold-glass tesserae, small cubes in which gold leaf was sealed between layers of glass. Instead of setting the cubes flat, craftsmen pressed them into the wet plaster at slightly different angles, which took more labor and left the surface visibly uneven. To modern viewers used to smooth, polished finishes, the result can look careless. ______ the irregularity was intentional: the tilted cubes scattered light from windows and lamps, so the golden vaults seemed to shimmer and shift as worshippers moved beneath them.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation:
정답 A(Nevertheless): 앞 문장은 현대인의 눈에는 결과물이 '엉성해 보일 수 있다'는 겉모습을 말하고, 마지막 문장은 그 불규칙성이 사실은 빛을 흩뜨리려는 '의도'였다고 말한다. 겉보기 인상과 실제 의도가 대조되므로 양보·대조의 전환어가 맞다.
B(As a result): 기울여 박은 방식의 결과(표면이 울퉁불퉁함, 엉성해 보임)에는 들어맞지만, 지문의 핵심은 결과가 아니라 의도다. '엉성해 보이니까 의도적이었다'는 인과도 성립하지 않는다.
C(Indeed): 앞 문장을 강화·확인하는 말인데, 마지막 문장은 '엉성하다'는 인상을 뒤집으므로 논리 관계가 반대다.
D(For instance): 마지막 문장은 앞 주장의 사례가 아니라 반박이므로 연결되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
A (Nevertheless) is correct. The sentence before the blank describes how the mosaics look: to modern eyes they can seem careless. The last sentence then says the unevenness was actually done on purpose, to scatter light. Because a first impression is being contrasted with the real intention, you need a contrast transition.
B (As a result) fits a consequence of the angled setting, like the uneven surface. But the passage's point is purpose, not outcome, and "it looks careless, so it was intentional" makes no sense as cause and effect.
C (Indeed) would confirm or strengthen the idea that the work looks careless. The final sentence overturns that idea instead.
D (For instance) would bring in an example of the previous claim. The final sentence rebuts that claim, so it isn't an example.

hardJudge.note: 정답 검산: 앞 문장 '현대인에게 엉성해 보일 수 있다'(겉보기 인상) ↔ 마지막 문장 '불규칙성은 의도적이었다'(실제 목적)의 대조이므로 Nevertheless가 유일하게 성립. B는 앞 문단의 '기울여 박음→울퉁불퉁함'이라는 부수적 인과에 끌리지만 '엉성해 보임→의도적'이라는 인과는 불성립(핵심 강조점은 결과가 아닌 의도). C는 강화, D는 예시로 논리 방향이 반대. 사실관계(유스티니아누스 1세, 6세기, 금유리 테세라를 각도를 달리 박아 반짝임을 냄)는 미술사 통설과 일치. 해설 내부 모순 없음. 난이도는 '결과 vs 의도'를 구별해야 하는 점에서 medium을 넘으나, 대조 신호가 비교적 명확해 hard 중 하단 수준으로 판단됨(경계선).

advisory.note: 정답 A는 맞다. '엉성해 보일 수 있다'와 '사실은 의도적이었다'가 바로 앞뒤 문장에서 맞붙는 전형적인 겉보기 인상 대 실제 의도의 대조여서, 빈칸 앞 문장 하나만 읽어도 풀린다. B는 울퉁불퉁한 표면이라는 결과 쪽 사실에 기대는 오답으로 설계됐지만, '엉성해 보인다 → 의도적이었다'가 인과로 읽히지 않아 쉽게 걸러진다. C와 D도 각각 강화·예시 관계라서 반박 구조와 바로 어긋난다. 여러 관찰을 종합하는 추론이나 목적과 내용의 미묘한 구분은 필요하지 않으므로 medium 수준 문항이다.

problem.passage:
In many verses, the thirteenth-century Persian poet Jalaluddin Rumi seems to scorn formal learning: he urges readers to "burn" their books and claims that the intoxication of divine love teaches more than any lecture by theologians. Yet his masterwork, the Masnavi, is full of Quranic citations, legal analogies, and careful philosophical arguments drawn from the very scholarly traditions he appears to mock. ______ Rumi's apparent hostility toward scholarship is best understood not as a rejection of learning itself but as a rejection of learning pursued as an end in itself, cut off from the ecstatic love it should serve.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In many verses, the thirteenth-century Persian poet Jalaluddin Rumi seems to scorn formal learning: he urges readers to "burn" their books and claims that the intoxication of divine love teaches more than any lecture by theologians. Yet his masterwork, the Masnavi, is full of Quranic citations, legal analogies, and careful philosophical arguments drawn from the very scholarly traditions he appears to mock. ______ Rumi's apparent hostility toward scholarship is best understood not as a rejection of learning itself but as a rejection of learning pursued as an end in itself, cut off from the ecstatic love it should serve.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation:
정답 B. 지문은 서로 어긋나 보이는 두 관찰을 제시한다. (1) 루미는 시에서 학문을 경멸하는 듯하다. (2) 그런데 『마스나비』에는 학문적 전거와 논증이 가득하다. 마지막 문장은 이 둘을 함께 설명하는 결론이다. 즉 루미가 거부한 것은 학문 그 자체가 아니라 사랑과 단절된 채 목적이 되어 버린 학문이라는 것이다. 따라서 두 관찰을 종합하는 'Taken together,'가 가장 논리적이다.
A(Indeed,)는 바로 앞 관찰을 강조하거나 덧붙일 때 쓴다. 그런데 마지막 문장은 두 번째 관찰(학문 활용)을 더 밀어붙이는 내용이 아니라 두 관찰을 함께 해석하는 내용이므로, 한쪽 관찰만 반영한 연결이 된다.
C(Nevertheless,)는 두 관찰이 상반된다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 것이다. 이미 두 번째 문장의 'Yet'이 대조를 맡고 있다. 마지막 문장은 그 대조를 해소하는 결론이지 앞 내용에 맞서는 진술이 아니다.
D(Meanwhile,)는 동시에 일어나는 별개의 사실을 이어 붙일 때 쓴다. 결론을 끌어내는 관계와는 무관하다.
problem.explanationEn:
The correct answer is B. The text gives two observations that seem to clash. First, Rumi's verses appear to scorn formal learning. Second, his Masnavi is packed with scholarly citations and arguments. The final sentence offers a conclusion that explains both at once: Rumi wasn't rejecting learning itself, only learning cut off from the love it should serve. Because this conclusion combines the two observations, "Taken together," is the most logical transition.
A ("Indeed,") would strengthen or add to the observation right before it. The final sentence doesn't push the second observation further; it interprets both observations together, so "Indeed," reflects only one side.
C ("Nevertheless,") treats the passage as a simple contrast. But the contrast is already marked by "Yet" in the second sentence. The last sentence resolves that tension instead of opposing what came before.
D ("Meanwhile,") joins separate facts that happen at the same time. It doesn't fit a sentence that draws a conclusion.

hardJudge.note: 두 관찰(학문 경멸 vs. 학문적 전거 활용)이 'Yet'으로 대립 제시되고, 마지막 문장이 이를 해소하는 종합 결론이므로 'Taken together,'가 유일하게 성립. A는 직전 관찰 강화(한쪽만 반영), C는 이미 'Yet'이 맡은 대조를 중복·오적용, D는 무관. 루미·마스나비 관련 사실도 정확. 해설은 정답과 오답 논리 모두 정확히 뒷받침함.

advisory.note: 모순되는 두 관찰을 결론으로 종합하는 구조가 명확하다. 'Yet' 뒤에 Nevertheless를 넣는 단순 대조 함정이 효과적이다. 정답은 B로 유일하다.

problem.passage:
Scholars of medieval Iberian verse have long debated how the muwashshaha, a strophic song form that flourished in al-Andalus, came to end many of its poems with a kharja—a closing refrain often written in colloquial Arabic or in a Romance vernacular rather than in the classical Arabic of the stanzas. One influential account holds that the more a poem was composed to be sung by performers who moved between courtly and popular audiences, the more its kharja drew on the vernacular speech of those audiences, because a familiar closing line let listeners join in. Musicologist Leila Haddad notes that a group of muwashshahat preserved in a twelfth-century Granadan songbook were, according to marginal notes, written specifically for itinerant singers who performed in both palace halls and town markets. If the account is correct, then compared with muwashshahat written only for recitation at court, the Granadan poems should ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Scholars of medieval Iberian verse have long debated how the muwashshaha, a strophic song form that flourished in al-Andalus, came to end many of its poems with a kharja—a closing refrain often written in colloquial Arabic or in a Romance vernacular rather than in the classical Arabic of the stanzas. One influential account holds that the more a poem was composed to be sung by performers who moved between courtly and popular audiences, the more its kharja drew on the vernacular speech of those audiences, because a familiar closing line let listeners join in. Musicologist Leila Haddad notes that a group of muwashshahat preserved in a twelfth-century Granadan songbook were, according to marginal notes, written specifically for itinerant singers who performed in both palace halls and town markets. If the account is correct, then compared with muwashshahat written only for recitation at court, the Granadan poems should ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: have kharjas that rely less on vernacular speech, since singers performing for mixed crowds would favor the prestige of classical Arabic.
have been sung by itinerant performers because their kharjas had already been written in vernacular speech.
have kharjas that reflect the rhyme schemes preferred by twelfth-century Granadan scribes who copied the songbook.
have kharjas that rely more heavily on the everyday speech of the people who heard them performed.
problem.explanation:
이론: 궁정과 대중 청중을 오가는 가수가 부를 목적으로 지어진 시일수록 kharja가 그 청중의 구어(vernacular)를 더 많이 쓴다. 그라나다 시들은 궁정과 시장 모두에서 공연하는 순회 가수용이므로, 궁정 낭송용 시보다 kharja가 구어에 더 크게 의존해야 한다 → D.
A: 관계의 방향을 반대로 뒤집었다(구어를 덜 씀).
B: 원인과 결과를 바꿨다. 이론에서는 공연 맥락이 원인이고 구어 kharja가 결과인데, B는 구어 kharja 때문에 순회 가수가 불렀다고 한다.
C: 필사자의 각운 선호라는, 이론과 상관없는 제3의 요인을 끌어들였다.
problem.explanationEn:
The theory says that the more a poem was written to be sung by performers who moved between courtly and popular audiences, the more its kharja used those audiences' vernacular speech. The Granadan poems were written for singers who performed in both palaces and markets. So compared with poems recited only at court, their kharjas should use more everyday speech. That makes D correct.
A flips the direction of the relationship and predicts less vernacular.
B swaps cause and effect. In the theory, the performance setting shapes the kharja's language, but B claims the vernacular kharjas caused the poems to be sung by itinerant performers.
C brings in a factor the theory never mentions: the scribes' rhyme preferences.

hardJudge.note: 이론 문장("the more … composed to be sung by performers who moved between courtly and popular audiences, the more its kharja drew on the vernacular")이 방향성을 명시하고, 그라나다 시(순회 가수용)라는 새 사례에 적용해 궁정 낭송용 시와 비교하는 구조. D는 방향을 그대로 유지한 유일한 선택지이며, A는 방향 반전, B는 원인-결과 역전(구어 kharja → 순회 가수 공연), C는 이론과 무관한 제3 요인(필사자 각운 선호). 해설이 각 오답의 함정 유형을 정확히 짚고 정답을 수치·논리적으로 뒷받침함. muwashshaha/kharja/al-Andalus 관련 배경 사실은 학계 통설과 부합하며, 인물·송북은 가상의 설정으로 사실 오류 아님. 디지털 SAT inference 문항 형식(빈칸 완성, 4지선다) 충족. 일반 medium 문항 대비 '비교 대상(궁정 전용 시) 대비 방향 판단'과 인과 역전 함정 식별이라는 추가 사고를 요구함.

advisory.note: 정답 D가 맞음. 다만 이론을 사례에 바로 대입하는 한 단계 적용에 그쳐 전형적인 medium 수준임. 방향을 뒤집은 오답(A)과 인과를 바꾼 오답(B)은 금방 걸러지고, 어려움은 전문 어휘와 지문 길이에서만 옴. 정답 D가 'everyday speech'로 바꿔 말했을 뿐 vernacular를 거의 그대로 반복해 정답이 쉽게 드러남.

problem.passage:
Aesthetic philosopher Mieko Arai surveyed visitors at a Kyoto craft exhibition, asking them to rate four tea bowls for "lasting appeal" (1–10) after a first viewing and again after a second viewing one week later. Arai hypothesizes that shibui—an ideal of restrained, understated beauty—reveals itself gradually: a work that truly embodies shibui should gain appeal on repeated viewing, whereas a work whose charm depends on immediate visual impact should lose appeal.

Bowl | Style | First viewing | Second viewing
W | bright glaze, bold pattern | 8.4 | 6.1
X | muted ash glaze, slight asymmetry | 5.2 | 7.6
Y | muted glaze, perfectly symmetrical | 5.9 | 5.8
Z | crackled glaze, bold pattern | 7.1 | 7.3

If Arai's hypothesis is correct, the data suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus:
Aesthetic philosopher Mieko Arai surveyed visitors at a Kyoto craft exhibition, asking them to rate four tea bowls for "lasting appeal" (1–10) after a first viewing and again after a second viewing one week later. Arai hypothesizes that shibui—an ideal of restrained, understated beauty—reveals itself gradually: a work that truly embodies shibui should gain appeal on repeated viewing, whereas a work whose charm depends on immediate visual impact should lose appeal.

Bowl | Style | First viewing | Second viewing
W | bright glaze, bold pattern | 8.4 | 6.1
X | muted ash glaze, slight asymmetry | 5.2 | 7.6
Y | muted glaze, perfectly symmetrical | 5.9 | 5.8
Z | crackled glaze, bold pattern | 7.1 | 7.3

If Arai's hypothesis is correct, the data suggest that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: bowl X, not bowl Y, best embodies shibui, even though both bowls have similarly muted glazes.
bowl W best embodies shibui, since it got the highest ratings of the four bowls at the first viewing.
bowl Y best embodies shibui, since a muted glaze is the defining sign of restrained, understated beauty.
bowl Z best embodies shibui, since its ratings went up over the two viewings the most of the four bowls.
problem.explanation: 가설에 따르면 shibui는 다시 볼 때 매력이 올라가는 것으로 드러난다. 표에서 X는 5.2→7.6(+2.4)로 가장 크게 올랐고, Y는 5.9→5.8로 거의 변화가 없다. 그러므로 유약이 비슷하게 차분해도 X가 shibui에 가장 가깝다(A). B는 표만 보고 첫 관람 점수가 가장 높다는 것만 근거로 삼았다. 가설상 W는 오히려 즉각적인 인상에 기대는 작품이고 점수도 떨어졌다. C는 '차분함'이라는 가설의 문구만 따르고 수치는 무시했다. Y의 점수는 오르지 않았다. D는 표의 항목을 잘못 짝지었다. Z는 0.2 오르는 데 그쳤고 가장 크게 오른 것은 X다.
problem.explanationEn: The hypothesis says true shibui shows itself through appeal that rises when a work is viewed again. Bowl X rose the most (5.2 to 7.6). Bowl Y, despite a similar muted glaze, barely changed (5.9 to 5.8). So X, not Y, best fits, which is choice A. B relies on the table alone: W's high first-viewing score is exactly the kind of immediate impact the hypothesis contrasts with shibui, and W's rating fell. C relies on the hypothesis's wording about restraint and ignores the data, since Y's rating did not rise. D matches the wrong row: Z gained only 0.2, while X gained the most.

hardJudge.note: 검산: W −2.3, X +2.4, Y −0.1, Z +0.2. 가설(반복 관람 시 매력 상승=shibui)을 적용하면 X가 유일하게 유의미한 상승을 보이므로 A가 정답. B는 첫 관람 최고점(표만), C는 '차분한 유약'이라는 텍스트 문구만, D는 최대 상승 항목을 Z로 잘못 연결. 특히 C는 겉모습(차분한 유약)과 가설의 행동적 기준(시간에 따른 상승)을 구별해야 하므로 medium 이상의 사고를 요구함. 해설의 수치·논리 모두 정확.

advisory.note: X +2.4, Z +0.2, Y -0.1, W -2.3이므로 A가 정답이다. 다만 가설을 '재관람 시 상승'으로 읽고 상승폭이 가장 큰 항목만 고르면 풀리는 전형적인 medium 수준 문항이다. 오답 매력도도 낮다. D는 수치를 명백히 틀리게 진술해 표만 확인하면 바로 배제되고, B는 가설과 정면으로 어긋난다. 관계 방향을 뒤집는 함정이나 근거 충분성 판단 같은 hard 요소가 없다.

problem.passage:
Many readers assume that Friedrich Nietzsche wrote in aphorisms because chronic illness and failing eyesight prevented him from sustaining long arguments. Literary scholar Hana Ferreira proposes a different explanation: Nietzsche chose the fragment deliberately, believing that a compressed, unresolved statement forces readers to complete the thought themselves rather than passively accept a finished system. If Ferreira's hypothesis is correct, then one would expect that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Many readers assume that Friedrich Nietzsche wrote in aphorisms because chronic illness and failing eyesight prevented him from sustaining long arguments. Literary scholar Hana Ferreira proposes a different explanation: Nietzsche chose the fragment deliberately, believing that a compressed, unresolved statement forces readers to complete the thought themselves rather than passively accept a finished system. If Ferreira's hypothesis is correct, then one would expect that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Nietzsche's letters from his years of worst illness describe headaches so severe that he could read for only brief periods each day.
Nietzsche's drafts show him cutting connecting explanations from passages he had first written out in full, leaving gaps the reader must fill.
Nietzsche's aphorisms were widely admired by later essayists, several of whom imitated his compressed style in their own philosophical work.
Nietzsche's early training as a classical philologist familiarized him with fragmentary ancient texts, such as surviving pieces of Heraclitus.
problem.explanation:
정답 B: 페헤이라 가설의 핵심 조건은 (1) 단편 형식이 의도적 선택이며 (2) 독자가 생각을 스스로 완성하게 하려는 목적이라는 것이다. 처음엔 완전한 논증으로 쓴 뒤 연결 설명을 일부러 삭제해 빈틈을 남긴 초고는 길게 쓸 능력이 있었음에도 압축을 택했고 그 빈틈을 독자가 채우게 했음을 보여 주므로 두 조건을 모두 직접 충족한다.
A: 지지하는 사실처럼 놓였지만 실제로는 반대 방향으로 작용한다. 질병 때문에 읽고 쓰는 시간이 제한됐다는 증거는 페헤이라가 반박하려는 '건강 탓' 설명을 강화한다.
C: 후대 작가들이 그 문체를 높이 평가하고 모방했다는 것은 수용사일 뿐이어서 겉으로만 관련 있어 보인다. 니체가 의도적으로 택했는지, 무슨 목적이었는지와는 무관하다.
D: 문헌학 훈련은 결론을 지지하는 것처럼 꾸민 배경 정보다. 단편 텍스트를 접했다는 사실이 독자 참여를 위해 단편을 의도적으로 택했다는 점을 보여 주지는 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer B: Ferreira's hypothesis depends on two conditions. First, the fragment form was a deliberate choice. Second, its purpose was to make readers finish the thought themselves. Drafts that were first written out in full and then cut on purpose to leave gaps show both conditions directly. They show Nietzsche could write long passages but chose to compress them, and that the gaps he left are ones the reader has to fill.
A: This is placed as if it supported the hypothesis, but it actually works against it. Evidence that illness limited his reading and writing strengthens the "health made him do it" explanation that Ferreira is arguing against.
C: This only looks relevant. Later admiration and imitation are about how his work was received, and they tell us nothing about whether Nietzsche chose the style on purpose or why.
D: This is background information made to look like support. Knowing fragmentary ancient texts doesn't show that he chose fragments deliberately to involve the reader.

hardJudge.note: 가설(의도적 선택 + 독자 참여 목적)이 명확히 제시되고, B는 두 조건을 모두 직접 충족하는 유일한 선택지. A는 경쟁 설명(질병)을 강화하는 반대 방향 사실, C는 수용사로 무관, D는 '의도적 선택' 가능성은 암시하나 '독자 참여 목적'을 뒷받침하지 못해 조건 일부만 충족하는 매력적 오답. 가설의 두 조건을 분리해 각 선택지의 증거 충분성을 평가해야 하므로 medium 이상의 사고를 요구함. 해설은 정답과 오답 모두 논리적으로 일관되며 사실 오류·저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 '의도적 선택'과 '독자가 생각을 완성하게 함'이라는 두 조건을 직접 충족한다. 오답 구성은 레시피를 따른다(A는 반대 방향, C는 무관, D는 배경 정보). 다만 B만 '빈틈을 독자가 채운다'는 핵심 표현을 거의 그대로 되풀이해서 정답이 바로 드러난다. 이론을 사례에 적용하는 추가 사고나 증거 충분성의 미묘한 판단이 필요 없어 전형적인 medium 수준이고 hard로는 부족하다.

problem.passage:
In ancient Egypt, many families set up a carved stone slab called a stele near a tomb to honor a dead relative. These stelae often showed the person's name along with prayers asking visitors to say offerings of bread and beer aloud. Egyptians believed that a name spoken by the living helped the dead person continue to exist in the afterlife. Some stelae from later periods, however, have the owner's name deliberately chipped away by enemies or rivals. Based on Egyptian beliefs, historians conclude that the people who damaged these names most likely intended to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: In ancient Egypt, many families set up a carved stone slab called a stele near a tomb to honor a dead relative. These stelae often showed the person's name along with prayers asking visitors to say offerings of bread and beer aloud. Egyptians believed that a name spoken by the living helped the dead person continue to exist in the afterlife. Some stelae from later periods, however, have the owner's name deliberately chipped away by enemies or rivals. Based on Egyptian beliefs, historians conclude that the people who damaged these names most likely intended to ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: make room on the stone so that a newer prayer for bread and beer could be carved in that spot.
show visitors that the stele had grown too old and worn to be read aloud anymore.
keep the dead person from being remembered and thus harm that person's existence after death.
honor the dead person by making the stele look more like the stelae of earlier periods.
problem.explanation: 지문은 산 사람이 이름을 말해 주면 죽은 자가 사후 세계에서 계속 존재한다고 Egyptians가 믿었다고 직접 밝히고, 이름을 깎아낸 사람들을 '적이나 경쟁자'라고 부른다. 그러므로 이름을 지우면 아무도 그 이름을 읽어 줄 수 없어 죽은 자의 존재가 해를 입게 되므로 정답은 C이다. A는 공간을 확보하려는 실용적 목적이라는 근거가 지문에 없다. B는 이름을 일부러 깎아낸 행위를 자연스러운 마모와 혼동했다. D는 적들의 행위를 '기리는' 행위로 보아 지문과 반대된다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage tells you directly that Egyptians believed speaking a dead person's name helped that person keep existing in the afterlife, and it calls the people who chipped away the names "enemies or rivals." If the name is gone, no visitor can say it aloud, so the damage was meant to hurt the dead person's existence. That makes C correct. A suggests a practical reason, freeing up space, that the passage never supports. B mixes up deliberate damage with natural wear. D is the opposite of what the passage says, since enemies would not be trying to honor the person.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Stele commemorative monument and ancient Egyptian hieroglyphic inscription funerary stone carving memorial tradition

hardJudge.note: 정답 C는 지문의 명시적 믿음(이름을 말하면 사후 존재 유지)과 '적이나 경쟁자'라는 단서에서 한 단계 추론으로 도출된다. A(공간 확보), B(마모), D(기림)는 지문 근거가 없거나 반대되어 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 표면적으로는 그럴듯한 오개념이다. 역사적 사실(damnatio memoriae 식 이름 삭제, 공양 기원문)도 정확하다. 한국어 해설에 'Egyptians'라는 영어 단어가 섞여 있으나 사소함. 영어 해설에 한글 없음, 자연스러움. 원문 지문은 독창적 작성으로 보여 저작권 의심 없음.

problem.passage:
The maqama is a form of medieval Arabic literature made up of short, separate episodes. In the famous collection by al-Hariri, written around 1100, each episode follows the same pattern: a narrator arrives in a new city, meets a clever wanderer named Abu Zayd, and watches him trick a crowd out of money with a dazzling speech. Each episode ends with Abu Zayd leaving town, and the next one begins somewhere else. Because no episode depends on events from an earlier one, a reader of al-Hariri's collection ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: The maqama is a form of medieval Arabic literature made up of short, separate episodes. In the famous collection by al-Hariri, written around 1100, each episode follows the same pattern: a narrator arrives in a new city, meets a clever wanderer named Abu Zayd, and watches him trick a crowd out of money with a dazzling speech. Each episode ends with Abu Zayd leaving town, and the next one begins somewhere else. Because no episode depends on events from an earlier one, a reader of al-Hariri's collection ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: would need to read the episodes in their original order to follow Abu Zayd's story.
would find that Abu Zayd's speeches grow longer as the collection goes on.
would discover that the narrator and Abu Zayd become close friends by the final episode.
could begin with almost any episode and still understand what happens in it.
problem.explanation: 지문은 어떤 에피소드도 이전 에피소드의 사건에 의존하지 않는다고 분명히 말하므로, 독자는 아무 에피소드부터 읽어도 이해할 수 있다는 D가 정답이다. A는 순서대로 읽어야 한다고 하여 '서로 독립적'이라는 단서와 정반대이다. B는 연설 길이의 변화를 말하지만 지문에는 그런 정보가 없다. C는 에피소드를 넘나드는 관계의 발전을 가정하는데, 이는 각 에피소드가 독립적이라는 진술과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage states that no episode depends on events from an earlier one, so a reader could start with almost any episode and still follow it, which is choice D. Choice A says the episodes must be read in order, which is the opposite of what the passage says about their independence. Choice B talks about speeches getting longer, but the passage gives no information about that. Choice C assumes a relationship that builds across episodes, which doesn't fit the claim that each episode stands on its own.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D는 "no episode depends on events from an earlier one"이라는 명시적 단서에서 한 단계 추론으로 도출된다. A는 단서와 정반대, B·C는 지문에 근거 없는 연속적 발전을 가정하는 전형적 오개념으로 그럴듯하되 배제 가능. al-Hariri 마카마트(약 1100년, 화자 al-Harith, 사기꾼 Abu Zayd al-Saruji) 사실 관계도 정확. 지문은 독창적 서술로 저작권 우려 없음. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하며 자연스럽다.

advisory.note: 단서 하나(에피소드 간 비의존)에서 한 단계만 추론하면 된다. 알하리리의 마카마(약 1100년, 아부 자이드) 관련 사실도 정확하다. 오답 B는 다소 약하지만 근거 없는 진술이라 배제하기 쉬운 전형적 유형이다.

problem.passage:
In Edo-period Japan, ukiyo-e prints such as Utagawa Hiroshige's landscape series were made through a division of labor. An artist drew the design, a carver cut it into blocks of cherry wood, and a printer pressed paper onto the inked blocks one color at a time. Because a single set of carved blocks could be inked and printed again and again, a publisher could produce thousands of copies of one design without asking the artist to redraw it. This method helps explain why Hiroshige's prints sold for roughly the price of a bowl of noodles: since the costly work of designing and carving was done only once for each image, ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: In Edo-period Japan, ukiyo-e prints such as Utagawa Hiroshige's landscape series were made through a division of labor. An artist drew the design, a carver cut it into blocks of cherry wood, and a printer pressed paper onto the inked blocks one color at a time. Because a single set of carved blocks could be inked and printed again and again, a publisher could produce thousands of copies of one design without asking the artist to redraw it. This method helps explain why Hiroshige's prints sold for roughly the price of a bowl of noodles: since the costly work of designing and carving was done only once for each image, ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the expense of making each additional copy remained low.
the expense of hiring skilled carvers rose with every copy printed.
the expense of the prints depended mainly on how famous the artist was.
the expense of cherry wood made each print costlier than a painting.
problem.explanation: 지문은 디자인과 조각처럼 비용이 큰 작업이 이미지마다 한 번만 이루어지고, 같은 목판으로 계속 인쇄할 수 있었다고 말한다. 따라서 추가로 찍는 한 장의 비용은 낮았고, 이것이 싼 가격을 설명하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 조각이 한 번만 이루어진다는 내용과 모순된다. C는 지문이 제시한 제작 방식과 무관한 설명이고, D는 판화가 싸게 팔렸다는 사실과 반대된다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says the costly design and carving work happened only once per image, and the same blocks could be printed again and again. So each extra copy cost little to make, which explains the low price. That makes A correct. B contradicts the point that carving happened only once. C brings in the artist's fame, which has nothing to do with the production method the passage describes. D contradicts the fact that the prints were cheap.

B contradicts one-time carving, C is unsupported (fame), D contradicts cheapness. Historical details (division of labor, cherry wood, cheap Hiroshige prints) are accurate. Korean and English explanations match in conclusion and letter references; English is natural and contains no Hangul. One explicit cue, one inference step, plausible distractors — fits easy.

advisory.note: 단서 'done only once'에서 한 단계로 추론할 수 있다. 오답들은 그럴듯한 오개념이며, 사실관계(벚나무 목판, 소바 한 그릇 가격)도 대체로 정확하다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Many historians credit the Phoenicians with the decisive step toward the alphabet. By reducing the hundreds of signs used in Egyptian and Mesopotamian scripts to roughly twenty-two consonant symbols, Phoenician scribes made writing far easier to learn. On this view, the alphabet's essential innovation was sheer simplification: fewer signs meant that literacy could spread beyond a narrow class of trained specialists.

Text 2
Some linguists argue that the number of signs in a script tells us little about what makes it alphabetic. Several syllabaries, such as the one later devised for Cherokee, use a modest inventory of symbols, yet each symbol still stands for a whole syllable. What distinguishes a true alphabet, these linguists contend, is the analytical principle of assigning separate symbols to individual consonants and vowels—a principle first applied systematically when Greek writers repurposed some Phoenician signs to represent vowels.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 about what made the Phoenician script innovative?

What distinguishes a true alphabet, these linguists contend, is the analytical principle of assigning separate symbols to individual consonants and vowels—a principle first applied systematically when Greek writers repurposed some Phoenician signs to represent vowels.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 about what made the Phoenician script innovative?
options: By agreeing that the Phoenicians' reduction of signs to about twenty-two was what allowed literacy to extend beyond trained specialists
By objecting that a small set of signs, by itself, does not make a script alphabetic, so Text 1 identifies the wrong feature as the alphabet's defining advance
By insisting that the true alphabet emerged only when Greek writers adapted Phoenician signs to stand for vowels
By questioning whether literacy actually spread more widely in Phoenician society than in Egypt or Mesopotamia
problem.explanation: 정답 B: Text 2는 체로키 음절문자처럼 기호 수가 적어도 알파벳이 아닐 수 있다는 전제를 제시한다. 따라서 '기호 축소'를 핵심 혁신으로 보는 Text 1에 대해, 기호 수는 알파벳의 정의적 특징이 아니라고 반박할 것이다. A: Text 1의 내용을 반복할 뿐 Text 2의 관점과 맞지 않는다. C: Text 2의 결론(그리스의 모음 표기)을 되풀이할 뿐, Text 1의 '단순화' 주장이 왜 틀렸는지에 대한 반응이 되지 못한다. D: 실제 문해율 확산 여부는 Text 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점이다.
problem.explanationEn: B is correct: Text 2 points out that syllabaries like Cherokee have small sign inventories yet aren't alphabets, so its author would reject Text 1's idea that reducing the number of signs was the alphabet's essential innovation. A just repeats Text 1's claim, which Text 2 undercuts. C restates Text 2's conclusion about Greek vowels but doesn't address the actual flaw in Text 1's reasoning, which is treating sign count as the defining feature. D brings in whether literacy really spread, an issue Text 2 never discusses.

hardJudge.note: Text 2는 Text 1을 직접 언급하지 않으며, 정답 B는 Text 2의 전제(기호 수는 알파벳 여부와 무관, 체로키 음절문자 사례)에서 Text 1의 '단순화=핵심 혁신' 주장에 대한 반응을 스스로 추론해야 도출된다. A는 Text 1 반복, D는 본문 밖 쟁점(실제 문해율 비교). C는 Text 2의 결론을 되풀이하면서 'only'로 강도를 확장한 선택지로, Text 1의 주장에 대한 직접 반응이 아니라는 점에서 B보다 열위이나 Text 2 내용과 상당히 부합해 다소 매력적인 오답임(정답 성립에는 문제 없음). 사실관계(페니키아 22자음, 체로키 음절문자, 그리스의 모음 도입) 정확. 해설은 정답과 오답 사유를 일관되게 뒷받침함.

advisory.note: B가 유일하게 옳다. 텍스트 2는 기호 수가 적다는 점이 알파벳의 정의적 특징이 아니라고 본다. C는 텍스트 2의 결론을 '오직'이라는 표현으로 과장했고 텍스트 1에 대한 반응으로도 빗나가 있어 강도를 판별하게 하는 함정으로 기능한다. hard 수준이지만 상위권 변별력은 중간 정도다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Byzantine scholia, the marginal notes that surround many medieval manuscripts of Homer and Sophocles, have long been prized as windows into lost ancient criticism. Some historians argue that the scholia's value as evidence lies chiefly in their consistency: because the same explanatory note often appears, nearly word for word, in manuscripts copied in different centuries and monasteries, the note must descend from a single authoritative ancient commentary. On this view, a note's wide distribution is itself evidence of its antiquity, and scholars can reconstruct Hellenistic scholarship simply by collecting the scholia that recur most often.

Text 2
A recent study of twelfth-century manuscripts from Constantinople complicates this picture. Examining ownership marks and handwriting, researchers found that a small circle of teachers lent their annotated copies widely, and students routinely transcribed those teachers' own marginal remarks into new books. Several notes that appear in dozens of later manuscripts can be traced to one twelfth-century schoolmaster, not to any ancient source. The study's authors do not dispute that some scholia preserve genuine Hellenistic material, but they caution that classroom copying could spread a medieval comment just as efficiently as an ancient one.

Based on the texts, which element of the reasoning described in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely challenge?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Byzantine scholia, the marginal notes that surround many medieval manuscripts of Homer and Sophocles, have long been prized as windows into lost ancient criticism. Some historians argue that the scholia's value as evidence lies chiefly in their consistency: because the same explanatory note often appears, nearly word for word, in manuscripts copied in different centuries and monasteries, the note must descend from a single authoritative ancient commentary. On this view, a note's wide distribution is itself evidence of its antiquity, and scholars can reconstruct Hellenistic scholarship simply by collecting the scholia that recur most often.

Text 2
A recent study of twelfth-century manuscripts from Constantinople complicates this picture. Examining ownership marks and handwriting, researchers found that a small circle of teachers lent their annotated copies widely, and students routinely transcribed those teachers' own marginal remarks into new books. Several notes that appear in dozens of later manuscripts can be traced to one twelfth-century schoolmaster, not to any ancient source. The study's authors do not dispute that some scholia preserve genuine Hellenistic material, but they caution that classroom copying could spread a medieval comment just as efficiently as an ancient one.
problem.question: Based on the texts, which element of the reasoning described in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely challenge?
options: The conclusion that Byzantine scholia are worth studying as sources for ancient literary criticism
The observation that the scholia accompany medieval manuscripts of authors such as Homer and Sophocles
The premise that a note recurring across many manuscripts must have originated in a single ancient commentary
The claim that at least some scholia transmit material that originated in Hellenistic scholarship
problem.explanation: 정답 C: Text 1의 결론(가장 자주 반복되는 주석으로 헬레니즘 학문을 재구성할 수 있다)은 '널리 퍼진 주석은 고대 단일 출처에서 왔다'는 가정에 기댄다. Text 2는 12세기 교사의 주석이 수업 필사를 통해 수십 개 사본에 퍼졌음을 보여 주어, 널리 퍼졌다는 사실이 고대성을 보장하지 않는다고 지적한다. 즉 결론이 아닌 그 가정을 공격한다. A: 결론 자체에 해당하는 넓은 주장이다. Text 2는 스콜리아의 가치를 부정하지 않으므로 이의를 제기하지 않는다. B: 지문의 부수적 세부일 뿐 논증의 핵심이 아니며, Text 2는 이에 대해 아무 말도 하지 않는다. D: Text 2의 저자들은 일부 스콜리아가 진짜 헬레니즘 자료를 보존한다는 점을 오히려 명시적으로 인정한다.
problem.explanationEn: C is correct. Text 1's method (rebuilding Hellenistic scholarship from the notes that show up most often) depends on one assumption: if a note is widely shared, it must come from one ancient source. Text 2 shows that a twelfth-century schoolmaster's remarks spread to dozens of manuscripts through classroom copying. So a note being widespread doesn't prove it's ancient, and that undercuts the assumption, not the conclusion. A is wrong because it's the broad conclusion. Text 2 never says scholia are worthless as sources. B is wrong because it's a side detail that Text 2 doesn't address at all. D is wrong because Text 2's authors openly agree that some scholia preserve genuine Hellenistic material.

hardJudge.note: Text 1은 결론(반복 빈도로 헬레니즘 학문 재구성 가능)과 근거(광범위한 분포=단일 고대 출처)를 명확히 구분하고, Text 2는 12세기 교사 주석의 교실 전파 사례로 그 근거만을 흔들며 일부 스콜리아의 고대성(D)은 명시적으로 인정한다. 정답 C는 가정에 해당하고, A는 결론을 과도하게 일반화한 선택지, D는 Text 2가 동의하는 부분으로 함정 구조가 적절하다. 해설의 논리도 지문과 정확히 일치한다. 다만 Text 2의 "do not dispute… but caution" 문장이 정답 방향을 비교적 직접적으로 시사해 hard 중에서는 난도가 낮은 편이다.

advisory.note: Text 2가 '널리 퍼진 것 ≠ 고대 기원'이라고 사실상 직접 말하고 있다. 그래서 어떻게 반응할지 따로 추론할 부담이 낮고, 전형적인 medium 문항 수준이다. D 오답으로 입장 강도를 가리는 장치는 있지만 명시적 양보 문장과 바로 맞아서 쉽게 걸러진다. B는 너무 명백하게 틀린 선택지다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Scholars often read Kasuga shrine mandalas, the medieval Japanese paintings that show the Kasuga Shrine compound beneath the slopes of Mount Kasuga, as straightforward topographic records. Art historian Mai Tanabe argues that any account of such images must be checked against how they were actually handled. In her view, an interpretation counts as persuasive only if it is backed by evidence of use, such as temple inventories, ritual manuals, or wear on the scrolls themselves, and not by visual resemblance alone.

Text 2
In many Kasuga mandalas, the deer, the shrine buildings, and the forested mountain are placed in a pattern that closely matches the arrangement of Buddhist deities in mandalas of the Esoteric Buddhist tradition. Given how strong this parallel is, one scholar concludes that the paintings were designed to make viewers see the landscape itself as a sacred body of buddhas. On this reading, they were made as objects of devotion, not as maps.

Based on the texts, how would Tanabe (Text 1) most likely evaluate the conclusion reached by the scholar in Text 2?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Scholars often read Kasuga shrine mandalas, the medieval Japanese paintings that show the Kasuga Shrine compound beneath the slopes of Mount Kasuga, as straightforward topographic records. Art historian Mai Tanabe argues that any account of such images must be checked against how they were actually handled. In her view, an interpretation counts as persuasive only if it is backed by evidence of use, such as temple inventories, ritual manuals, or wear on the scrolls themselves, and not by visual resemblance alone.

Text 2
In many Kasuga mandalas, the deer, the shrine buildings, and the forested mountain are placed in a pattern that closely matches the arrangement of Buddhist deities in mandalas of the Esoteric Buddhist tradition. Given how strong this parallel is, one scholar concludes that the paintings were designed to make viewers see the landscape itself as a sacred body of buddhas. On this reading, they were made as objects of devotion, not as maps.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would Tanabe (Text 1) most likely evaluate the conclusion reached by the scholar in Text 2?
options: She would find it convincing, since the close match between the painted landscape and the arrangement of Esoteric Buddhist deities is precisely the kind of pattern that shows what the paintings were meant to do.

She would find it partly convincing, since the visual parallel shows the paintings' devotional function, though their topographic accuracy would still need to be checked against the actual shrine site.
She would find it unconvincing, since medieval painters were generally trying to show real places accurately, which makes a devotional reading of these landscape scenes unlikely.
She would find it insufficiently supported, since the scholar infers what the paintings were for from their composition without pointing to any record of how they were kept or used.
problem.explanation:
정답 D: Tanabe의 기준은 해석이 시각적 유사성만이 아니라 사용의 증거(사찰 목록, 의례 지침서, 두루마리의 마모)로 뒷받침되어야 한다는 것이다. Text 2의 학자는 구도의 유사성만으로 신앙 대상이라는 결론을 내리므로, Tanabe는 결론이 틀렸다고 단정하기보다 근거가 부족하다고 평가할 것이다.
A: Text 2 저자의 기준(시각적 패턴의 강한 일치)으로 평가한 것이다. Tanabe는 바로 이런 근거만으로는 부족하다고 본다.
B: 두 기준을 섞었다. 시각적 유사성으로 기능을 인정하면서 현장과의 지형 대조를 덧붙이는데, 지형 대조는 Tanabe가 요구하는 사용 증거가 아니다.
C: 일반 상식(중세 화가는 사실적 재현을 추구했다)에 기댄 평가로, 지문 어디에도 근거가 없다. Tanabe는 오히려 지형 기록으로 읽는 해석에도 비판적이다.
problem.explanationEn:
D is correct. Tanabe's standard is that an interpretation is persuasive only when it rests on evidence of use, such as inventories, ritual manuals, or wear on the scrolls, and not on visual resemblance alone. The scholar in Text 2 draws a conclusion about the paintings' devotional purpose purely from how they are composed. So Tanabe wouldn't necessarily say the conclusion is false. She would say it lacks the kind of support she requires.
A judges the conclusion by Text 2's own standard, the strength of the visual parallel. That is exactly the kind of evidence Tanabe considers insufficient.
B mixes the two standards. It accepts the visual parallel as proof of function and then adds a check of the topography against the site. Comparing the painting to the site is still not evidence of how the paintings were used.

hardJudge.note: Text 1의 기준(사용 증거 필요, 시각적 유사성만으로 불충분)이 명시되어 있고, Text 2 학자는 구도 유사성만으로 신앙 대상이라는 결론을 내리므로 D가 유일하게 Tanabe 관점에서 도출된다. D는 '틀렸다'가 아니라 '근거 부족'으로 강도가 조정되어 있어 claim strength 판별도 요구한다. A는 Text 2 저자 기준, B는 두 관점 혼합(지형 대조는 사용 증거가 아님), C는 지문 외 일반화. 해설의 'Tanabe는 지형 기록 해석에도 비판적'은 약간 강한 표현이나 Text 1 맥락상 수용 가능. 가상의 학자·원창작 지문으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: D는 Tanabe의 기준(사용 증거 필요, 시각적 유사성만으로는 불충분)을 바탕으로 '틀렸다'가 아니라 '근거 부족'이라는 알맞은 강도로 판정한다. A는 Text 2의 기준을 쓴 오답이고, B는 두 관점을 섞은 오답이며, C는 강도를 넘어선 데다 본문에 근거가 없다. 다만 Text 1에 기준이 명시되어 있어 추론 깊이는 보통 수준이다. 그래도 강도 구분(D와 C의 차이)이 hard 요소로 작동한다.

Many scholars describe tsukumogami, the household objects in Japanese folklore said to come alive after about a hundred years, as a product of ancient animism. On this view, the stories simply reflect a very old belief that spirits live in all things, including tools and utensils.

problem.passage:
Many Nahua codices produced before and shortly after the Spanish conquest record events through pictographic images rather than through alphabetic text. Scholars once assumed that these images were simply illustrations meant to accompany spoken accounts, so that a codex alone could not convey a specific narrative. However, historian Elizabeth Boone has shown that the codices follow consistent visual conventions: footprints mark the direction of travel, a speech scroll marks who is speaking, and place-name glyphs pair images with sounds that identify particular towns. Moreover, readers trained in these conventions in different regions arrived at closely matching readings of the same manuscripts. Taken together, these findings suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

Moreover, readers trained in these conventions in different regions arrived at closely matching readings of the same manuscripts. Taken together, these findings suggest that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the codices were mainly decorative objects whose images varied freely from one painter to the next.
the codices were understood only by readers who already knew the spoken accounts that went with them.
the codices were read the same way across regions mostly because Spanish officials required a standard style after the conquest.
the codices were able to communicate particular narratives through a shared visual system, not just through accompanying speech.
problem.explanation: 지문은 코덱스가 일관된 시각적 관습(발자국, 말풍선, 지명 글리프)을 따른다는 점과, 서로 다른 지역의 독자들이 같은 해석에 도달했다는 점을 제시한다. 두 근거를 합치면 코덱스는 구술 없이도 공유된 체계를 통해 특정 서사를 전달할 수 있었다는 D가 결론이 된다. A는 '일관된 관습'과 모순된다. B는 지문이 반박하는 기존 학자들의 가정을 그대로 반복한다. C는 지역 간 해석이 일치한 이유를 설명하는 것처럼 보이지만, 스페인의 강제는 지문에 근거가 없고 정복 이전 코덱스도 다룬다는 점과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text gives you two pieces of evidence: the codices follow consistent visual conventions (footprints, speech scrolls, place-name glyphs), and trained readers in different regions reached matching readings. When you put these together, they show the codices could convey specific narratives through a shared system without relying only on speech, which is choice D. Choice A contradicts the point about consistent conventions. Choice B just repeats the older assumption that the text is arguing against. Choice C might seem to explain why readings matched across regions, but the text never mentions Spanish requirements, and it also discusses codices made before the conquest.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Classical Latin poets prized zeugma, in which a single verb governs two objects in different senses, as in a line where a figure "lost her sandal and her composure." Many commentators argue that the device was chiefly ornamental: poets used it to display wit, and its function was to amuse a learned audience rather than to carry meaning that plainer phrasing could not.

Text 2
Latin verse was bound by strict metrical patterns, so every syllable had to earn its place. Zeugma let a poet make one verb do the work of two, joining a concrete and an abstract sense in a single slot. When Ovid has a character carry "arms and grief," the reader must hold both senses at once, and the pairing implies that the physical burden and the emotional one are inseparable—a claim that two separate verbs would weaken.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the commentators' view described in Text 1?

problem.passage:
Text 1
Anglo-Saxon law codes such as those of King Æthelberht list precise payments, or wergeld, owed for killing or injuring a person, with sums scaled to the victim's social rank. Some historians read these tariffs as evidence that early English communities had largely replaced blood feud with orderly monetary settlement. On this view, the codes describe how disputes were actually resolved: a killing triggered a fixed payment, and the matter closed.

Text 2
Old English poetry complicates that picture. In Beowulf, the poet repeatedly shows wergeld being offered and accepted, yet the settlements rarely hold; the Finnsburg episode and the tale of Ingeld both depict compensation agreements collapsing into renewed violence once old grievances are stirred. Such scenes suggest that audiences understood payment as a fragile truce rather than a final resolution, and that the tidy tariffs of the codes record an ideal more than a routine practice.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the historians' view described in Text 1?

Researchers studying business negotiations have found that negotiators from many cultures soften such requests with indirect phrasing, such as "Would it be possible to revisit the price?" ______ negotiators in some settings, including certain Dutch and Israeli business contexts, often prefer direct statements and may view heavy softening as unclear or evasive.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: According to politeness theory, developed by linguists Penelope Brown and Stephen Levinson, a request can threaten a listener's "face," or public self-image, because it limits the listener's freedom to act. Researchers studying business negotiations have found that negotiators from many cultures soften such requests with indirect phrasing, such as "Would it be possible to revisit the price?" ______ negotiators in some settings, including certain Dutch and Israeli business contexts, often prefer direct statements and may view heavy softening as unclear or evasive.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 여러 문화의 협상가들이 요청을 간접적인 표현으로 완화한다고 말하고, 뒤 문장은 일부 환경의 협상가들이 직접적인 진술을 선호한다고 말한다. 두 문장은 서로 반대되는 행동을 제시하므로 대조를 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 사례가 아니라 반대 경우이므로 틀리다. C는 간접 표현 사용이 직접 표현 선호의 원인이 아니므로 틀리다. D는 두 행동이 비슷하지 않고 반대이므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The first sentence says negotiators in many cultures soften requests with indirect phrasing, and the next sentence says negotiators in some settings prefer direct statements. Since these two behaviors are opposites, you need a transition that shows contrast, so A is correct. B is wrong because the second sentence isn't an example of indirect phrasing; it describes the opposite approach. C is wrong because using indirect phrasing doesn't cause other negotiators to prefer directness. D is wrong because the two behaviors aren't similar; they're opposite.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In the 1960s, British sociologist Basil Bernstein studied how schoolchildren from different social classes used language. He found that working-class children often relied on a "restricted code," speech that assumes listeners already share the speaker's background and so leaves much unsaid. ______ middle-class children more often used an "elaborated code," spelling out meanings in full so that even a stranger could follow them.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 노동계층 아이들이 많은 것을 생략하는 '제한 코드'를 쓴다고 하고, 뒤 문장은 중산층 아이들이 의미를 모두 풀어 말하는 '정교 코드'를 쓴다고 한다. 서로 다른 두 집단의 반대되는 언어 습관을 나란히 놓으므로 대조를 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 사례일 때 쓰지만, 중산층 아이들은 노동계층 아이들의 예가 아니다. C는 인과 관계를 나타내지만, 한 집단의 말투가 다른 집단의 말투를 일으키지 않는다. D는 같은 방향의 정보를 더할 때 쓰므로 반대되는 내용에는 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The first sentence says working-class children used a "restricted code" that leaves much unsaid. The next sentence says middle-class children used an "elaborated code" that spells meanings out in full. These two groups have opposite speech habits, so the transition has to show contrast, and that makes B correct. A doesn't work because the middle-class children are not an example of the working-class children's speech. C doesn't work because one group's way of talking did not cause the other group's. D is for adding similar information, so it can't link two opposite ideas.

problem.passage:
In her 1983 book The Managed Heart, sociologist Arlie Hochschild studied flight attendants and introduced the term "emotional labor." She found that airlines trained attendants to stay cheerful and calm with every passenger, even rude ones, and to keep smiling for hours at a time. ______ many attendants told Hochschild that they began to feel cut off from their own real emotions, both at work and at home.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In her 1983 book The Managed Heart, sociologist Arlie Hochschild studied flight attendants and introduced the term "emotional labor." She found that airlines trained attendants to stay cheerful and calm with every passenger, even rude ones, and to keep smiling for hours at a time. ______ many attendants told Hochschild that they began to feel cut off from their own real emotions, both at work and at home.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 승무원들이 몇 시간씩 억지로 밝은 감정을 유지하도록 훈련받았다는 원인을 제시하고, 뒤 문장은 그 때문에 자신의 진짜 감정과 단절된 느낌을 받았다는 결과를 말한다. 따라서 결과를 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 앞 내용의 구체적 사례를 들 때 쓰는데, 뒤 문장은 훈련의 사례가 아니라 그 영향이다. B는 대조를 나타내지만 두 문장은 서로 반대되지 않는다. D는 비슷한 내용을 하나 더 덧붙일 때 쓰지만, 뒤 문장은 비슷한 사실이 아니라 결과이다.
problem.explanationEn: The first sentences describe a cause: attendants were trained to stay cheerful for hours, even with rude passengers. The last sentence describes what happened because of this training: the attendants felt cut off from their real emotions. Since that is a cause-and-effect relationship, C is correct. A introduces a specific instance, but the last sentence is an effect of the training, not an example of it. B signals contrast, and the two ideas don't oppose each other. D adds a parallel point, but the last sentence is a consequence, not a similar fact.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(장시간 억지 미소 훈련)이 원인, 뒤 문장(진짜 감정과의 단절)이 결과로 명확한 인과 구조이므로 'As a result'(C)가 유일하게 논리적임. A(예시)·B(대조)·D(유사 추가)는 전형적 오개념 오답으로 적절. Hochschild 1983 The Managed Heart·emotional labor·승무원 연구는 사실과 부합. 빈칸 뒤 소문자 'many'는 전환어+쉼표 구조와 일치. 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움. 한 단계 추론·평이한 어휘로 easy 적합.

advisory.note: 원인(장시간 감정 유지 훈련)→결과(감정 단절)의 관계가 지문에 바로 드러나 한 단계 추론으로 풀 수 있다. Hochschild(1983), 승무원 연구, '감정 노동'이라는 용어, 자기 감정과 멀어지는 현상은 모두 사실과 맞는다. 오답 세 개(예시·대조·유사)는 전형적인 오개념이다.

problem.passage:
In the 1980s, psychologist Sherry Turkle interviewed children who played with early electronic toys and computers. She found that the children did not treat these machines as simple objects like blocks or balls. Instead, many children ______ the devices with feelings and intentions, saying that a game "wanted" to win or that a toy could be "sad" when it was switched off.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In the 1980s, psychologist Sherry Turkle interviewed children who played with early electronic toys and computers. She found that the children did not treat these machines as simple objects like blocks or balls. Instead, many children ______ the devices with feelings and intentions, saying that a game "wanted" to win or that a toy could be "sad" when it was switched off.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 아이들이 기기가 무언가를 "원한다"거나 "슬플" 수 있다고 말했다고 하므로, 아이들이 기기에 감정과 의도가 있다고 여겼다는 뜻의 단어가 필요하다. D의 credited는 "credit A with B" 구조로 'A에 B가 있다고 여기다'라는 뜻이어서 정답이다. A의 repaired(수리했다)는 감정을 부여하는 것과 관련이 없다. B의 compared는 비교를 뜻할 뿐, 기기에 감정이 있다고 믿었다는 뜻을 전달하지 못한다. C의 replaced(교체했다)는 지문 내용과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the children claimed a game "wanted" to win or a toy could be "sad," so the blank needs a word meaning the children thought the devices had feelings and intentions. Choice D, "credited," fits the pattern "credit A with B," which means to believe that A has B, so D is the best answer. Choice A, "repaired," means fixed and has nothing to do with giving the devices feelings. Choice B, "compared," only means looking at similarities and doesn't say the children believed the devices had feelings. Choice C, "replaced," doesn't match what the passage describes.

hardJudge.note: 정답 검증: 뒤따르는 "wanted"/"sad" 인용이 기기에 감정·의도를 부여했다는 단서를 직접 제공하므로 "credited ... with"가 유일하게 논리적·관용적으로 맞음. 셰리 터클의 1980년대 아동·컴퓨터 연구(The Second Self, 1984) 내용과 부합하며 지문은 원작 인용이 아닌 재서술이라 저작권 문제 없음. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 지지하고 선택지 글자 참조가 정확하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 난이도: 단서가 지문에 명시적이고 한 단계 추론으로 풀리므로 easy 적합. 다만 A(repaired)·C(replaced)는 "with feelings"와 결합 시 의미가 다소 비현실적이어서 오답 매력도가 약한 편이며, B(compared ... with)만이 구조적으로 그럴듯한 함정 역할을 함. 치명적 결함은 아님.

advisory.note: "credit A with B" 구조와 'wanted', 'sad'라는 단서가 지문에 바로 드러나 있어 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. 오답 중 compared는 'compare A with B'라는 같은 구조를 이용한 그럴듯한 함정이다. repaired와 replaced는 다소 약하지만 easy 수준에서는 허용 범위다. Turkle의 1980년대 연구 내용(The Second Self)과도 맞는다.

problem.passage:
In his 1975 book Discipline and Punish, philosopher Michel Foucault examined the panopticon, a prison design in which a central tower allows a guard to watch every cell. Because prisoners cannot see into the tower, they never know whether they are being watched at a given moment. Foucault argued that this uncertainty leads prisoners to ______ their own behavior: acting as though a guard is always present, they follow the rules even when no one is actually looking.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In his 1975 book Discipline and Punish, philosopher Michel Foucault examined the panopticon, a prison design in which a central tower allows a guard to watch every cell. Because prisoners cannot see into the tower, they never know whether they are being watched at a given moment. Foucault argued that this uncertainty leads prisoners to ______ their own behavior: acting as though a guard is always present, they follow the rules even when no one is actually looking.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 뒤 콜론 다음 내용이 단서이다. 수감자들은 감시자가 늘 있는 것처럼 행동하며 아무도 보지 않을 때도 규칙을 지킨다고 했으므로, 스스로 행동을 '통제한다'는 뜻의 A가 정답이다. B(버리다)는 행동을 그만둔다는 뜻이라 규칙을 지킨다는 내용과 맞지 않는다. C(과장하다)는 행동을 부풀린다는 뜻이라 규칙 준수라는 단서와 관련이 없다. D(잊다)는 자기 행동에 신경 쓰지 않는다는 뜻이 되어, 늘 감시를 의식한다는 설명과 반대된다.
problem.explanationEn: The clue comes after the colon: the prisoners act as though a guard is always present and follow the rules even when no one is watching. That means they control their own behavior, so A is correct. B means to give up the behavior entirely, which doesn't fit with prisoners carefully following rules. C means to make the behavior bigger or more extreme, and nothing in the text suggests that. D would mean the prisoners stop paying attention to how they act, which is the opposite of always being aware they might be watched.

hardJudge.note: 콜론 뒤 "acting as though a guard is always present ... follow the rules even when no one is looking"이 '스스로 통제한다(regulate)'를 직접 뒷받침하므로 A가 유일한 정답. B(abandon)·C(exaggerate)·D(forget)는 단서와 상충하거나 무관하여 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제되지만 어휘만 보면 그럴듯한 전형적 오답임. 사실관계(Foucault, Discipline and Punish 1975, 파놉티콘 구조) 정확. 한·영 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 지문은 원창작으로 저작권 의심 없음. 단일 단서·한 단계 추론으로 easy 적합.

advisory.note: Discipline and Punish(Surveiller et punir) 1975년 출간, 판옵티콘 설명 모두 사실과 맞음. 콜론 뒤에 단서가 직접 나오고 한 단계 추론으로 풀 수 있어 easy에 적합함.

problem.stimulus: Linguist Deborah Tannen's research on mixed-gender conversation suggests that what listeners call an interruption is often a matter of conversational style. In her turn-taking analyses, a speaker's overlapping comments ______ frequently meant as signs of enthusiastic support rather than as attempts to take control of the discussion.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 동사의 주어는 단수 소유격 "a speaker's"가 아니라 복수 명사 "comments"이다. 따라서 복수 동사가 필요하고, 지문 전체가 현재 시제(suggests, is)이므로 B "are"가 정답이다. A "is"는 단수 동사로, 바로 앞의 "speaker's"에 맞춘 오류이다. C "has been"과 D "was"도 모두 단수형이라 복수 주어 "comments"와 수가 일치하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of the verb in the blank is the plural noun "comments." It is not the singular possessive "a speaker's," which only describes the comments. A plural subject needs a plural verb, and the text uses the present tense ("suggests," "is"), so B, "are," is correct. A, "is," is singular, so it wrongly agrees with "speaker's." C, "has been," and D, "was," are also singular forms, so neither one agrees with the plural subject "comments."

hardJudge.note: 주어 "comments"(복수)에 맞는 복수 동사는 B "are"뿐이며, A·C·D는 모두 단수형으로 배제된다. 검산 결과 정답 타당. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 모순 없음. 지문은 자체 작성 문장으로 저작권 우려 없고, Tannen의 '협력적 겹침' 연구 내용과도 부합. 수일치 규칙 하나로 풀리고 단서가 빈칸 바로 앞에 드러나므로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 주어-동사 수일치 한 가지 규칙만 묻는다. 단수 소유격이 주어를 헷갈리게 만드는 함정은 easy 수준에 맞다. 오답 세 개가 모두 단수형이라 수일치 규칙만 알면 바로 걸러진다.

problem.passage:
Sociologist Erving Goffman argued that people work together to protect one another's "face," or public self-image, during conversation. According to Goffman, when someone commits an embarrassing slip, such as calling a coworker by the wrong name, the other people present often help repair the moment, for example by laughing it off or quickly changing the subject. A student researcher hypothesizes that, consistent with Goffman's view, listeners are more likely to offer this kind of help when the speaker shows visible embarrassment than when the speaker shows none.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the student researcher's hypothesis?
problem.stimulus: Sociologist Erving Goffman argued that people work together to protect one another's "face," or public self-image, during conversation. According to Goffman, when someone commits an embarrassing slip, such as calling a coworker by the wrong name, the other people present often help repair the moment, for example by laughing it off or quickly changing the subject. A student researcher hypothesizes that, consistent with Goffman's view, listeners are more likely to offer this kind of help when the speaker shows visible embarrassment than when the speaker shows none.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the student researcher's hypothesis?
options: In recorded conversations, listeners made a joke or shifted the topic after 70 percent of slips by blushing or stammering speakers but after only 25 percent of slips by speakers who appeared calm.
In recorded conversations, speakers who appeared calm after a slip made just as many slips overall as speakers who blushed or stammered.
In recorded conversations, listeners made a joke or shifted the topic about equally often after slips, whether or not the speaker blushed or stammered.
In recorded conversations, speakers who blushed or stammered after a slip were more likely to apologize than speakers who appeared calm.
problem.explanation: 가설은 화자가 당황한 모습을 보일 때 청자가 상황 수습을 더 자주 돕는다는 것이다. A는 당황한 화자 쪽에서 청자의 도움(농담, 화제 전환) 비율이 훨씬 높다고 보여 주므로 가설을 직접 뒷받침한다. B는 실수 횟수에 관한 것이고 청자의 반응은 다루지 않는다. C는 차이가 없다고 하므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다. D는 청자가 아니라 화자 자신의 행동(사과)에 관한 것이다.
problem.explanationEn: The hypothesis says listeners help repair a slip more often when the speaker looks embarrassed. A shows listeners joking or changing the subject much more often after slips by embarrassed speakers, so it directly supports the hypothesis. B is about how many slips speakers make, not how listeners respond. C finds no difference, so it would actually weaken the hypothesis. D describes what the speakers did (apologizing), not what the listeners did.

quality.seed: social science research — Erving Goffman face-work and repair strategies managing social interaction breakdowns and embarrassment

hardJudge.note: 가설(화자의 가시적 당황 → 청자의 수습 행동 증가)에 대해 A만이 청자 행동을 두 조건에서 비교하여 차이를 보여 준다. B는 실수 빈도, C는 차이 없음(약화), D는 화자 자신의 사과 행동으로 모두 전형적 오개념형 오답. Goffman의 face-work 서술은 사실에 부합하며 지문은 자체 작성으로 보임. 한·영 해설 결론과 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움. 한 단계 대응으로 풀리는 easy 수준에 적합.

advisory.note: 비교 조건(당황 vs 침착)과 청자 반응을 직접 대응시키는 단일 단계 추론. 오답은 측정 대상이 다른 변수(B·D)를 다루거나 반대 결과(C)를 제시하는 전형적 오개념이어서 easy 난이도에 맞음.

problem.passage:
Linguist Deborah Cameron has argued that differences between "men's talk" and "women's talk" are not fixed traits that speakers carry from birth or early childhood. Instead, she claims, speakers adjust their speech to fit what a situation seems to demand. On her view, a person's way of talking about feelings, for example, depends more on the setting and the role the speaker is playing than on whether the speaker is a man or a woman.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Cameron's claim?
problem.stimulus: Linguist Deborah Cameron has argued that differences between "men's talk" and "women's talk" are not fixed traits that speakers carry from birth or early childhood. Instead, she claims, speakers adjust their speech to fit what a situation seems to demand. On her view, a person's way of talking about feelings, for example, depends more on the setting and the role the speaker is playing than on whether the speaker is a man or a woman.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Cameron's claim?
options: Men in a large survey reported that they talk about their feelings less often than women do, and their answers stayed the same across ten years.
Male nurses comforting patients used as much emotional language as female nurses did, but the same men used far less such language when chatting with friends at a sports bar.
Women in a large survey reported that they talk about their feelings more often than men do, and their answers stayed the same across ten years.
Girls as young as four used more emotional language than boys of the same age in every setting the researchers observed.
problem.explanation: Cameron의 주장은 말하는 방식이 성별보다 상황과 역할에 따라 달라진다는 것이다. B는 같은 남성이 간호 역할에서는 여성 간호사만큼 감정 표현을 쓰고, 친구와의 자리에서는 덜 쓴다는 결과이므로 상황에 따른 변화를 직접 보여 준다. A와 C는 성별 간 차이가 시간이 지나도 고정되어 있다는 결과라서 오히려 성별이 결정한다는 견해에 가깝다. D는 어린 나이부터 모든 상황에서 성별 차이가 나타난다는 결과이므로 Cameron의 주장을 약화한다.
problem.explanationEn: Cameron claims that speech style depends on the setting and the speaker's role more than on gender. B supports this directly: the same men match female nurses in emotional language while comforting patients but use much less at a sports bar, so their speech shifts with the situation. A and C describe gender differences that stay fixed over time, which fits the view Cameron rejects. D shows a gender difference appearing early and in every setting, which would weaken her claim.

quality.seed: social science research — Deborah Cameron language and gender performativity and sociolinguistic construction of masculine versus feminine speech

hardJudge.note: B는 동일 화자가 역할·상황에 따라 감정 언어 사용량을 바꾸는 결과로 Cameron의 주장을 직접 뒷받침함. A/C는 시간적으로 고정된 성차, D는 어린 나이·모든 상황의 성차로 오답 배제가 명확함. 한국어·영어 해설 결론과 선택지 참조 일치. 사소한 점: A와 C가 성별만 바꾼 거울 선택지라 변별력이 다소 떨어지나 easy 난이도에서는 허용 범위.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 같은 화자가 상황에 따라 말투를 바꾼다는 점을 직접 보여 주므로 정답이 맞다. 다만 A와 C는 같은 결과(여성이 남성보다 감정 이야기를 더 자주 한다고 응답, 10년간 변화 없음)를 남성 쪽과 여성 쪽에서 각각 서술한 것에 불과해 내용상 동일한 선택지다. 이 때문에 사실상 오답 선택지가 2개뿐이고, '둘 다 맞을 수는 없다'는 소거법으로도 풀 수 있다. 정답이 하나로 정해지는 데는 문제가 없지만 선택지 설계 품질은 떨어진다.

problem.question: The student wants to give an example of an everyday English expression that reflects a metaphor described by Lakoff and Johnson. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

C does this: it quotes the phrase "He defended his position" and links it to the metaphor "argument is war." A only tells you when the book came out and who wrote it, so it gives no example. B sums up the book's main claim but never names a specific expression. D gets the notes wrong, because they say metaphor is NOT just decoration.

hardJudge.note: 목표(일상 표현 예시 제시)에 C만 구체적 표현("He defended his position")과 은유("argument is war")를 연결함. A는 서지 정보, B는 주장 요약, D는 메모와 모순. 정답·해설 모두 정확하며 한 단계 추론으로 풀리는 easy 수준에 적합. 메모 사실관계(1980년 출간, Lakoff·Johnson, argument is war)도 정확함.

advisory.note: C만 구체적 표현과 은유를 연결함. D는 메모와 모순되어 다소 쉽게 배제되지만 easy 수준에 적합.

Lave's theory was developed with Etienne Wenger, who worked with her after her early studies of tailors.
Lave's theory holds that apprentices should first learn to cut cloth before they are allowed to sew buttons.
