problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to explain the main idea of the theory Lave helped develop. D does this by using the last note to state the theory's central claim: people learn best by taking part in a community's real practices. A only tells where the theory came from, not what it says. B only names a co-developer. C reverses the order in the notes (buttons came before cutting cloth), so it is inaccurate.

hardJudge.note: D는 마지막 메모(실제 공동체 활동 참여를 통한 학습이 가장 효과적, 분리된 기술 학습과 대비)를 정확히 재진술하여 '이론의 핵심 내용 설명'이라는 목표를 충족한다. Jean Lave·Etienne Wenger·라이베리아 재단사 연구 등 사실관계도 실제와 부합한다.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 마지막 메모를 그대로 풀어 쓴 문장이고, 오답 A·B는 배경 정보만 담았으며 C는 메모의 순서를 왜곡했다. 단서가 직접 드러나 있어 easy 난이도에 맞다. 다만 B의 'after her early studies of tailors'에서 시간 순서는 메모의 'later'로 뒷받침되므로 문제없다.

In nineteenth-century Lucknow, reciting Urdu qasida poetry was more than a literary pastime. Linguistic anthropologists describe this as a register, a style of speech that listeners link to a particular social identity. Performing the qasida well did not simply reflect a speaker's elite ______ it helped create and maintain that status in the eyes of others.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In nineteenth-century Lucknow, reciting Urdu qasida poetry was more than a literary pastime. Courtiers who mastered its ornate Persian-derived vocabulary used the form to signal refinement and to mark themselves off from lower-ranking groups. Linguistic anthropologists describe this as a register, a style of speech that listeners link to a particular social identity. Performing the qasida well did not simply reflect a speaker's elite ______ it helped create and maintain that status in the eyes of others.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Performing the qasida well did not simply reflect a speaker's elite status"와 뒤 "it helped create and maintain that status..."는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문장부호가 전혀 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 등위접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 붙어 표준 구두점에 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank, "Performing the qasida well did not simply reflect a speaker's elite status," form an independent clause, and so do the words after it, "it helped create and maintain that status..." A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence. D adds an extra comma after the conjunction "and," and Standard English doesn't put a comma there.

problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 "these phrases seem harmless on the surface"와 빈칸 뒤의 "they quietly link..."는 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 쉼표와 등위접속사로 이어야 하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 문장부호도 접속사도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. C는 접속사 "but" 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 주어 "they"와 접속사 사이를 끊는다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank ("these phrases seem harmless on the surface") and the words after it ("they quietly link...") are both independent clauses. B uses no punctuation and no conjunction, so it's a run-on sentence. C adds an unneeded comma after "but," which separates the conjunction from the subject "they."

problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Most participants picked ... at first glance"는 긴 동격구가 붙어 있지만 독립절이고, 뒤의 "words with K ... are actually about twice as common..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 이어야 하며, 전환어 "in fact" 뒤에는 쉼표를 붙이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 "in fact"를 쉼표로 감싸 삽입어처럼 보이지만 결국 쉼표만으로 두 절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C도 쉼표로만 절을 이어 같은 오류가 있고, "in fact" 뒤 쉼표까지 빠졌다. D는 두 절 사이에 아무 문장부호도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank, "Most participants picked ... at first glance," is an independent clause, even with the long appositive phrase attached to it. The part after it, "words with K ... are actually about twice as common...," is also an independent clause. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, and a transition like "in fact" takes a comma after it, so A is correct. B puts commas around "in fact" so it looks like an interrupter, but that still leaves only a comma joining the two clauses, which is a comma splice. C has the same comma splice and is also missing the comma after the transition. D has no punctuation at all between the clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence.

quality.seed: social science research — Availability heuristic memory accessibility and probability estimation overweighting easily recalled examples

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞 "Most participants picked the first position, a judgment that seems sensible at first glance"는 동격구가 붙은 독립절, 뒤 "words with K ... are ... common, but they are ... recall"도 독립절. 세미콜론+전환어+쉼표인 A만 적법. B·C는 comma splice, D는 run-on. 사실 확인: Tversky & Kahneman(1973) 'Availability' 논문의 K 위치 실험과 '3번째 위치가 약 2배' 주장 모두 원문과 일치. 해설 한·영 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 난이도: 긴 동격구로 첫 절의 독립성을 가리는 2단계 판단이 필요하고, B·C가 삽입어처럼 보여 비교가 필요하며 D도 표면상 그럴듯함 → medium 적합(세미콜론이 한 선택지뿐이라 다소 쉬운 편일 수 있음). 사소: D 선택지 앞 공백 표기.

advisory.note: 긴 동격 명사구 때문에 앞 절의 경계를 판단해야 하고, B가 그럴듯한 오답이어서 medium에 맞는다. 'in fact'와 'actually'가 함께 쓰여 약간 중복되지만 어법 오류는 아니다. 1973년 Tversky·Kahneman 연구의 K 사례도 사실과 맞는다.

This assumption, known as the fixed-pie bias, can prove surprisingly costly______ often overlook integrative trades that would leave both parties better off, such as giving up a point on a low-priority issue in exchange for a concession on a high-priority one.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 완전한 독립절이고 뒤의 내용은 그 '비용'을 설명하는 또 하나의 독립절이므로, 콜론으로 두 절을 이어야 한다. 또한 "who hold it"은 어떤 협상가인지 한정하는 필수 수식어이므로 쉼표로 분리하면 안 된다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 콜론은 맞지만 필수 수식어를 쉼표로 감싸 모든 협상가가 그 편향을 가진 것처럼 의미를 바꾼다. C는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 되고, D는 두 독립절 사이에 아무 문장부호가 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 되며 필수 수식어에 쉼표까지 넣었다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank is a complete independent clause, and what follows is another independent clause explaining why the bias is costly, so a colon correctly joins them. Also, "who hold it" is an essential modifier: it tells you which negotiators are meant, so it shouldn't be set off with commas. That makes A correct. B uses the colon correctly, but the commas make the modifier nonessential, which wrongly suggests that all negotiators hold the bias. C joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. D puts no punctuation between the clauses, so it's a run-on, and it also wrongly sets off the essential modifier with commas.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞 "This assumption ... can prove surprisingly costly"는 독립절, 뒤 "negotiators who hold it often overlook integrative trades..."도 독립절이며 앞 절의 '비용'을 설명하므로 콜론이 적절. advisory.note: 두 가지를 판단해야 함(절 경계 + 제한적/비제한적 수식어). B가 가장 강력한 함정 선지이고 C·D는 각각 쉼표 오류, 무종지문으로 배제됨. 중간 난이도에 적합.

problem.passage:
In a 1992 paper, economists Sushil Bikhchandani, David Hirshleifer, and Ivo Welch described the information cascade, a situation in which people who make decisions one after another begin to ignore their own private information and simply copy those who acted ______ once such a cascade forms, each new imitator adds nothing to the public pool of knowledge, so even a vast crowd of investors may be resting on the judgments of just a few early movers.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In a 1992 paper, economists Sushil Bikhchandani, David Hirshleifer, and Ivo Welch described the information cascade, a situation in which people who make decisions one after another begin to ignore their own private information and simply copy those who acted ______ once such a cascade forms, each new imitator adds nothing to the public pool of knowledge, so even a vast crowd of investors may be resting on the judgments of just a few early movers.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 긴 동격 수식어(a situation in which ...)가 끝난 뒤, 'once such a cascade forms, each new imitator adds...'라는 새 독립절이 시작되므로 두 독립절을 바르게 잇는 경계가 필요하다. B의 세미콜론은 두 독립절을 올바르게 연결한다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 run-on이 된다. D는 등위접속사 and 앞에 쉼표가 없어 긴 두 독립절이 부적절하게 결합되고, 'copy those who acted earlier and once...'로 잘못 읽힌다.
problem.explanationEn: After the long appositive phrase (a situation in which ...) ends, a new independent clause begins: "once such a cascade forms, each new imitator adds...". So you need punctuation that can join two independent clauses. B works because a semicolon correctly links two independent clauses. A uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C has no punctuation at all, so the two clauses run together. D puts "and" between two long independent clauses with no comma before it, which is nonstandard, and it also makes the sentence read as if "earlier and once" belong together.

quality.seed: social science research — Bandwagon effect information cascade and sequential decision-making herd behavior financial markets asset bubbles

hardJudge.note: 첫 독립절(economists ... described the information cascade, a situation in which ... copy those who acted earlier)과 둘째 독립절(once such a cascade forms, each new imitator adds ..., so ...)의 경계이므로 세미콜론(B)이 유일하게 적합. A는 comma splice, C는 run-on, D는 쉼표 없는 and로 두 긴 독립절을 결합하고 'earlier and once'로 오독되게 함. 한·영 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 글자 참조 일치, 한글 혼입 없음. 1992년 Bikhchandani·Hirshleifer·Welch의 정보 폭포 논문은 실제 사실. 긴 동격구 뒤에 종속절(once ...)로 시작하는 독립절이 이어져 경계 식별에 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 A·D가 그럴듯한 오답이므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 1992년 Bikhchandani·Hirshleifer·Welch 논문의 정보 폭포 개념 설명은 사실과 맞다. 정답은 세미콜론(B)이다. 앞쪽 수식어가 길어 절의 경계를 찾기 어렵고, 빈칸 뒤 'once' 종속절 때문에 C와 D가 그럴듯해 보여 medium 난이도에 맞다.

Statisticians urge caution, however. Because a single year's unusually low score partly reflects bad luck, such as a flu outbreak during testing week or a noisy exam room, scores tend to drift back toward the average on their own. This tendency, known as regression to the mean ______ an improvement that would have occurred even without any intervention.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: can make a program appear to cause
; can make a program appear to cause
, it can make a program appear to cause
, can make a program appear to cause
problem.explanation: "known as regression to the mean"은 주어 "This tendency"와 동사 "can make" 사이에 끼어든 비필수 삽입구이다. 앞에 쉼표가 이미 열려 있으므로 뒤에도 쉼표로 닫아야 하며, 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 닫는 쉼표가 없어 삽입구가 끝나지 않은 채 동사로 이어진다. B의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 있어야 하는데, 앞부분은 동사가 없는 주어구일 뿐이다. C는 쉼표를 제대로 넣었지만 주어 "This tendency"를 대명사 "it"으로 다시 반복해 문장의 주어가 중복된다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "known as regression to the mean" is a nonessential element that interrupts the subject "This tendency" and its verb "can make." A comma already opens the phrase, so another comma has to close it, which makes D correct. A leaves out the closing comma, so the interrupting phrase runs straight into the verb. B uses a semicolon, but a semicolon needs an independent clause on each side, and the words before the blank are only a subject phrase with no verb. C closes the phrase correctly but then adds "it," which repeats the subject "This tendency" and gives the sentence two subjects.

quality.seed: social science research — Regression to mean statistical phenomenon and misattribution to causal interventions in performance improvement

hardJudge.note: 검산: "This tendency, known as regression to the mean, can make a program appear to cause an improvement..." — 주어 뒤 쉼표가 이미 열려 있으므로 삽입구를 닫는 쉼표가 필요. D 정답 확인. A(닫는 쉼표 누락)와 C(쉼표는 맞지만 'it'으로 주어 중복)는 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답이고, B(세미콜론)도 문장 구조를 훑어 읽으면 선택할 수 있어 medium 기준(규칙 적용 + 앞 문맥의 열린 쉼표 확인) 충족. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 통계 내용(평균으로의 회귀) 사실관계 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 삽입구를 닫는 쉼표를 묻는 표준 문항이다. 오답 B와 C는 그럴듯하고, A는 훑어 읽는 수험생을 유인한다. 다만 회귀 효과가 개선을 '일으킨' 것처럼 보이게 한다는 문장 의미가 약간 어색하다는 점은 사소한 흠이다.

problem.passage:

The results have not been uniform. A version conducted in Germany, a nation whose postwar culture was often assumed to discourage blind deference, produced obedience rates higher than Milgram's ______ an Australian replication found noticeably lower rates, particularly among female participants. Researchers caution that differences in procedure make such cross-cultural comparisons difficult to interpret.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Stanley Milgram's obedience studies, in which participants were instructed to deliver what they believed were painful shocks to another person, have been replicated in several countries. The results have not been uniform. A version conducted in Germany, a nation whose postwar culture was often assumed to discourage blind deference, produced obedience rates higher than Milgram's ______ an Australian replication found noticeably lower rates, particularly among female participants. Researchers caution that differences in procedure make such cross-cultural comparisons difficult to interpret.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "A version ... produced obedience rates higher than Milgram's original"과 뒤 "an Australian replication found..."는 각각 독립절이며, "by contrast"는 뒤 절에 속하는 접속부사이다. 따라서 세미콜론으로 두 절을 나누고 접속부사 뒤에 쉼표를 찍은 A가 맞다. B와 D는 접속부사를 쉼표로만 연결해 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 세미콜론 위치가 틀려 "by contrast"가 앞 절에 붙어 버리므로, 앞 절과 대조되어야 할 뒤 절이 대조 표지를 잃게 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank ("A version ... produced obedience rates higher than Milgram's original") is an independent clause, and so is the text after it ("an Australian replication found..."). The transition "by contrast" goes with the second clause. A is correct because it separates the two clauses with a semicolon and puts a comma after the transition. B and D join two independent clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. C puts the semicolon in the wrong spot: "by contrast" ends up attached to the first clause, so the second clause, which is the one actually being contrasted, loses its contrast signal.

quality.seed: social science research — Milgram obedience experiments variation and cultural differences in authority compliance across Japan Germany Australia

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞("A version ... produced obedience rates higher than Milgram's original")과 뒤("an Australian replication found ...")는 모두 독립절이며 "by contrast"는 뒤 절의 접속부사 → "original; by contrast," (A)가 유일하게 올바름. B·D는 comma splice, C는 세미콜론 자체는 두 독립절을 나누지만 "by contrast"가 앞 절에 붙어 의미·관습상 부적절(SAT 표준 오답 패턴). 한국어·영어 해설 모두 A를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 사실 관계(독일 Mantell 1971 높은 복종률, 호주 Kilham & Mann 1974 낮은 복종률·여성 참가자에서 특히 낮음) 정확. 난이도: 독립절 판별 + 접속부사 소속 절 판단의 두 단계가 필요하고 C가 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능하여 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 세미콜론+접속부사 배치 문항으로, 앞뒤 절을 확인해야 하므로 medium에 맞음. D는 쉼표조차 불완전해 다소 약한 오답이지만 허용 범위임. 독일 재현 연구(Mantell 1971, 약 85%)와 호주 재현 연구(Kilham & Mann 1974, 여성 복종률 낮음)는 사실과 대체로 부합함.

problem.passage:

By the year's end, many of those students ______ researchers have since argued that the teachers' altered behavior, such as offering more praise and longer wait times, rather than any trait of the students themselves, produced the difference.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In their 1968 study, psychologist Robert Rosenthal and school principal Lenore Jacobson told teachers that certain randomly chosen students, identified by a supposedly predictive test of "intellectual blooming," would make unusual gains during the year. By the year's end, many of those students ______ researchers have since argued that the teachers' altered behavior, such as offering more praise and longer wait times, rather than any trait of the students themselves, produced the difference.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: had, in fact, outperformed their peers on IQ measures,
had, in fact, outperformed their peers on IQ measures, and,
had, in fact, outperformed their peers on IQ measures;
had in fact, outperformed their peers on IQ measures; and
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'many of those students had ... outperformed'는 독립절이고, 뒤의 'researchers have since argued...' 역시 독립절이므로 두 절을 바르게 연결해야 한다. C는 삽입구 'in fact'를 쉼표 한 쌍으로 바르게 감싸고 세미콜론으로 두 독립절을 연결하므로 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. B는 'and' 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 'and'와 주어 사이를 끊는다. D는 'in fact' 앞 쉼표가 빠져 삽입구가 짝을 이루지 못하고, 세미콜론과 'and'를 함께 쓰는 것도 부적절하다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank ("many of those students had ... outperformed their peers") form an independent clause, and "researchers have since argued..." is another independent clause, so the two need a proper boundary. Choice C correctly sets off "in fact" with a pair of commas and joins the clauses with a semicolon, so it's the right answer. Choice A uses only a comma between two independent clauses, which creates a comma splice. Choice B adds a comma after "and" that wrongly separates the conjunction from the subject of the clause it introduces. Choice D leaves out the comma before "in fact," so the interrupting phrase isn't enclosed by a matching pair, and it also uses a semicolon together with "and," which doesn't work.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞 "many of those students had, in fact, outperformed their peers on IQ measures"는 독립절, 뒤 "researchers have since argued..."도 독립절. C(삽입구 쉼표 쌍 + 세미콜론)만 바른 경계. A는 comma splice, B는 'and' 뒤 불필요한 쉼표, D는 'in fact' 앞 쉼표 누락 + '; and' 중복 연결로 배제됨. 한국어·영어 해설 결론과 글자 참조 일치, 모순 없음. Rosenthal & Jacobson(1968) 'Pygmalion in the Classroom' 관련 사실(무작위 선정, "intellectual blooming" 검사, 교사 행동 변화 설명) 정확. 난이도: 독립절 2개 식별 + 삽입구 쉼표 쌍 확인의 두 단계 판단이 필요하고, B·D가 부분적으로 그럴듯한 요소('and' 사용, 세미콜론 사용)를 가져 비교가 필요하므로 medium 적합. 형식상 선택지 끝 공백(B, C)은 사소함.

advisory.note: C의 세미콜론으로 두 독립절이 바르게 연결된다. A는 comma splice, B는 'and' 뒤에 쉼표 하나만 붙어 있어 오류, D는 삽입구 쉼표 짝이 맞지 않고 '; and'도 부적절하다. 오답마다 그럴듯한 요소가 있어 medium 난이도에 맞다. B 선택지 끝에 공백이 하나 남아 있으나 사소하다. 피그말리온 연구 사실관계(1968년, Rosenthal과 초등학교 교장 Jacobson)도 정확하다.

problem.stimulus: In 1973, psychologist David Rosenhan published the results of an unusual experiment. Eight mentally healthy volunteers, Rosenhan himself among them, sought admission to psychiatric hospitals by reporting that they heard a voice saying words such as "empty" and "hollow." Once admitted, the pseudopatients stopped mentioning any symptoms and behaved ______ staff nonetheless interpreted ordinary actions, such as taking notes, as evidence of mental illness.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "the pseudopatients ... behaved normally"와 뒤 "hospital staff nonetheless interpreted ..."는 각각 독립절이므로 둘을 이으려면 쉼표+등위접속사나 세미콜론이 필요하다. D는 쉼표와 'but'으로 두 절을 바르게 연결하고, 'nonetheless'가 나타내는 대조와도 맞는다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 쉼표 오류(comma splice)다. B는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. C는 세미콜론 뒤에 'and'를 불필요하게 넣어 표준 용법에 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank ("the pseudopatients ... behaved normally") and the words after it ("hospital staff nonetheless interpreted ...") are both independent clauses, so you need either a comma plus a coordinating conjunction or a semicolon to join them. D does this correctly with a comma and "but," and "but" also fits the contrast that "nonetheless" signals. A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes it a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between the clauses at all, so it's a run-on sentence. C adds an unnecessary "and" after the semicolon, which isn't standard usage.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞뒤가 모두 독립절("the pseudopatients ... behaved normally" / "hospital staff nonetheless interpreted ...")임을 직접 확인함. D(쉼표+but)만 표준 연결이며, A는 comma splice, B는 run-on, C는 세미콜론+and 비표준 결합으로 정답 유일성 확보. 'but'과 'nonetheless' 공존은 표준 영어에서 허용되는 용법. Rosenhan 1973 실험 세부(8명, "empty"/"hollow", 필기 행위를 증상으로 해석)는 사실과 부합. 지문은 자체 작성 서술로 저작권 우려 없음. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 결론이 동일하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 독립절 판별 + 적절한 연결 수단 선택의 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 A·C가 그럴듯한 함정이므로 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: Rosenhan(1973) 관련 사실이 맞다. 'nonetheless'와 'but'이 함께 쓰여도 허용된다. 쉼표 오류, 무종지문, 세미콜론+and를 고르는 표준적인 경계 문항이며 medium 난이도로 적절하다.

Dunning and Kruger argued that this pattern is not simple arrogance: the very skills needed to answer the questions correctly are also the skills needed to recognize a wrong answer, so poor performers lack the means to detect their own errors. In this view, low competence and inflated self-assessment are ______, two outcomes of a single underlying deficit rather than separate problems.

Dunning and Kruger argued that this pattern is not simple arrogance: the very skills needed to answer the questions correctly are also the skills needed to recognize a wrong answer, so poor performers lack the means to detect their own errors. In this view, low competence and inflated self-assessment are ______, two outcomes of a single underlying deficit rather than separate problems.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 문제를 푸는 능력과 오답을 알아보는 능력이 같다고 하므로, 낮은 능력과 부풀려진 자기평가는 '하나의 결핍에서 나온 두 결과', 즉 서로 얽혀 있다(B). A는 둘이 함께 나타난다는 점은 맞지만, 우연이라는 뜻이어서 공통 원인을 강조하는 지문과 맞지 않는다. C는 낮은 점수와 높은 자기평가가 겉보기에 어긋나 보인다는 점에 끌리지만, 저자는 둘이 일관되게 설명된다고 주장한다. D는 밀접한 관계를 암시하기는 하지만, 지문은 둘을 '두 결과'로 구분하므로 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다는 뜻은 지나치다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the skills needed to answer correctly are the same skills needed to spot errors, so low competence and inflated self-assessment come from one shared deficit. That makes them intertwined, which is choice B. Choice A fits the idea that the two show up together, but calling them accidental contradicts the text's point about a common cause. Choice C may tempt you because a low score paired with high confidence looks inconsistent, but the authors argue the two fit together logically. Choice D does suggest a close link, but the text treats them as "two outcomes," so saying they are interchangeable goes too far.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 뒤 동격구 "two outcomes of a single underlying deficit rather than separate problems"가 '서로 얽혀 있다(intertwined)'를 명확히 뒷받침하며, 앞 문장의 '같은 기술이 필요하다'는 논리와 연결해야 하므로 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. A(coincidental)는 공존은 맞지만 공통 원인을 부정하고, C(contradictory)는 낮은 점수·높은 자평의 표면적 모순에 끌리게 하며, D(interchangeable)는 밀접함은 맞지만 '두 결과'로 구분한 지문과 충돌해 오답 설계가 적절하다. Dunning–Kruger(1999) 실험 묘사(논리·문법 테스트, 하위 25%의 과대평가)도 사실과 부합한다. 한·영 해설 결론과 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음.

advisory.note: Dunning-Kruger(1999) 내용을 정확하게 요약함. 'two outcomes of a single underlying deficit'라는 단서가 B를 뒷받침하고, A·C·D는 각각 그럴듯한 함정 역할을 함. 문맥을 확인해야 풀 수 있어 중간 난이도에 맞음.

problem.stimulus: In a series of simulated used-car negotiations, researchers found that the price named first by the seller tended to shape where talks ended, even when buyers had been given accurate market data beforehand. Buyers who heard a high opening figure adjusted downward from it, but rarely far enough; their final offers stayed closer to the seller's number than to the market value. According to the researchers, the opening figure does not merely start the conversation; it ______ the range of outcomes that both parties come to regard as reasonable.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 구매자가 첫 제시 가격에서 하향 조정하지만 충분히 벗어나지 못해 결과가 그 숫자 근처에 머문다고 설명하므로, 첫 가격이 합리적으로 여겨지는 결과의 범위를 제한한다는 D(constrains)가 정답이다. A(predicts)는 첫 가격과 결과가 연관된다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 첫 가격이 결과를 실제로 형성한다는 인과적 영향이 아니라 단순한 예측만 뜻한다. B(announces)는 판매자가 숫자를 '말한다'는 표면적 의미와 맞아 보이지만, 범위를 알리는 것이 아니라 범위에 영향을 준다는 핵심을 놓친다. C(disrupts)는 영향력은 있음을 나타내지만, 지문은 기대를 흐트러뜨리는 것이 아니라 일정한 방향으로 묶어 둔다고 말하므로 맞지 않다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says buyers adjust downward from the seller's first price but not far enough, so their offers stay near that number. That means the opening figure limits the range of outcomes people see as reasonable, which makes D (constrains) the answer. A (predicts) is tempting because the first price and the final outcome are linked, but "predicts" only means forecasting, while the text describes the first price actually shaping the result. B (announces) matches the idea of the seller stating a number, but the point is that the figure influences the range, not that it declares it. C (disrupts) does suggest influence, but the text says the figure pulls expectations toward it rather than throwing them into disorder.

problem.explanationEn: The text says that the preference formed through repeated contact alone, without conversation or conscious recognition, so A ("fostered"), which means encouraged to develop, is the best answer. B ("forgotten") is tempting because students hardly remembered seeing the woman, but what they forgot was the exposure, not the liking. C ("disclosed") might seem to fit because the ratings made the liking visible, but the main point is that repeated contact created the liking, not that it revealed it. D ("tested") matches the experimental setting, but repeated contact didn't test liking; it produced it, which is what the last clause says.

C는 투자와 관련된 단어이지만 자원을 예측한다는 것은 실제로 돈을 쓰는 일이 아니고, Staw가 미래 수익 계산 문제가 아니라고 한 점과도 맞지 않는다. D는 자원 배분과 관련 있어 보이지만 기존 자원을 재배치한다는 뜻일 뿐, 실패한 프로젝트에 '추가로' 투입한다는 의미를 정확히 담지 못한다.

So the blank needs a verb meaning "put in" more resources, and that makes B the answer. A means holding resources back, which is the opposite of spending more. C fits the investment setting, but forecasting resources is not the same as actually spending them, and Staw says the behavior is not a calculation about future returns. B(conceal)는 불편함을 다룬다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 지문에 나온 것은 남에게 감정을 숨기는 것이 아니라 태도를 바꿔 불편함 자체를 줄이는 과정이다. C(anticipate)는 결정과 관련된 감정이라는 점은 맞지만, 평가 변화는 선택을 한 뒤에 일어났으므로 불편함을 '예상하는' 것과는 맞지 않는다. D(intensify)는 불편함을 더 키운다는 뜻이어서 "eased"와 정반대다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says participants rated the chosen item higher and the rejected item lower so their decision would seem correct, and that this "eased the tension." So the blank needs a word meaning "reduce," and that makes A (alleviate) the answer. B (conceal) is tempting because it also deals with discomfort, but the participants didn't hide their feelings from anyone; they changed their attitudes so the discomfort itself got smaller. C (anticipate) does connect to feelings about a decision, but the ratings changed after the choice was made, so they weren't predicting a feeling in advance. D (intensify) means making the discomfort stronger, which is the opposite of "eased."

A(verify)는 '확인하다'라는 뜻으로 수사와 관련된 말처럼 들리지만, 피드백은 확신을 검증하는 것이 아니라 정확도와 상관없이 왜곡한다. B(diminish)는 '왜곡'이라는 방향은 맞지만 확신이 줄어든다는 의미라서 '커진다'는 지문 내용과 반대다. C(document)는 기록 행위를 뜻해 '영향'이 하는 일을 나타내지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says confidence "grows" because of encouraging feedback and rehearsal, even though memory doesn't improve. So the blank has to describe these influences making confidence bigger without good reason, and D, "inflate," does exactly that. A, "verify," fits the investigative setting, but feedback doesn't check confidence; it distorts it no matter how accurate the witness is. B, "diminish," gets the idea of distortion right but points the wrong way, because the passage says confidence increases. C, "document," means recording, which isn't something these influences do to confidence.

quality.seed: social science research — Eyewitness memory confidence accuracy dissociation and false identification rates in criminal justice lineups

hardJudge.note: 지문의 'confidence often grows ... even though memory does not improve'와 'before such influences can ___ it'를 연결하면 D(inflate)가 유일하게 논리적. B(diminish)는 방향 반대, A(verify)는 수사 맥락에 어울리는 그럴듯한 오답, C(document)는 문맥상 부적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. Gary Wells의 사후 피드백/확신 부풀리기 연구는 실제 내용과 부합. 두 정보 연결이 필요하고 오답 구조가 적절해 medium에 부합.

advisory.note: 'grows'와 'encouraging feedback'이라는 단서를 통해 방향을 판단해야 함. diminish는 방향을 거꾸로 잡은 매력 오답이고, verify·document는 사법·수사 맥락에 그럴듯하게 어울림. medium 난이도에 적합.

In studies of source amnesia, participants often recall a fact accurately while forgetting where they learned it—attributing, for example, a claim they read on an anonymous website to a respected newspaper. Psychologist Marcia Johnson and colleagues found that this error does more than blur memory's origins: because people tend to judge a remembered claim's reliability by its imagined source, a misattribution can ______ their confidence, leading them to trust weakly supported information as though it had been carefully vetted.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In studies of source amnesia, participants often recall a fact accurately while forgetting where they learned it—attributing, for example, a claim they read on an anonymous website to a respected newspaper. Psychologist Marcia Johnson and colleagues found that this error does more than blur memory's origins: because people tend to judge a remembered claim's reliability by its imagined source, a misattribution can ______ their confidence, leading them to trust weakly supported information as though it had been carefully vetted.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 출처를 잘못 기억하면 사람들이 근거가 약한 정보를 검증된 정보처럼 믿게 된다고 하므로, 출처 오귀속이 확신을 부당하게 '부풀린다'는 뜻의 A가 정답이다. B는 확신을 흔든다는 뜻이라 신뢰가 커진다는 결과와 반대이다. C는 확신을 그대로 보여 준다는 뜻이어서, 오류가 확신을 왜곡해 키운다는 인과 관계를 담지 못한다. D는 확신을 숨긴다는 뜻이지만, 지문은 확신이 감춰지는 게 아니라 오히려 커져 신뢰로 이어진다고 말한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says that misremembering a source leads people to trust weakly supported information as if it had been vetted, so the misattribution must inflate, or unjustifiably increase, their confidence. That makes A correct. B is wrong because "unsettle" means weakening confidence, which is the opposite of the greater trust the text describes. C is wrong because "reflect" only means showing confidence as it is, so it misses the idea that the error distorts confidence upward. D is wrong because the text never says confidence is hidden; it says confidence grows and turns into trust.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 뒤 "leading them to trust weakly supported information as though it had been carefully vetted"가 확신의 '증가'를 요구하므로 A(inflate)가 유일하게 정확하다. B(unsettle)는 지문 전반의 부정적 어조("error", "blur")만 훑으면 고를 수 있는 반대 의미 오답, C(reflect)는 "judge reliability by its imagined source"와 부분적으로 연결되어 비교가 필요하며, D(conceal)도 "blur memory's origins"와 표면적으로 연결되어 말이 된다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. Marcia Johnson의 출처 모니터링 연구 언급은 사실적으로 타당. 표절 의심 없음. 두 단계 추론(인과 구조 파악 + 결과 문맥 확인)이 필요해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 'trust weakly supported information as though vetted'에서 방향(증가)과 부당성을 함께 읽어야 하는 2단계 판단 구조. unsettle은 지문의 '흐림(blur)'에 끌린 오답으로, reflect는 '출처로 신뢰도를 판단한다'는 논리에 끌린 오답으로 그럴듯하다. 다만 D(conceal)는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Psychologists studying the illusory truth effect have found that repeated exposure to a false claim can make it seem more credible, even to people who initially doubted it. In one study, participants who had correctly labeled a headline as false when first seeing it rated the same headline as more accurate after encountering it several more times. The researchers concluded that repetition does not simply reinforce beliefs people already hold; rather, it can gradually ______ their original skepticism, so that a claim once dismissed comes to feel plausible.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Psychologists studying the illusory truth effect have found that repeated exposure to a false claim can make it seem more credible, even to people who initially doubted it. In one study, participants who had correctly labeled a headline as false when first seeing it rated the same headline as more accurate after encountering it several more times. The researchers concluded that repetition does not simply reinforce beliefs people already hold; rather, it can gradually ______ their original skepticism, so that a claim once dismissed comes to feel plausible.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 처음에 거짓이라고 판단했던 참가자들도 반복 노출 후 같은 헤드라인을 더 정확하다고 평가했다고 말하므로, 반복이 원래의 회의감을 점차 약화시킨다는 의미가 필요하다. 따라서 '서서히 약화시키다'라는 뜻의 B가 'gradually'와 결과(일축했던 주장이 그럴듯해짐)에 모두 들어맞는다. A는 회의감을 강화한다는 뜻이 되어 결과와 정반대이며, '기존 믿음을 강화하는 것만은 아니다'라는 구절에 끌린 오답이다. C는 회의감을 드러낸다는 뜻이라 회의감이 줄어드는 과정을 설명하지 못한다. D는 회의감을 불러일으킨다는 뜻이라 처음부터 있던 회의감과 맞지 않고, 신뢰가 커지는 결과와도 반대다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says that participants who first labeled a headline false later rated it more accurate after seeing it again, so repetition must gradually weaken their original doubt. Choice B, meaning "to wear away slowly," fits both "gradually" and the result that a dismissed claim comes to feel plausible. Choice A would mean repetition strengthens the skepticism, which is the opposite of the finding; it may tempt you because of the phrase about reinforcing beliefs. Choice C would mean repetition only makes the skepticism visible, which doesn't explain why it fades. Choice D would mean repetition creates skepticism, but the participants already had it, and the result shows their trust growing, not their doubt.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 'erode'는 'gradually', 'original skepticism', 'so that a claim once dismissed comes to feel plausible'와 논리적으로 일치. A는 'reinforce beliefs' 구절에 끌리는 유인 오답, C·D도 문맥상 그럴듯하되 배제 가능. 해설 한·영 모두 글자 참조 일치, 한글 혼입 없음. 지문은 일반적 심리학 연구 요약으로 특정 출처 복제 의심 없음. 'rather' 대비 구조와 결과절을 함께 읽어야 하므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 명확하다. A(confirm)는 'reinforce' 구절에 끌리게 만든 오답으로 잘 작동한다. 다만 C와 D는 너무 쉽게 배제되므로 medium 난이도로서는 하한선에 가깝다.

problem.passage:
In a classic study of hindsight bias, participants estimated the likelihood of various outcomes of an upcoming diplomatic trip before it happened. After the trip, they were asked to recall exactly what probabilities they had originally given. Rather than reproducing their earlier estimates faithfully, participants tended to ______ them: outcomes they now knew had occurred were remembered as having been judged more likely than the participants had actually rated them, as though knowledge of the result had quietly rewritten their prior predictions.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In a classic study of hindsight bias, participants estimated the likelihood of various outcomes of an upcoming diplomatic trip before it happened. After the trip, they were asked to recall exactly what probabilities they had originally given. Rather than reproducing their earlier estimates faithfully, participants tended to ______ them: outcomes they now knew had occurred were remembered as having been judged more likely than the participants had actually rated them, as though knowledge of the result had quietly rewritten their prior predictions.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 참가자들이 이전 추정치를 그대로 재현하지 않고, 결과를 안 뒤 실제 일어난 결과의 확률을 더 높게 기억했다고 설명하므로, 기억을 '왜곡하다'라는 의미의 C가 정답이다. A는 '정확히 재현하지 않았다'는 부분과는 맞지만, 참가자들은 추정치를 잊은 것이 아니라 특정 방향으로 바꿔 기억했으므로 적절하지 않다. B는 일부 확률을 높게 기억했다는 점과 겹치지만, 지문은 추정치 전체를 과장했다기보다 알게 된 결과 쪽으로 다시 썼다고 말하므로 정확하지 않다. D는 참가자들이 자신의 추정치를 의심했다는 근거가 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says participants didn't reproduce their earlier estimates faithfully. Instead, they remembered outcomes that had actually happened as more likely than they had first rated them, as if the result had "rewritten" their predictions. That is distorting a memory, so C is correct. A fits the idea that their recall wasn't faithful, but they didn't simply lose their estimates; they changed them in a specific direction. B overlaps with some probabilities being recalled as higher, but the text describes estimates being reshaped to match the known result, not all of them being inflated. D doesn't work because nothing in the text suggests participants doubted their estimates.

quality.seed: social science research — Hindsight bias knew-it-all-along effect and outcome knowledge distorting recall of prior predictions

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 뒤 콜론 이하가 "실제 일어난 결과를 더 높게 기억 / 결과 지식이 예측을 다시 썼다"로 정의하므로 '왜곡하다(distort)'가 정확. B(exaggerate)는 '더 높게 기억'과 부분적으로 겹치지만 추정치 전체를 부풀린 것이 아니라 결과 방향으로 선택적으로 바꾼 것이므로 배제되고, A(forget)는 '그대로 재현하지 않았다'와 부분 일치하나 방향성 있는 변경과 불일치, D는 근거 없음. 두 단계 판단(대조 구조 + 콜론 뒤 설명 확인)이 필요하고 오답 2개가 부분 근거를 가져 medium에 적합. 소재는 Fischhoff & Beyth(1975) 닉슨 외교 순방 연구와 부합하며 사실 오류 없음. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음.

advisory.note: B(exaggerate)는 강한 오답이다. 지문에 명시된 것은 실제 일어난 결과의 확률을 부풀려 기억했다는 점뿐이기 때문이다. 다만 'them'은 추정치 전체를 가리키고 'rewritten'은 한 방향의 과장보다 넓은 '변형'을 뜻하므로 C가 더 정확하다. Fischhoff & Beyth(1975) 연구를 일반적으로 묘사한 것이며 사실 오류는 없다.

problem.passage:
In a classic set of experiments, participants read a brief personality sketch of "Jack," described as reserved, fond of mathematical puzzles, and uninterested in politics. They were told Jack had been drawn at random from a pool of 100 people, only 30 of whom were engineers. Even so, most participants judged Jack very likely to be an engineer, and their estimates barely changed when the pool was said to contain 70 engineers instead. Psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky argued that such judgments ______ the statistical information entirely: people rated how closely Jack matched a stereotype of an engineer and treated that resemblance as if it were probability.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In a classic set of experiments, participants read a brief personality sketch of "Jack," described as reserved, fond of mathematical puzzles, and uninterested in politics. They were told Jack had been drawn at random from a pool of 100 people, only 30 of whom were engineers. Even so, most participants judged Jack very likely to be an engineer, and their estimates barely changed when the pool was said to contain 70 engineers instead. Psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky argued that such judgments ______ the statistical information entirely: people rated how closely Jack matched a stereotype of an engineer and treated that resemblance as if it were probability.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 엔지니어 비율이 30명에서 70명으로 바뀌어도 추정치가 거의 변하지 않았다고 하고, 빈칸 뒤에서 'entirely'와 함께 사람들이 고정관념 유사성만 사용했다고 설명하므로, 통계 정보를 '무시했다'는 D가 정답이다. A는 정보를 왜곡했다는 뜻인데, 참가자들은 기저율을 잘못 전달한 것이 아니라 아예 사용하지 않았다. B는 정보를 과장했다는 뜻이어서 오히려 기저율에 큰 비중을 두었다는 의미가 되므로 추정치가 변하지 않은 결과와 모순된다. C는 정보를 의심했다는 뜻으로, 의식적으로 검토했다는 암시가 있어 단순히 간과했다는 지문의 서술과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says estimates barely changed when the share of engineers went from 30 to 70, and the sentence after the blank explains that people relied only on how well Jack fit a stereotype, so D ("disregarded," together with "entirely") fits best. A suggests participants distorted the base rates, but they didn't misstate the numbers; they just didn't use them. B would mean they gave the statistics too much weight, which contradicts the fact that their estimates stayed the same. C implies they consciously doubted the numbers, but the text describes people overlooking the numbers, not challenging them.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검증: 기저율이 30→70으로 바뀌어도 추정치가 거의 변하지 않았고, 빈칸 뒤에서 고정관념 유사성만을 확률로 취급했다고 하므로 통계 정보를 '완전히 무시했다(disregarded ... entirely)'가 유일하게 논리적. A(왜곡)·C(의심)은 정보를 어떤 식으로든 다루었다는 함의가 있어 배제되고, B(과장)은 결과와 정면 모순. 한·영 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조이며 모순 없음. 사실 관계: Kahneman & Tversky(1973) 엔지니어-변호사 문제의 'Jack' 묘사 및 30/70 조건 설정과 일치. 지문은 실험 요약의 자체 서술로 저작권 우려 없음. 난이도: 'barely changed'와 'entirely'를 연결해야 하는 두 단계 추론이 있고 A·C가 부분적 타당성을 가지므로 medium에 부합(다소 쉬운 편이나 허용 범위).

advisory.note: Kahneman & Tversky(1973)의 엔지니어-변호사 기저율 실험을 바꿔 쓴 내용이며, 성격 묘사를 축약한 것은 허용 범위다. 정답을 고르려면 '30→70으로 바꿔도 추정치가 거의 변하지 않음'과 빈칸 뒤의 '고정관념 유사성만 사용함'을 함께 고려해야 한다. 'entirely'가 단서로 꽤 강하지만, A(misrepresented)와 C(questioned)는 둘 다 통계 정보를 제대로 쓰지 않았다는 방향이라 부분적으로 그럴듯하다. 그래서 비교해 봐야 배제된다.

Instead, she found that vendors adjusted their bargaining styles depending on whether she, a university-affiliated outsider, was nearby. Rather than treating this effect as a flaw to be hidden, Okonkwo chose to ______ it in her published analysis, devoting an entire chapter to how her own position shaped what she was able to observe.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: When anthropologist Mara Okonkwo began fieldwork among street vendors in Lagos, she expected that her long-term presence in the market would gradually make her invisible, allowing her to record interactions as they "naturally" occurred. Instead, she found that vendors adjusted their bargaining styles depending on whether she, a university-affiliated outsider, was nearby. Rather than treating this effect as a flaw to be hidden, Okonkwo chose to ______ it in her published analysis, devoting an entire chapter to how her own position shaped what she was able to observe.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 오콘쿠오가 자신의 존재가 관찰에 미친 영향을 숨길 결함으로 보지 않고, 한 장 전체를 할애해 다루었다고 말한다. 따라서 그 영향을 분석에서 '전면에 내세우다'라는 뜻의 C가 가장 적절하다. A는 '최소화하다'로, 숨기지 않았다는 'Rather than' 대조와 정반대이다. B는 문제를 '해결하다'라는 뜻이라 결함을 다루는 것처럼 보이지만, 그녀는 효과를 없앤 것이 아니라 드러내 분석했다. D는 '예상하다'인데, 그녀는 오히려 자신이 보이지 않게 될 것이라고 예상했고 출판된 분석에서 한 일과도 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says Okonkwo refused to treat her influence on the vendors as a flaw to hide, and she gave a whole chapter to how her position shaped what she observed. So the blank needs a word meaning "make prominent," and that's C. A means to reduce or downplay, which is the opposite of what the "Rather than" contrast sets up. B sounds plausible because it's about dealing with a problem, but she didn't get rid of the effect; she brought it into the open and analyzed it.
