Interviews showed that many saw themselves as Dominican and Spanish-speaking first, and that they used Spanish to push back when others classified them as Black.
problem.question: Based on the texts, which part of the reasoning in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely challenge?
options: The claim that the teens' language patterns tell us something about how they see themselves socially
The observation that most of the participants had been born in the United States rather than in the Dominican Republic
The finding that the teens often shifted into African American English when talking with Black classmates
The belief that speaking African American English with Black peers mainly signals that a speaker identifies racially with them
problem.explanation:
정답 D: Text 1은 '흑인 친구와 대화할 때 AAE로 전환한다 → 흑인 정체성을 받아들인다'로 결론짓는데, 이 추론은 'AAE 사용이 곧 인종적 동일시를 뜻한다'는 가정에 기대고 있다. Text 2는 같은 학생들이 도미니카계·백인 친구와도 AAE를 썼고, 그 목적이 지역 청소년 문화에 속해 있다는 것을 보여주는 데 있었으며, 스스로를 도미니카인으로 여겼다고 보고한다. 따라서 Text 2가 정면으로 약화시키는 것은 바로 이 가정이다.
A: 언어 사용이 사회적 자기인식을 반영한다는 생각은 Text 2도 공유한다(또래 소속감을 나타내고, 스페인어로 분류에 저항함). 그러니 Text 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분이다.
B: 참가자 출생지는 부수적 세부일 뿐이고, Text 2는 이를 다루지 않는다.
C: Text 2는 이 전환 현상을 직접 확인했으므로 동의하는 부분이다.
problem.explanationEn:
D is correct. Text 1 reasons that because the teens shift into African American English (AAE) with Black classmates, they must be adopting a Black racial identity. That conclusion rests on an unstated assumption: that using AAE with Black peers mainly signals racial identification with them. Text 2 weakens this assumption directly. The same teens used AAE with Dominican and white friends to show they belonged to a local youth culture, and they saw themselves as Dominican first.
A is wrong because Text 2 agrees that language reflects social self-understanding. In Text 2, the teens use language to show group belonging and use Spanish to resist being classified as Black.
B is wrong because birthplace is a minor detail in Text 1, and Text 2 never discusses it.
C is wrong because Text 2 explicitly confirms this shifting pattern rather than disputing it.

hardJudge.note: Text 1의 결론(흑인 정체성 수용)과 근거(흑인 급우와 대화 시 AAE 전환)가 명확히 분리되어 있고, 그 사이를 잇는 암묵적 가정('흑인 또래와의 AAE 사용 = 인종적 동일시')이 D에 해당. Text 2는 같은 화자가 도미니카계·백인 친구와도 AAE를 썼고 목적이 지역 청소년 문화 소속감이었으며 자신을 도미니카인으로 규정했다고 보고하므로 D만 정면 공격. C는 Text 2가 명시적으로 확인한 관찰, A는 '언어가 사회적 자기인식을 반영한다'는 Text 2도 공유하는 넓은 전제(범위 과대 함정), B는 Text 2가 다루지 않는 부수 정보. 해설은 각 선택지 판정과 수치·논리 모순 없이 일관됨. Providence 도미니카계 연구(Bailey)를 소재로 하나 문장은 독자적 서술로 저작권 우려 없음. 정답을 고르려면 Text 2의 입장을 유지한 채 Text 1 논증의 어느 층위(관찰/가정/결론/일반 전제)가 흔들리는지 추론해야 하므로 medium 수준의 단순 역할 식별을 넘어섬.

advisory.note: D는 Text 1에 직접 쓰이지 않은 가정을 끌어내야 정답으로 보인다. A(언어가 자기인식을 반영한다는 점)는 Text 2도 공유하는 일반 명제이고, C는 Text 2가 확인한 관찰이라 강도와 범위를 구분해야 한다. B는 Text 2가 다루지 않는 부수적 세부이고, 지문은 Text 2가 '2세대' 학생을 다룬다고 밝혀 이 점을 비켜 간다. 문항은 대체로 견고하다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Sociolinguist Carmen Fought's research on Chicano English in Los Angeles is persuasive, in my view, because of how she justified her claims. Fought did not rely on a single measured feature. She paired recordings of speech with long-term observation of who spent time with whom, and she linked each linguistic pattern to specific social ties. For me, a claim that speech reflects belonging deserves acceptance only when it is supported by evidence about the speakers' actual social networks, not merely by where those speakers live.

Text 2
A recent survey of vowel pronunciation across several Los Angeles neighborhoods found that residents of predominantly Latino neighborhoods produced certain vowels differently from residents of nearby areas. The researchers recorded short word lists from hundreds of participants and grouped the results by home address. Because the differences lined up so neatly with neighborhood boundaries, the researchers concluded that these vowel patterns express residents' sense of belonging to their local community.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the conclusion reached by the researchers described in Text 2?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Sociolinguist Carmen Fought's research on Chicano English in Los Angeles is persuasive, in my view, because of how she justified her claims. Fought did not rely on a single measured feature. She paired recordings of speech with long-term observation of who spent time with whom, and she linked each linguistic pattern to specific social ties. For me, a claim that speech reflects belonging deserves acceptance only when it is supported by evidence about the speakers' actual social networks, not merely by where those speakers live.

Text 2
A recent survey of vowel pronunciation across several Los Angeles neighborhoods found that residents of predominantly Latino neighborhoods produced certain vowels differently from residents of nearby areas. The researchers recorded short word lists from hundreds of participants and grouped the results by home address. Because the differences lined up so neatly with neighborhood boundaries, the researchers concluded that these vowel patterns express residents' sense of belonging to their local community.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the conclusion reached by the researchers described in Text 2?
options: As premature, because grouping speakers by home address does not show which social relationships the speakers actually participate in
As well supported, because recordings from hundreds of participants make the neighborhood differences statistically reliable
As partly justified, because the vowel differences are real even though the study measured only one type of linguistic feature
As doubtful, because short word lists are too artificial to capture how people speak in everyday conversation
problem.explanation:
정답 A: Text 1 저자는 '말투가 소속감을 반영한다'는 주장은 거주지가 아니라 실제 사회적 관계망 증거가 있을 때만 받아들일 수 있다는 기준을 명시한다. Text 2는 주소로만 묶어 소속감을 결론 내렸으므로, 그 기준에서는 성급한 결론이다.
B: 표본 크기와 깔끔한 일치라는 Text 2 연구자들의 기준으로 평가한 것으로, Text 1 저자는 거주지 기반 증거를 충분하다고 보지 않는다.
C: 두 기준을 섞은 평가. 단일 특징 문제는 Text 1에서 언급되지만 저자의 핵심 수용 조건은 관계망 증거이며, '부분적으로 정당하다'는 결론은 기준과 맞지 않는다.
D: 단어 목록의 인위성이라는 일반적 방법론 상식에 기댄 평가로, Text 1 저자가 제시한 기준이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer A: The author of Text 1 states a clear standard. A claim that speech reflects belonging should be accepted only when it's backed by evidence about speakers' actual social networks, not just by where they live. The Text 2 researchers grouped speakers only by home address and still concluded that the vowel patterns express belonging. By Text 1's standard, that conclusion is premature.
B judges the study by the Text 2 researchers' own standard: a large sample and a neat match with neighborhood boundaries. The author of Text 1 says that evidence based on where people live isn't enough.
C mixes the two standards. Text 1 does mention that Fought didn't rely on a single feature, but the author's actual condition for accepting the claim is network evidence. Text 1 offers no grounds for calling the conclusion "partly justified."
D uses a general methodological point, that word lists are artificial. Text 1 never raises this as its criterion.

hardJudge.note: Text 1 기준("not merely by where those speakers live")이 명시적이고, Text 2 결론은 주소 기반 분류만으로 소속감을 도출하므로 A가 유일하게 Text 1 기준에서 도출된다. B는 Text 2 연구자 기준(표본 수·깔끔한 일치), C는 Text 1의 부수 언급(단일 특징)과 '부분 정당' 강도를 섞은 혼합 오답, D는 외부 방법론 상식. Carmen Fought의 LA Chicano English 연구(사회관계망 활용)는 실제와 부합. 다만 Text 1 기준이 매우 직설적으로 서술되어 있어 hard 상단보다는 하단 수준의 난이도로 보임.

advisory.note: Text 1이 기준('거주지가 아니라 사회적 관계망')을 사실상 그대로 문장으로 밝히고, Text 2는 '주소로 묶음'을 명시하므로 A가 어휘 대응만으로 바로 고정된다. 판정을 위해 추론해야 할 것이 거의 없어 전형적인 medium 수준이다. 오답 C는 단일 특징이라는 Text 1의 부차 요소를 미끼로 쓰지만, 'partly justified'가 기준과 어긋나 쉽게 걸러진다. 정답 근거는 확실하고 형식에도 문제가 없다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Anthropologist Robin Dunbar proposed that humans can maintain only about 150 stable relationships. He based this figure on the size of the brain's neocortex, arguing that our brains limit how many people we can truly keep track of. In his view, this number is fixed by biology for everyone.

Text 2
Some researchers question whether one number applies to all people. When a team of scientists reanalyzed Dunbar's data using different statistical methods, they found estimates ranging from fewer than 20 to more than 500 relationships. They concluded that group size depends heavily on culture, technology, and personal circumstances, not on brain size alone.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Dunbar's view as described in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Anthropologist Robin Dunbar proposed that humans can maintain only about 150 stable relationships. He based this figure on the size of the brain's neocortex, arguing that our brains limit how many people we can truly keep track of. In his view, this number is fixed by biology for everyone.

Text 2
Some researchers question whether one number applies to all people. When a team of scientists reanalyzed Dunbar's data using different statistical methods, they found estimates ranging from fewer than 20 to more than 500 relationships. They concluded that group size depends heavily on culture, technology, and personal circumstances, not on brain size alone.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Dunbar's view as described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that the brain sets a fixed number of relationships, since the reanalysis confirmed a figure close to 150
By disputing the idea that a single number applies to everyone, since estimates vary widely and depend on more than biology
By arguing that the neocortex plays no role at all in human social life, since culture is the only factor that matters
By suggesting that the number 150 is too high, since people can actually maintain fewer than 20 relationships
problem.explanation: Text 1은 150이라는 수치가 생물학적으로 모든 사람에게 고정되어 있다고 주장하고, Text 2는 재분석 결과 추정치가 20 미만에서 500 이상까지 다양하며 문화·기술·개인 상황에 좌우된다고 말하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 150에 가까운 값을 확인했다고 하므로 틀렸다. C는 Text 2가 '뇌 크기만으로는 아니다(not alone)'라고 했을 뿐 뇌의 역할을 완전히 부정하지 않았으므로 과장이다. D는 범위의 한쪽 끝만 골라 하나의 다른 수치를 주장한 것으로, 단일 수치 자체를 의심하는 Text 2의 요지와 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Text 1 says the figure of 150 is fixed by biology for everyone. Text 2 reports estimates from under 20 to over 500 and says group size depends on culture, technology, and circumstances, so B is correct. A is wrong because Text 2 never confirms a figure near 150. C goes too far: Text 2 says "not on brain size alone," which still leaves the brain some role. D picks one end of the range and offers a new single number, but Text 2 questions the idea of any one number.

quality.seed: social science research — Dunbar number 150 cognitive limit and social group size human relationship stability and network constraints

hardJudge.note: Text 2 explicitly questions "whether one number applies to all people" and reports a 20–500+ range tied to culture/technology/circumstances, directly supporting B. A contradicts the reanalysis result, C overstates "not on brain size alone" into total denial, D converts the range's low end into a new single figure—each a typical misreading, none absurd. Korean and English explanations match in conclusion and letter references, with no Korean in the English version. Content reflects Dunbar's neocortex-based claim and the 2021 reanalysis reasonably. Single-step inference with explicit textual cues; suitable for easy.

advisory.note: Text 2의 "Some researchers question whether one number applies to all people"라는 문장 하나로 바로 풀린다. 오답은 각각 전형적 오개념이다: A는 반대 방향, C는 지나친 일반화(not alone을 무시), D는 범위의 한쪽 끝만 고른 경우. A에 대한 한국어 해설은 'A가 ~라고 하므로'로 읽혀 표현이 조금 모호하지만, 뜻은 영어 해설과 같다. 재분석 내용(약 2~520)은 실제 연구 결과와 대체로 맞는다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In her 1983 study of flight attendants, sociologist Arlie Hochschild described "emotional labor": workers are required to display cheerful feelings to customers. Hochschild argued that this constant performance harms workers, leaving many feeling cut off from their own real emotions.

Text 2
Later researchers interviewed customer service workers in several industries. Many reported that emotional labor felt draining when it was strictly scripted by managers. But workers who could choose how to express friendliness often said the work felt meaningful and did not leave them feeling distant from themselves.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Hochschild's argument about the effects of emotional labor, as described in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In her 1983 study of flight attendants, sociologist Arlie Hochschild described "emotional labor": workers are required to display cheerful feelings to customers. Hochschild argued that this constant performance harms workers, leaving many feeling cut off from their own real emotions.

Text 2
Later researchers interviewed customer service workers in several industries. Many reported that emotional labor felt draining when it was strictly scripted by managers. But workers who could choose how to express friendliness often said the work felt meaningful and did not leave them feeling distant from themselves.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Hochschild's argument about the effects of emotional labor, as described in Text 1?
options: By claiming that it is accurate for all customer service workers, whether or not managers script their behavior
By claiming that it is mistaken because flight attendants are not actually required to appear cheerful
By claiming that it applies mainly when workers have little freedom in how they show their feelings
By claiming that it overlooks the fact that emotional labor rarely happens outside the airline industry
problem.explanation: Text 1의 Hochschild는 감정 노동이 노동자를 자기 감정에서 멀어지게 한다고 주장한다. Text 2는 관리자가 엄격히 대본을 정할 때는 소진되지만, 표현 방식을 스스로 고를 수 있으면 의미 있게 느낀다고 보고하므로, 그 주장은 자율성이 적을 때 주로 맞는다는 C가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 대본 없는 노동자에게는 해가 덜하다고 했으므로 틀리다. B는 Text 2가 쾌활함 요구 자체를 부정하지 않으므로 틀리다. D는 Text 2가 여러 산업의 감정 노동을 다루므로 오히려 반대이다.
problem.explanationEn: In Text 1, Hochschild argues that emotional labor harms workers by cutting them off from their real feelings. Text 2 finds that the work feels draining when managers strictly script it, but meaningful when workers choose how to show friendliness, so the author would say Hochschild's claim holds mainly when workers lack freedom, which is C. A is wrong because Text 2 says workers with freedom often were not harmed. B is wrong because Text 2 never denies that cheerfulness is required. D is wrong because Text 2 actually studies emotional labor across several industries.

quality.seed: social science research — Hochschild emotional labor and flight attendants affective performance managing feeling rules in customer service

hardJudge.note: Text 2가 '엄격히 대본화된 경우 소진 / 자율성 있으면 자기와 멀어지지 않음'이라고 명시하므로 C가 직접 뒷받침된다. A(전면 동의), B(전제 부정), D(범위 오류)는 지문과 직접 모순되어 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되며, 전형적 오개념 유형으로 그럴듯하다. Hochschild 1983 The Managed Heart 서술은 사실에 부합. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 지문은 독창적 요약으로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: Text 2는 대본이 정해진 경우를 '소진(draining)'으로만 서술하고 '자기 감정과의 단절'은 선택권이 있는 노동자에 대해서만 부정하지만, 대비 구조가 명확해 C를 추론하는 데 문제는 없다. 오답들은 전형적인 과잉일반화와 사실 왜곡 유형이다.

problem.passage:
In her studies of tailors' apprentices in Liberia, anthropologist Jean Lave observed that novices did not begin by sewing simple practice pieces. Instead, they first performed real tasks near the end of production, such as attaching buttons and hemming finished garments that customers would actually wear, and only later moved back to cutting cloth. Lave argued that this ordering mattered: by starting with finishing work, apprentices repeatedly saw how each step contributed to a completed garment before they attempted the steps on which everything else depended. Some educators have since designed workshops in which beginners practice isolated skills on scrap materials that are discarded afterward. If Lave's account is correct, these workshops are likely to be less effective than Lave's apprenticeships because ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: In her studies of tailors' apprentices in Liberia, anthropologist Jean Lave observed that novices did not begin by sewing simple practice pieces. Instead, they first performed real tasks near the end of production, such as attaching buttons and hemming finished garments that customers would actually wear, and only later moved back to cutting cloth. Lave argued that this ordering mattered: by starting with finishing work, apprentices repeatedly saw how each step contributed to a completed garment before they attempted the steps on which everything else depended. Some educators have since designed workshops in which beginners practice isolated skills on scrap materials that are discarded afterward. If Lave's account is correct, these workshops are likely to be less effective than Lave's apprenticeships because ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: learners practicing on scraps would not see how each skill fits into a finished product that others will use.
learners practicing on scraps would master cutting cloth before they ever learned to attach buttons or hem garments.
learners practicing on scraps would spend less total time on skill practice than apprentices in tailors' shops do.
learners practicing on scraps would receive less direct instruction from experienced tailors than apprentices do.
problem.explanation: Lave은 마무리 작업부터 시작하는 순서 덕분에 도제가 각 단계가 실제로 쓰일 완성품에 어떻게 기여하는지 볼 수 있다고 했으므로, 버려지는 자투리 천으로 고립된 기술을 연습하면 바로 그 이점이 사라진다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 지문의 '순서' 문제를 건드리지만, 워크숍이 재단부터 가르친다는 정보는 지문에 없다. C의 연습 시간과 D의 직접 지도는 그럴듯한 차이처럼 보이지만, 지문에서 Lave이 효과의 원인으로 제시한 것이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: Lave credits the finishing-first order with letting apprentices see how each step contributes to a real garment that customers will wear. Isolated practice on scraps that get thrown away removes exactly that benefit, so A is correct. B picks up on the passage's focus on order, but the passage never says the workshops teach cutting first. C (total practice time) and D (direct instruction) sound like reasonable differences, but Lave doesn't name either one as the reason her apprenticeships work.

quality.seed: social science research — Lave situated learning and apprenticeship community of practice cognitive development in authentic contexts

hardJudge.note: 지문의 핵심 논리(마무리 작업부터 시작 → 각 단계가 실제 사용될 완성품에 기여하는 방식을 봄)와 워크숍의 특징(고립된 기술, 버려지는 자투리)을 연결해야 A가 도출되며, 직접 검산 결과 A가 유일하게 지문에 근거한 완결이다. B는 '순서'라는 지문 요소를 활용하나 워크숍이 재단부터 가르친다는 근거가 없고, D는 도제제도에 숙련 재단사가 있다는 암시를 이용한 그럴듯한 오답, C는 말은 되지만 근거 없음. Jean Lave의 라이베리아 Vai/Gola 재단사 도제 연구(단추 달기·단 처리부터 시작해 재단으로 거슬러 감)와 사실 부합. 한·영 해설 모두 A를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움. 두 단계 추론과 비교 배제가 필요한 표준 medium 수준에 적합.

advisory.note: Lave의 Vai·Gola 재단사 도제 연구(합법적 주변 참여)를 정확히 반영함. 정답 A는 '완성품 기여를 본다'는 근거와 '버려지는 자투리'를 연결해야 하므로 두 단계 판단이 필요함. B는 순서라는 키워드를 이용한 그럴듯한 오답이고, C와 D도 말은 되지만 근거가 없어 medium 수준에 맞음.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Drawing on Etienne Wenger's work, many organizational researchers argue that workplace expertise develops mainly through communities of practice: informal groups whose members share a craft and learn by working alongside one another. On this view, formal training programs add little. Because knowledge lives in the group's everyday conversations and shared problem-solving, these researchers conclude, managers should simply leave such communities alone and let learning emerge on its own.

Text 2
In a two-year study of hospital nursing units, sociologist Hana Okafor found that informal peer networks were indeed where most clinical know-how circulated. Yet the units that learned fastest were not the ones managers ignored. In those units, supervisors set aside protected time for nurses to meet and brought in nurses from other wards to share techniques. Where managers stayed out entirely, the networks often became closed, and new practices spread slowly or not at all.

Based on the texts, how would Okafor (Text 2) most likely respond to the conclusion drawn by the researchers in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Drawing on Etienne Wenger's work, many organizational researchers argue that workplace expertise develops mainly through communities of practice: informal groups whose members share a craft and learn by working alongside one another. On this view, formal training programs add little. Because knowledge lives in the group's everyday conversations and shared problem-solving, these researchers conclude, managers should simply leave such communities alone and let learning emerge on its own.

Text 2
In a two-year study of hospital nursing units, sociologist Hana Okafor found that informal peer networks were indeed where most clinical know-how circulated. Yet the units that learned fastest were not the ones managers ignored. In those units, supervisors set aside protected time for nurses to meet and brought in nurses from other wards to share techniques. Where managers stayed out entirely, the networks often became closed, and new practices spread slowly or not at all.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would Okafor (Text 2) most likely respond to the conclusion drawn by the researchers in Text 1?
options: She would agree that informal peer networks are where expertise mainly develops and would add that managers who step in usually make those networks less effective.
She would accept their view of where expertise mainly develops but would question their claim that managers do best by staying out of such networks.
She would reject their view that informal peer networks matter much and would argue that formal training programs better explain how fast units learn.
She would accept their recommendation about managers but would argue that it applies only to settings outside health care, such as offices.
problem.explanation: Text 2의 Okafor는 비공식 동료 네트워크에서 대부분의 임상 지식이 오간다는 점은 인정하지만, 관리자가 시간을 확보해 주고 다른 병동 간호사를 데려온 병동이 가장 빨리 배웠다고 보고한다. 따라서 지식이 어디서 생기는지에 대한 Text 1의 견해는 받아들이되, '그냥 내버려 두라'는 결론에는 반대할 것이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 앞부분의 동의는 맞지만 관리자 개입이 해롭다는 내용이 연구 결과와 정반대다. C는 Okafor가 네트워크의 중요성을 인정했으므로 틀렸고, 공식 교육은 언급되지도 않는다. D는 관리자에 대한 권고를 받아들인다고 하지만 Okafor는 그 권고를 반박하며, 의료 분야 밖으로 범위를 한정하는 근거도 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Okafor agrees that informal peer networks are where most clinical know-how moves around. But she found that the units that learned fastest had managers who set aside meeting time and brought in nurses from other wards. That means she would accept Text 1's view of where expertise develops and reject its "leave them alone" conclusion, so B is correct. A gets the first half right, but saying that managers who step in make networks worse is the opposite of what she found. C is wrong because she clearly says the networks matter, and she never mentions formal training. D says she accepts the advice about managers, but her study actually argues against that advice, and nothing in her text limits it to settings outside health care.

quality.seed: social science research — Wenger communities of practice and organizational learning distributed knowledge development in social participation networks

hardJudge.note: Text 2 explicitly concedes informal networks carry most know-how ("indeed") yet shows manager involvement sped learning, so B is uniquely correct. A shares the correct first half but inverts the finding; D grabs the manager recommendation but reverses Okafor's stance; C contradicts the concession. Two-step reasoning (identify agreement + identify disagreement) matches medium. Explanations in both languages are consistent, accurate, and reference the correct letters; English has no Korean characters. Wenger/communities of practice is real scholarship, Okafor appears fictional—no factual or copyright issue.

advisory.note: B가 유일한 정답. A는 앞부분만 맞는 부분 정답형 오답으로 잘 만들어졌다. C와 D는 비교적 쉽게 배제되지만 그럴듯하다. 오답 중 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가진 것은 사실상 A 하나라서 medium 기준의 하한에 가깝지만, 두 단계 판단(어디서 배우는가 / 관리자의 역할)이 필요하므로 적합하다.

problem.passage:
From about 650 to 1377, the kingdom of Srivijaya, centered on the island of Sumatra, controlled the Strait of Malacca, a narrow waterway linking the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea. Merchant ships carrying cloves, nutmeg, and other spices had to pass through this strait to reach markets in China and India. ______ Srivijaya was able to collect taxes from a large share of the region's sea trade, and those taxes helped make the kingdom wealthy.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: From about 650 to 1377, the kingdom of Srivijaya, centered on the island of Sumatra, controlled the Strait of Malacca, a narrow waterway linking the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea. Merchant ships carrying cloves, nutmeg, and other spices had to pass through this strait to reach markets in China and India. ______ Srivijaya was able to collect taxes from a large share of the region's sea trade, and those taxes helped make the kingdom wealthy.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 앞 문장들은 스리비자야가 해협을 장악했고 향신료 상선이 반드시 그 해협을 지나야 했다는 원인을 제시한다. 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 결과로 왕국이 해상 무역에 세금을 거둬 부유해졌다는 내용이므로 결과를 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 대조를 나타내지만 두 내용은 서로 반대되지 않는다. B는 예시를 나타내지만 세금 징수는 앞 내용의 한 사례가 아니다. C는 유사한 다른 사례를 덧붙일 때 쓰지만 여기서는 새로운 비교 대상이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The earlier sentences give a cause: Srivijaya controlled the strait, and spice ships had to sail through it. The sentence after the blank gives the effect: the kingdom taxed that trade and became wealthy. That cause-and-effect link calls for D. A signals a contrast, but the two ideas don't conflict. B introduces an example, but collecting taxes isn't an instance of what came before. C signals that something similar is being compared, and nothing is being compared here.

quality.seed: history and civics — Srivijaya maritime Buddhist kingdom 650-1377 and spice trade network controlling Malacca Strait shipping routes

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(해협 장악·상선 통과 필수)이 원인, 빈칸 뒤 문장(세금 징수·부유)이 결과로 명시적 인과 관계이므로 'As a result'가 유일하게 타당함. 오답은 대조·예시·유사 비교라는 전형적 오개념 선택지로 적절. 역사적 사실(스리비자야 약 650–1377, 수마트라, 말라카 해협)도 통설과 일치. 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치.

advisory.note: 명확한 인과 관계 하나로 풀 수 있다. 오답들은 전형적인 연결어 오개념이다. 스리비자야의 연대와 해협 장악은 통설에 부합한다.

problem.passage:
In 1791, enslaved Africans in the French colony of Saint-Domingue rose up against the brutal plantation system. Led by figures such as Toussaint Louverture and later Jean-Jacques Dessalines, they fought for more than a decade and finally defeated the French army in 1803. ______ the colony declared its independence on January 1, 1804, taking the new name Haiti and becoming the first nation in the Americas founded by people who had freed themselves from slavery.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In 1791, enslaved Africans in the French colony of Saint-Domingue rose up against the brutal plantation system. Led by figures such as Toussaint Louverture and later Jean-Jacques Dessalines, they fought for more than a decade and finally defeated the French army in 1803. ______ the colony declared its independence on January 1, 1804, taking the new name Haiti and becoming the first nation in the Americas founded by people who had freed themselves from slavery.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 반란군이 1803년에 프랑스군을 물리쳤다는 원인을, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 결과로 1804년에 독립을 선언했다는 내용을 제시하므로 결과를 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A는 대조를 나타내지만 승리와 독립 선언은 서로 반대되는 내용이 아니다. C는 예시를 나타내지만 독립 선언은 프랑스군 격파의 한 사례가 아니다. D는 유사성을 나타내지만 두 문장은 비슷한 사건을 나란히 놓은 것이 아니라 원인과 결과로 이어진다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the blank gives a cause: the rebels defeated the French army in 1803. The sentence after it gives what followed from that victory: the colony declared independence in 1804. So B, which signals a result, is correct. A signals contrast, but winning the war and declaring independence don't oppose each other. C signals an example, but the declaration isn't one instance of defeating the French. D signals similarity, but the two sentences are connected as cause and effect, not as two similar events.

quality.seed: history and civics — Haitian Revolution 1791-1804 and enslaved African uprising overthrowing French colonial rule establishing independent nation

hardJudge.note: 원인(1803년 프랑스군 격파)→결과(1804년 독립 선언) 관계가 지문에 명시적으로 드러나 'As a result'가 유일하게 성립. 역사적 사실(1791 봉기, 루베르튀르·데살린, 1803 승리, 1804.1.1 독립, 아이티 명칭) 모두 정확. 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 오답은 대조·예시·유사의 전형적 오개념형. 난이도 easy 적합.

advisory.note: 역사적 사실 정확(1791 봉기, 1803 프랑스군 패배, 1804.1.1 독립 선언). 인과관계 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나 있어 easy 수준에 맞음. 사소한 점: 빈칸이 문장 맨 앞에 있는데 뒤 단어 'the'가 소문자라 대문자 표기가 어색하지만 SAT 형식상 흔히 쓰이는 방식임.

problem.passage:
Before 1868, Japanese society was organized around a rigid feudal order in which samurai held special privileges and peasants were bound to the land. After the Meiji Restoration, however, the new government moved quickly to ______ this old system: it abolished the samurai class's right to carry swords, replaced feudal domains with prefectures run by the central state, and built a national army drawn from ordinary citizens.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Before 1868, Japanese society was organized around a rigid feudal order in which samurai held special privileges and peasants were bound to the land. After the Meiji Restoration, however, the new government moved quickly to ______ this old system: it abolished the samurai class's right to carry swords, replaced feudal domains with prefectures run by the central state, and built a national army drawn from ordinary citizens.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 정부가 사무라이의 특권을 폐지하고, 봉건 영지를 현으로 바꾸고, 일반 시민으로 군대를 만들었다고 설명하므로 옛 봉건 체제를 해체했다는 뜻의 C가 정답이다. A는 '보존하다'라는 뜻이어서 제도를 폐지하고 교체했다는 내용과 정반대이다. B는 '기념하다'라는 뜻인데, 지문은 옛 체제를 기리는 것이 아니라 없앤 과정을 다룬다. D는 '모방하다'라는 뜻이지만, 정부는 옛 체제를 따라 한 것이 아니라 새로운 제도로 대체했다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the government abolished samurai privileges, replaced feudal domains with prefectures, and built an army of ordinary citizens, so it was taking the old system apart. That makes C the correct answer. A means to keep something as it is, which is the opposite of abolishing and replacing it. B means to honor the system, but the text describes ending it, not praising it. D means to copy the system, yet the government replaced it with new institutions instead of copying it.

quality.seed: history and civics — Meiji Restoration 1868 and rapid Japanese industrialization modernizing military institutions transforming feudal society

hardJudge.note: 정답 C 검증: 콜론 뒤에 '폐지(abolished)', '대체(replaced)', '시민군 창설'이라는 직접 단서가 나열되어 '해체하다(dismantle)'가 유일하게 논리적으로 맞음. A(보존)는 정반대, B(기념)·D(모방)는 문맥 불일치로 규칙(콜론 뒤 구체화가 빈칸 의미를 결정)을 알면 즉시 배제 가능하되, 'old system'이라는 어구 때문에 역사 맥락을 대충 읽는 학생에게는 그럴듯함. 역사적 사실(1876 폐도령, 1871 폐번치현, 1873 징병령) 모두 정확. 한국어·영어 해설은 동일 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 한글 혼입 없음. 단서가 명시적이고 어휘가 평이하여 easy 난이도에 적합.

advisory.note: 역사 사실(1871 폐번치현, 1873 징병령, 1876 폐도령)이 정확함. 콜론 뒤에 '폐지·대체'라는 단서가 바로 나와 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. preserve는 반의어 오답으로 그럴듯하고, celebrate와 imitate는 다소 약하지만 허용할 수준이다.

problem.passage:
Before 1833, many British textile mills employed young children for twelve hours a day or more. The Factory Act of that year changed this by setting clear limits: children aged nine to thirteen could work no more than nine hours a day, and factory inspectors were hired to make sure mill owners followed the rules. Later Factory Acts, passed between 1844 and 1901, continued to ______ the hours that children were allowed to work, reducing them step by step.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Before 1833, many British textile mills employed young children for twelve hours a day or more. The Factory Act of that year changed this by setting clear limits: children aged nine to thirteen could work no more than nine hours a day, and factory inspectors were hired to make sure mill owners followed the rules. Later Factory Acts, passed between 1844 and 1901, continued to ______ the hours that children were allowed to work, reducing them step by step.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 1833년 법이 아동 노동 시간에 '제한'을 두었고, 이후 법들도 시간을 '단계적으로 줄였다(reducing them step by step)'고 말하므로 빈칸에는 '제한하다'라는 뜻의 D가 와야 한다. A는 '늘리다'로 시간을 줄였다는 단서와 정반대이다. B는 '기념하다'로 법이 노동 시간에 하는 작용을 나타내지 못한다. C는 '무시하다'로 감독관까지 두어 규칙을 시행했다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the 1833 Act set limits on children's working hours and that later Acts kept "reducing them step by step," so the blank needs a word meaning "limit," which is D. A means "lengthen," the opposite of reducing hours. B means "honor," which doesn't describe what a law does to working hours. C means "pay no attention to," which clashes with laws that hired inspectors to enforce the rules.

quality.seed: history and civics — British Factory Acts labor legislation 1833-1901 and child worker protection regulations limiting working hours

hardJudge.note: "continued to ___ the hours ... reducing them step by step"에서 'restrict'가 유일하게 논리적으로 성립. A는 반대어, B·C는 문맥상 배제되며 전형적 오개념 수준의 그럴듯함을 갖춤. 1833 Factory Act 내용(9~13세 하루 9시간, 감독관 임명)은 역사적 사실과 일치. 해설 양쪽 모두 D를 정답으로 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 단일 단서·한 단계 추론으로 easy 적합.

advisory.note: 'reducing them step by step'라는 단서가 지문에 바로 나와 있어서 restrict가 정답임을 한 번만 추론하면 알 수 있다. 1833년 공장법 관련 사실(9~13세 아동 하루 9시간 제한, 감독관 임명)도 맞다. B(celebrate)는 오답으로서 다소 약하지만 easy 수준에서는 허용할 만하다.

problem.passage:
In 1861, President Abraham Lincoln ordered a naval blockade of Southern ports, hoping to cut the Confederacy off from foreign trade. At first, the Union navy had too few ships to watch thousands of miles of coastline. By 1864, however, the fleet of patrolling vessels ______ grown to several hundred, and fewer and fewer Confederate blockade runners managed to slip through with cotton and supplies.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In 1861, President Abraham Lincoln ordered a naval blockade of Southern ports, hoping to cut the Confederacy off from foreign trade. At first, the Union navy had too few ships to watch thousands of miles of coastline. By 1864, however, the fleet of patrolling vessels ______ grown to several hundred, and fewer and fewer Confederate blockade runners managed to slip through with cotton and supplies.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 문장은 "By 1864"라는 과거 시점과 과거형 동사 "managed"를 쓰고 있으므로, 그 시점 이전에 완료된 일을 나타내는 과거완료 "had"가 맞습니다. 따라서 A가 정답입니다. B는 "vessels"를 주어로 착각한 복수 현재완료이고, 시제도 과거 맥락과 맞지 않습니다. C는 주어 "fleet"와 수는 일치하지만 현재완료라서 과거 시점과 맞지 않습니다. D는 진행형이라 시제가 틀리고, 뒤의 "grown"과도 문법적으로 결합할 수 없습니다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence is set in the past, marked by "By 1864" and the past-tense verb "managed," so you need the past perfect "had" to show something finished before that past moment. That makes A correct. B treats "vessels" as the subject and uses the present perfect, which clashes with the past setting. C agrees with the singular subject "fleet," but the present perfect still doesn't fit a past time frame. D is a progressive form in the wrong tense, and it can't combine grammatically with "grown."

quality.seed: history and civics — American Civil War blockade strategy 1861-1865 and naval enforcement strangling Confederate supply lines economy

hardJudge.note: "By 1864" + 과거형 "managed" 맥락에서 과거완료 "had grown"이 유일하게 적합. 오답은 수일치·시제 오개념 기반으로 그럴듯함. 역사적 사실(1861 봉쇄령, 함대 규모 증가)도 문제 없음. 해설 한·영 일치, 선택지 참조 정확.

advisory.note: 시제(과거완료)와 주어-동사 수일치(fleet 단수, 수식어구 vessels가 함정)를 묻는 문항으로 easy 수준에 맞음. 사실관계(1861년 봉쇄령, 1864년 함대 수백 척 규모)도 정확함.

problem.passage:
Between November 1884 and February 1885, representatives of fourteen nations met in Berlin to set rules for claiming territory in Africa. The delegates at the conference ______ no African leaders to the talks, so decisions that shaped the lives of millions of people were made without their input.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Between November 1884 and February 1885, representatives of fourteen nations met in Berlin to set rules for claiming territory in Africa. The delegates at the conference ______ no African leaders to the talks, so decisions that shaped the lives of millions of people were made without their input.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 지문은 1884~1885년에 있었던 과거의 사건을 다루며, 'met', 'were made' 같은 과거 시제 동사를 쓴다. 따라서 빈칸에도 과거 시제인 B가 와야 시제가 일관된다. A는 현재 시제라서 과거 사건과 맞지 않는다. C는 현재완료 시제로, 현재와 이어지는 의미를 주기 때문에 끝난 역사적 사건에는 어색하다. D는 미래 시제라서 이미 일어난 일을 설명하는 문장에 쓸 수 없다.
problem.explanationEn: This passage describes events from 1884–1885, and it uses past tense verbs like "met" and "were made." So the blank needs the past tense, B, to keep the tenses consistent. A is present tense, which doesn't fit a past event. C is present perfect, which connects the action to the present, so it sounds wrong for a finished historical event. D is future tense, and you can't use it for something that already happened.

quality.seed: history and civics — Berlin Conference 1884-1885 and European imperial powers partitioning African continent without African representation

hardJudge.note: 지문의 'met', 'were made'와 1884~1885 날짜가 과거 시제를 명시적으로 요구하므로 B 'invited'가 정답. 오답 A(현재), C(현재완료), D(미래)는 시제 일관성 규칙 하나로 즉시 배제되며, 전형적 오개념(현재완료로 역사 서술)으로 그럴듯함. 한·영 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 베를린 회의 관련 사실(14개국, 아프리카 지도자 미초청) 정확. 지문은 독자 작성으로 보이며 저작권 우려 없음. easy 난이도 적합.

advisory.note: 베를린 회의(1884-85, 14개국 참가, 아프리카 대표 불참)라는 사실이 정확함. 단서는 시제 일관성 하나로 easy 수준에 맞음.

problem.passage:
In October 1917, the Bolsheviks, led by Vladimir Lenin, seized power in Petrograd. The tsar had already given up the throne earlier that year, and the Bolsheviks now overthrew the Provisional Government that had replaced him. Their victory led to the first Soviet communist state. Today, a collection of telegrams and decrees from those weeks ______ historians a detailed record of how the new state took shape.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In October 1917, the Bolsheviks, led by Vladimir Lenin, seized power in Petrograd. The tsar had already given up the throne earlier that year, and the Bolsheviks now overthrew the Provisional Government that had replaced him. Their victory led to the first Soviet communist state. Today, a collection of telegrams and decrees from those weeks ______ historians a detailed record of how the new state took shape.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'a collection'이며, 'of telegrams and decrees from those weeks'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 동사가 필요하고, 'Today'와도 맞는 현재 시제 단수 동사인 C가 정답이다. A, B, D는 모두 복수 동사(give, are giving, have given)여서 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'weeks'나 'decrees'를 주어로 잘못 본 선택지이다. 수식어를 지우고 'a collection ___ historians'로 읽으면 단수 동사가 필요하다는 것을 쉽게 알 수 있다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "a collection." The phrase "of telegrams and decrees from those weeks" only describes the subject. So the verb has to be singular, and C, a singular present-tense verb that also fits "Today," is the correct answer. A, B, and D are all plural verbs ("give," "are giving," "have given"). They could only be right if the subject were a plural noun near the blank, like "weeks" or "decrees," but neither of those is the subject. If you drop the modifying phrase and read "a collection ___ historians," it's easy to see that you need a singular verb.

quality.seed: history and civics — Russian Revolution October 1917 and Bolshevik overthrow of Tsarist autocracy establishing Soviet communist state

hardJudge.note: 주어 'a collection'(단수)에 맞는 단수 현재형 동사 'gives'(C)가 유일하게 적합. A·B·D는 모두 복수형으로, 바로 앞 복수 명사(weeks/decrees)에 끌리는 전형적 오개념 선택지 — 단일 규칙(주어-동사 수일치, 수식어 무시)만으로 풀리므로 easy 적합. 역사적 사실(1917년 10월 볼셰비키 집권, 황제 퇴위, 임시정부 전복)도 정확. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 주어-동사 수일치 단일 규칙 문항이다. 역사적 사실(1917년 10월 페트로그라드, 2월 차르 퇴위, 임시정부 전복)에는 오류가 없다. 오답은 모두 근접 복수명사로 인한 전형적 오개념이다.

problem.passage:
After 1492, ships crossing the Atlantic carried not only people but also plants, animals, and germs between the Americas and the rest of the world. Historians call this movement the Columbian Exchange. One historian argues that crops from the Americas, especially the potato, helped populations in parts of Europe grow during the 1600s and 1700s. According to this view, the potato gave farmers a dependable, high-calorie food that grew well in cool, wet soil where wheat and other grains often failed.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historian's claim?
problem.stimulus: After 1492, ships crossing the Atlantic carried not only people but also plants, animals, and germs between the Americas and the rest of the world. Historians call this movement the Columbian Exchange. One historian argues that crops from the Americas, especially the potato, helped populations in parts of Europe grow during the 1600s and 1700s. According to this view, the potato gave farmers a dependable, high-calorie food that grew well in cool, wet soil where wheat and other grains often failed.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historian's claim?
options: European regions that took up potato farming early grew in population faster than similar regions that took it up later.
European regions that took up potato farming early sent more ships across the Atlantic than regions that took it up later.
European regions that took up potato farming early were the first to plant American crops such as tomatoes for decoration.
European regions that took up potato farming early had grown wheat for many centuries before 1492.
problem.explanation: 이 주장은 감자가 유럽의 인구 증가를 도왔다는 것이므로, 이를 뒷받침하려면 감자 재배와 인구 증가를 직접 연결하는 증거가 필요하다. A는 감자를 일찍 받아들인 지역이 비슷한 다른 지역보다 인구가 더 빨리 늘었다고 하므로 이 연결을 바로 보여 준다. B는 항해 횟수에 관한 내용이라 인구와는 상관이 없다. C는 장식용 작물 이야기라 식량이나 인구와 관련이 없다. D는 1492년 이전의 밀 재배에 관한 내용일 뿐, 감자가 인구에 미친 영향은 전혀 말해 주지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The historian claims that the potato helped European populations grow, so the evidence you need has to link potato farming directly to population growth. Choice A does exactly that: regions that adopted the potato early grew faster than similar regions that adopted it later. Choice B is about how many ships sailed, which says nothing about population. Choice C is about plants grown for decoration, which has nothing to do with food or population. Choice D only tells you about wheat farming before 1492 and says nothing about the potato's effect on population.

quality.seed: history and civics — Columbian Exchange 1492-1650 and transatlantic transfer of crops diseases animals reshaping Old World New World

hardJudge.note: 정답 A가 감자 재배(원인)와 인구 증가(결과)를 비슷한 지역 간 비교로 직접 연결하여 주장을 가장 직접적으로 뒷받침함. B(항해 횟수), C(장식용 작물), D(1492년 이전 밀 재배)는 인구 변화와 무관하여 배제됨. 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 지문은 일반적 역사 지식 기반의 자작 문장으로 저작권 우려 없음. 단일 규칙(주장의 두 변수 연결 증거 찾기)으로 풀리고 단서가 명시적이므로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 감자 도입과 인구 증가를 비교 집단으로 연결하므로 명확하다. 오답 B·C·D는 같은 주제(대서양 교류, 아메리카 작물, 곡물 재배)에 걸쳐 있어 그럴듯해 보이지만 인구와 연결되지 않아 바로 배제된다. easy 난이도에 맞다. 역사적 내용(Nunn & Qian 등의 감자-인구 가설)도 사실에 부합한다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- Under the millet system, each officially recognized religious community was organized as a separate group called a millet.
- Each millet could use its own religious law for matters such as marriage, divorce, and inheritance.

problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Ottoman Empire ruled a population that included Muslims, Christians, and Jews.
- Under the millet system, each officially recognized religious community was organized as a separate group called a millet.
- Each millet could use its own religious law for matters such as marriage, divorce, and inheritance.
- Religious leaders, such as the Greek Orthodox patriarch, represented their millets before the Ottoman government.
- Members of non-Muslim millets paid a special tax to the state.
problem.question: The student wants to explain what kind of independence a religious community had in its family affairs. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Under the millet system, members of non-Muslim millets paid a special tax to the Ottoman state.
Under the millet system, each millet could follow its own religious law on marriage, divorce, and inheritance.
Under the millet system, leaders such as the Greek Orthodox patriarch spoke for their millets before the government.
Under the millet system, the Ottoman Empire ruled a population of Muslims, Christians, and Jews.
problem.explanation: 목표는 종교 공동체가 가족 문제에서 가졌던 자율성을 설명하는 것이다. B는 각 밀레트가 결혼·이혼·상속에 자신의 종교법을 적용할 수 있었다는 메모를 사용하므로 목표에 정확히 맞는다. A는 세금에 관한 내용으로, 자율이 아니라 국가에 대한 의무를 다룬다. C는 지도자의 대표 역할을 말할 뿐 가족 문제를 언급하지 않는다. D는 제국 인구의 구성만 소개한다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to explain the independence a religious community had in family affairs. B does this by using the note that each millet could apply its own religious law to marriage, divorce, and inheritance. A is about a tax, which is a duty owed to the state, not a form of independence. C describes leaders representing their communities, but it says nothing about family matters. D only describes who lived in the empire.

quality.seed: history and civics — Ottoman millet system religious communities and legal autonomy within Islamic imperial administrative structure

hardJudge.note: 목표(가족 문제에서의 자율성)와 메모 3(결혼·이혼·상속에 자체 종교법 적용)이 직접 대응하여 B가 유일한 정답. A(세금 의무), C(대표 역할), D(인구 구성)는 모두 메모에 근거하나 목표와 무관한 전형적 오답. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 밀레트 제도에 관한 역사적 서술도 정확. 단일 규칙·한 단계 대응으로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 목표의 '가족 문제'와 결혼·이혼·상속이 바로 대응되어 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. C(대표 역할)는 자율성처럼 보여서 그럴듯한 오답이다. 역사적 내용도 정확하다.

- His fleet, often called the treasure fleet, included hundreds of ships and thousands of sailors.

problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Zheng He was an admiral who served the Yongle Emperor of China's Ming dynasty.
- Between 1405 and 1433, he led seven naval expeditions across the Indian Ocean.
- His fleet, often called the treasure fleet, included hundreds of ships and thousands of sailors.
- The voyages reached ports in Southeast Asia, India, the Arabian Peninsula, and East Africa.
- After the final voyage, the Ming court stopped sponsoring such long-distance expeditions.
problem.question: The student wants to tell readers how far Zheng He's fleet traveled. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Zheng He's fleet, known as the treasure fleet, included hundreds of ships and thousands of sailors.
Zheng He's fleet sailed for the Yongle Emperor, who ruled China during the Ming dynasty.
Zheng He's fleet visited ports as distant as the Arabian Peninsula and East Africa.
Zheng He's fleet made its last voyage in 1433, after which the Ming court stopped funding such trips.
problem.explanation: 목표는 함대가 얼마나 멀리 갔는지, 즉 항해 범위를 보여 주는 것이다. C는 아라비아반도와 동아프리카라는 도착지를 제시해 항해 거리를 직접 보여 준다. A는 함대의 규모만 말할 뿐 거리를 말하지 않는다. B는 함대를 후원한 황제에 관한 정보이고, D는 항해가 언제 끝났는지만 설명하므로 둘 다 목표와 관계없다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to show how far the fleet traveled, so the right choice has to describe where the voyages went. C does this by naming places as far away as the Arabian Peninsula and East Africa. A tells you how big the fleet was, not how far it sailed. B is about the emperor who sponsored the fleet, and D only says when the voyages ended, so neither one shows distance.

quality.seed: history and civics — Ming Dynasty Zheng He voyages 1405-1433 and Chinese treasure fleet naval expeditions across Indian Ocean

hardJudge.note: 정답 C는 노트의 도착지(아라비아반도·동아프리카)를 활용해 항해 범위를 직접 전달하므로 목표에 부합. A(규모), B(후원자), D(종료 시점)는 노트에 근거한 사실이지만 목표와 무관한 전형적 오답. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 역사적 사실(1405~1433, 7차 원정, 영락제)도 정확. easy 난이도에 적합.

advisory.note: 목표(거리)와 직접 대응하는 선택지는 C 하나뿐이다. 오답 A(규모), B(후원자), D(종료 시점)는 노트에 실린 사실이라 그럴듯해 보이지만 목표와 맞지 않는 전형적인 오답이다. 쉬운 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
The Treaty of Nanjing, signed in 1842 after British naval forces had overwhelmed the Qing dynasty's coastal defenses during the First Opium War, ______ five Chinese ports to British merchants and ceded Hong Kong Island to the British Crown, terms that many historians later grouped among the so-called unequal treaties.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: The Treaty of Nanjing, signed in 1842 after British naval forces had overwhelmed the Qing dynasty's coastal defenses during the First Opium War, ______ five Chinese ports to British merchants and ceded Hong Kong Island to the British Crown, terms that many historians later grouped among the so-called unequal treaties.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The Treaty of Nanjing'이고, 그 뒤의 'signed in 1842 ... Opium War'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어구일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 정동사가 와야 하며, 이 동사는 'and ceded'와 병렬을 이루는 과거 시제여야 하므로 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'defenses'나 'forces'와 수를 맞춘 복수형이라 단수 주어와 일치하지 않고, B는 'ceded'와 시제도 맞지 않는다. D는 분사라서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The Treaty of Nanjing." The phrase "signed in 1842 ... Opium War" just modifies that subject. So the blank needs a finite verb, and that verb has to be in the past tense to stay parallel with "and ceded." That makes C correct. A and B are plural forms that match the nearby plural nouns "defenses" or "forces," so they don't agree with the singular subject, and B also doesn't match the tense of "ceded." D is a participle, which would leave the sentence with no finite verb.

quality.seed: history and civics — Qing Dynasty Opium Wars 1839-1860 and British forced trade imposing unequal treaties on China

hardJudge.note: 주어 'The Treaty of Nanjing'(단수)과 긴 분사 수식어구 뒤에서 정동사가 필요하며, 'and ceded'와 병렬인 과거형 'opened'(C)가 유일하게 적합. A·B는 인접 복수 명사(forces/defenses)에 끌리는 오답, D는 정동사 부재. 역사적 사실(1842년, 5개 개항장, 홍콩섬 할양, 불평등 조약) 정확. 한국어·영어 해설 결론과 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 주어 식별+시제 병렬의 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 긴 수식어구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어 수 일치와 시제를 함께 따져야 함. 병렬 구조 ceded도 단서가 되어 medium에 적합.

problem.stimulus: The League of Nations, established in 1920 under the peace settlement that ended the First World War and joined by more than forty founding member states, ______ to settle disputes between countries through arbitration and collective negotiation rather than armed conflict. problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The League of Nations'이고, 'established ... and joined by ... states'는 삽입된 분사 수식어구이므로 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하다. Choice D, "sought," is a past-tense finite verb that completes the sentence, and it fits the past time frame of the next sentence. hardJudge.note: 주어 'The League of Nations'(단수) + 긴 삽입 분사구 뒤에 정동사 필요. D 'sought'만 단수 일치 정동사. A·C는 분사로 문장 미완성, B는 인접 'states'에 이끌린 복수 동사로 오답. 한·영 해설 결론과 글자 참조 일치, 영문 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 1920년 설립·40여 창립국 등 사실 정확. 정동사 판별+삽입구 건너뛴 수일치의 두 단계 판단으로 medium 적합.

problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

Choices A and D are participles, so with either one the sentence has no main verb and becomes a fragment. Choice C is a finite verb, but it is plural. hardJudge.note: 주어 'The Magna Carta'(단수) 뒤 긴 동격어구 'a charter ... Runnymede'를 지나 정동사가 필요하며, B 'established'가 유일한 단수 정동사로 정답 확인. A/D는 분사형(문장 조각), C는 복수 정동사(수 일치 오류). 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조로 일관되고 영어 자연스러움. 역사적 사실(1215년 러니미드, 존 왕, 반란 귀족) 정확. 긴 동격어구 넘어 주어 식별 + 정동사/수 일치 판단의 두 단계 요구로 medium 적합.

problem.explanationEn: The subject of the sentence is "The General Act," and the clause "which required ... coastal regions" is just a modifier set off by commas, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with that singular subject. Choice C, the past-tense "accelerated," works with a singular subject and fits a passage about events in the 1880s, so it is the correct answer. Choice A is a participle, which leaves the sentence with no main verb. Choice B is a finite verb, but it is plural, matching the nearby nouns "states" and "regions" instead of the singular subject "Act." Choice D adds "which," turning the verb into another modifying clause, so the sentence still has no main verb.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The General Act"(단수) 뒤에 긴 삽입 관계절("which required ... coastal regions")이 오고, 빈칸은 주절의 정동사 자리. C "accelerated"만 단수 주어와 호응하는 정동사. A(분사)·D(관계절)는 정동사 부재로 문장 조각, B는 인접 복수 명사(states/regions)에 끌린 복수형이라 Act와 불일치. 역사적 사실(1884–85, 14개국·아프리카 불참, 실효적 점유 원칙의 연안 적용)도 정확. 삽입절 길이와 B의 근접 명사 유인, D의 관계사 유인이 있어 medium에 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 선택지 참조 및 결론 일치, 한글 혼입 없음.

advisory.note: 주어와 동사 사이에 긴 삽입절이 있어 주어-동사 일치와 정동사 여부를 함께 판단해야 하므로 medium에 맞다. 실효 점유 원칙은 해안 지역에 적용되었다는 서술도 사실과 대체로 일치한다.

problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 주절의 주어는 단수 명사 'the reaction'이고, 'from Washington and Moscow'는 그 주어를 꾸미는 전치사구일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 정동사가 필요하므로 A의 'was'가 정답이다. B의 'were'는 바로 앞의 복수처럼 보이는 'Washington and Moscow'에 맞춘 것이어서 주어-동사 수 일치가 틀린다. C의 'being'과 D의 'having been'은 분사라서 정동사가 아니므로, 콜론 앞의 절이 동사 없는 불완전한 절이 된다.

advisory.note: 수식어구 속 복수처럼 보이는 명사(Washington and Moscow)로 수 일치를 헷갈리게 하는 전형적인 중간 난이도 문항이다. C와 D는 비정동사라 배제하기 쉽지만 문장 흐름상 말이 된다. 역사적 사실(1956년 7월 국유화 발표, 가을 침공, 미국과 소련의 압력, 철수)도 정확하다.

A and D are finite verbs, but they're plural forms that match the nearby plural nouns "officials" or "Red Guards," so they don't agree with "assault." hardJudge.note: 주어 'assault'(단수) + 긴 삽입구('on senior party officials, many of whom ... Red Guards') 뒤 정동사 필요. C 'weakened'만 단수 주어와 일치하는 과거 정동사. problem.explanationEn: The previous sentence describes the revolt's quick failure—Tyler was killed and the king took back his charters—while the next sentence says the rebels' main goal was achieved anyway, so D, which signals a contrast after a concession, is correct. problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 둘째 문장은 왕실이 파리의 소수 지도자 살해를 명령했다는 점을 인정하고(양보), 셋째 문장은 지방으로 번진 대규모 학살이 왕의 명령 없이 지역 민병대에 의해 이루어졌다고 말해 '계획된 왕실 음모'라는 통념을 반박한다. 따라서 양보 뒤에 반전을 표시하는 B가 정답이다. A는 파리 명령이 지방 폭력을 촉발했다는 인과로 읽힐 수 있지만, 셋째 문장의 핵심은 왕의 지시가 없었다는 대비이므로 결과 관계가 아니다. C는 두 사건이 모두 학살이라는 점에서 유사해 보이지만, 지문은 명령 유무를 대조하고 있다. D는 앞 내용을 강화하는 표현인데, 셋째 문장은 왕실 음모설을 강화하지 않고 오히려 그 범위를 제한한다.
problem.explanationEn: The second sentence concedes that the crown did order the killing of a few Huguenot leaders in Paris. The third sentence then turns against the old "royal plot" view: it says the larger killings in other cities happened without written orders from the king. A concession followed by a reversal calls for a contrast, so B is correct. A might look logical, since the Paris killings could have set off violence elsewhere, but the third sentence is stressing the lack of royal orders, not describing a result. C and D don't fit either. C points to a similarity, but the text contrasts ordered and unordered violence. D would strengthen the idea of a royal plot, while the third sentence actually narrows it.

problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 이미 독립을 선포한 아기날도 세력이 미국의 통치를 전혀 다르게 받아들였다는 내용이고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 결과로 1899년 전쟁이 발발했다는 내용이므로 인과 관계를 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A might look tempting because the passage as a whole does contrast American expectations with what actually happened. However, the sentence right before the blank is about Filipino opposition, and the outbreak of fighting follows from that opposition instead of contradicting it. B treats the war as an example of the Filipino view, but the war was a result of that view, not an illustration of it. C would add a similar point, but the final sentence describes a new event that grew out of the earlier one, not a parallel case.

hardJudge.note: 직접 검산: 빈칸 앞 문장(아기날도 세력의 반대) → 뒤 문장(1899년 전쟁 발발)은 인과 관계이므로 D 'Consequently'가 타당. A는 두 문장 앞의 미국 측 기대와의 대비로 읽힐 수 있어 매력적인 오답이지만, 직전 문장과는 대립하지 않음. B(예시), C(유사 추가)는 관계 불일치. 사실 확인: 1898 파리조약, 1898.6 독립 선언, 1899.2.4 교전 개시, 1902 공식 종전, 민간인 사망 수십만 명 추정 — 모두 역사적 사실과 부합. 한국어·영어 해설 결론과 선택지 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 오답 A·B가 부분적 근거를 가져 비교 필요, C도 말이 되므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 사실관계 확인 완료: 독립 선포는 1898년 6월, 'benevolent assimilation'은 1898년 12월 매킨리 선언, 개전은 1899년 2월, 공식 종전은 1902년, 민간인 사망자 수십만 명. 모두 맞다. A(Nevertheless)는 지문 전체의 '기대와 현실' 대비 때문에 그럴듯한 오답이고, 정답을 고르려면 빈칸 바로 앞 문장과의 관계를 확인해야 하므로 medium 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
In 1899 and 1900, a severe drought struck northern China's Shandong and Zhili provinces, leaving many farmers without work or food. Rumors spread through the villages that foreign missionaries and Chinese Christian converts had angered local gods by rejecting traditional rituals, and that this was why the rains had stopped. ______ the Boxers, a loosely organized movement that claimed its martial-arts training made members immune to bullets, found eager recruits among idle young villagers that spring, and its attacks on mission stations spread quickly toward Beijing.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In 1899 and 1900, a severe drought struck northern China's Shandong and Zhili provinces, leaving many farmers without work or food. Rumors spread through the villages that foreign missionaries and Chinese Christian converts had angered local gods by rejecting traditional rituals, and that this was why the rains had stopped. ______ the Boxers, a loosely organized movement that claimed its martial-arts training made members immune to bullets, found eager recruits among idle young villagers that spring, and its attacks on mission stations spread quickly toward Beijing.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 앞 문장들은 가뭄으로 일이 없고 굶주린 농민들, 그리고 가뭄을 선교사 탓으로 돌리는 소문이라는 원인을 제시한다. 빈칸 뒤 문장은 의화단이 한가한 젊은 농민들 사이에서 신병을 쉽게 모은 결과를 서술하므로 인과를 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 역접이지만, 가뭄과 반외세 소문은 모집을 막는 조건이 아니라 오히려 모집을 부추긴 조건이다. C는 뒤 문장이 앞 내용을 구체화한다고 보지만, 의화단 모집은 소문을 자세히 풀어 설명하는 것이 아니라 소문이 낳은 새로운 사건이다. D는 비슷한 사례를 나란히 놓는 표현인데, 뒤 문장은 앞의 내용과 평행한 사례가 아니라 그로 인한 결과다.
problem.explanationEn: The earlier sentences give the causes: drought left farmers idle and hungry, and rumors blamed missionaries and converts for the missing rain. The sentence after the blank describes what followed: the Boxers easily recruited idle young villagers. That cause-and-effect relationship makes A correct. B signals contrast, but the hardship and anti-foreign rumors encouraged recruitment rather than working against it. C would mean the next sentence adds detail to the rumors, but the Boxers' recruitment is a new event caused by those conditions, not a closer explanation of them. D sets up a parallel example, yet the final sentence is a result of the earlier conditions, not a similar case.

quality.seed: history and civics — Boxer Rebellion 1900 China and anti-foreign peasant uprising against Western imperial missionary influence

hardJudge.note: 정답 검산: 앞 문장(가뭄→실업·기근, 선교사 탓 소문)이 원인, 빈칸 뒤(의화단이 한가한 젊은 농민을 쉽게 모집, 선교 거점 공격 확산)가 결과이므로 Consequently가 유일하게 성립. Nevertheless는 역접 관계 없음, Specifically는 소문의 세부 설명이 아님, Similarly는 평행 사례 아님. 역사적 사실(1899–1900 산둥·즈리 가뭄, 의화단의 총알 불사 주장, 반기독교 공격의 베이징 확산) 모두 정확. 해설 한·영 결론과 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 난이도: 원인 문장이 두 개(가뭄+소문)이고 결과 문장이 길어 연결을 확인해야 하며, C·D가 '뒤 문장이 앞 내용을 상술/병렬한다'는 표면적 유혹을 가져 medium에 적합. 다만 인과 신호가 비교적 뚜렷해 medium 하한에 가까움.

advisory.note: 인과 관계가 너무 분명하게 드러난다(가뭄+소문 → 실직한 젊은 농민 모집). 오답 중 'Specifically'만 조금 헷갈릴 여지가 있고, 'Nevertheless'와 'Similarly'는 바로 배제된다. 따라서 '오답 중 최소 2개가 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져야 한다'는 medium 기준에 못 미친다. 역사 사실(1899–1900년 산둥·즈리 가뭄, 의화단의 총탄을 막는다는 주장)은 정확하다.

problem.passage:
In 1915 and 1916, British officials exchanged letters with Sharif Hussein of Mecca, suggesting that Britain would support an independent Arab state if he led a revolt against the Ottoman Empire. At the same time, British diplomat Mark Sykes and French diplomat François Georges-Picot secretly agreed to divide much of that same territory into British and French zones of control. After seizing power in Russia in 1917, the Bolsheviks published the secret agreement to expose the wartime deals of the Allied powers. ______ Arab leaders who had trusted British assurances came to view them with deep suspicion, a distrust that shaped negotiations at the postwar peace conferences.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In 1915 and 1916, British officials exchanged letters with Sharif Hussein of Mecca, suggesting that Britain would support an independent Arab state if he led a revolt against the Ottoman Empire. At the same time, British diplomat Mark Sykes and French diplomat François Georges-Picot secretly agreed to divide much of that same territory into British and French zones of control. After seizing power in Russia in 1917, the Bolsheviks published the secret agreement to expose the wartime deals of the Allied powers. ______ Arab leaders who had trusted British assurances came to view them with deep suspicion, a distrust that shaped negotiations at the postwar peace conferences.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 볼셰비키가 비밀 협정을 공개했다는 원인이고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 아랍 지도자들이 영국의 약속을 의심하게 되었다는 결과이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 지문 전체에 '약속 대 비밀 분할'이라는 대조가 있어 끌리지만, 그 대조는 첫 두 문장 사이의 관계이고 빈칸 앞뒤 문장은 서로 반대되지 않는다. C는 뒤 문장이 '전시 비밀 거래 폭로'의 한 사례가 아니라 그 폭로가 낳은 반응이므로 맞지 않는다. D는 두 문장이 서로 비슷한 사건을 나란히 놓는 관계가 아니므로 배제된다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the blank gives a cause: the Bolsheviks published the secret agreement. The sentence after it gives the effect: Arab leaders became suspicious of British assurances. That makes B the answer. A is tempting because the passage does contrast Britain's promises with the secret partition, but that contrast is between the first two sentences, and the sentences on either side of the blank don't oppose each other. C doesn't work because the Arab leaders' distrust isn't an example of the Allied deals being exposed; it's a reaction to that exposure. D doesn't fit because the second sentence doesn't describe a similar, parallel event.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞 문장(볼셰비키의 비밀 협정 공개)은 원인, 뒤 문장(아랍 지도자들의 불신)은 결과이므로 'As a result'(B)가 유일하게 논리적임. A는 지문 전반의 '약속 vs 비밀 분할' 대조 때문에 훑어 읽으면 끌리는 함정으로 적절히 설계됨. C·D는 비교적 약한 오답이나 말은 됨. 역사적 사실(후세인-맥마흔 서한 1915-16, 사이크스-피코 협정, 1917년 볼셰비키 공개)은 정확. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 난이도는 medium 하단에 가깝지만 다문장 인과 추적과 A 함정이 있어 적합으로 판정.

advisory.note: 후사인-맥마흔 서한(1915–16), 사이크스-피코 협정, 1917년 볼셰비키의 공개는 모두 사실과 맞음. 인과 관계가 명확하고, A는 지문 전체의 대조 때문에 그럴듯한 오답이 됨. C와 D는 다소 약하지만 말은 됨. medium 수준에 맞음.

problem.passage:
When Irish republicans seized the General Post Office and other sites in Dublin on Easter Monday, 1916, many Dubliners reacted with hostility; some jeered the rebels as they were marched away after their surrender six days later. ______ the British authorities' decision to court-martial and execute fifteen of the rising's leaders over the following weeks transformed that mood, turning the executed men into martyrs and swelling support for the republican cause.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: When Irish republicans seized the General Post Office and other sites in Dublin on Easter Monday, 1916, many Dubliners reacted with hostility; some jeered the rebels as they were marched away after their surrender six days later. ______ the British authorities' decision to court-martial and execute fifteen of the rising's leaders over the following weeks transformed that mood, turning the executed men into martyrs and swelling support for the republican cause.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 첫 문장은 봉기 직후 더블린 시민들이 반란군에게 적대적이었다는 내용이고, 둘째 문장은 영국 당국의 처형이 그 분위기를 바꿔 공화주의 지지를 키웠다는 내용이므로 대조 관계이다. 그래서 C가 정답이다. A는 처형이 시간상 뒤에 일어나서 결과처럼 보이지만, 시민의 적대감이 처형을 불러온 것이 아니고 둘째 문장은 그 적대감이 뒤집힌 것을 말하므로 틀리다. B는 둘째 문장이 적대감의 사례가 아니라 반대되는 변화이므로 틀리다. D는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용이 아니라 반대되는 내용이므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The first sentence says that right after the rising, Dubliners were hostile to the rebels. The second sentence says the British executions changed that mood and built support for the republicans, so the two sentences contrast, and C is correct. A may look right because the executions came afterward, but the public's hostility didn't cause the executions, and the second sentence describes that hostility being reversed. B is wrong because the second sentence isn't an example of hostility; it shows the opposite change. D is wrong because the sentences describe opposite reactions, not similar ones.

hardJudge.note: 정답 C 검산 완료: 1문장(시민의 적대감) → 2문장("transformed that mood", 지지 급증)은 명백한 대조이므로 However가 유일하게 성립. A는 시간 순서상 그럴듯해 보이는 유인 오답으로 기능하고, 해설이 그 배제 근거(적대감이 처형의 원인이 아님)를 정확히 짚음. B·D는 상대적으로 약하나 말은 됨. 역사 사실: 1916 부활절 월요일 점거, 항복 후 조롱, 지도자 15인 처형(더블린 14 + 코크 1, 5월 3~12일), 순교자화와 여론 반전 모두 정확. 다만 "six days later"는 봉기가 '6일간' 지속되었다는 관용적 표현에 기댄 것으로, 실제 항복(4/29 토)은 월요일 기준 5일 후라 엄밀히는 약간의 부정확이 있으나 문항 판단에 영향 없음. 난이도는 medium 하단(대조 신호가 비교적 분명)이나 A의 유인력과 긴 문장 구조를 고려하면 기준 범위 내로 판단.

advisory.note: 사실관계 정확(1916년 부활절 봉기, 처형된 지도자 수는 통상 16명으로 집계되지만 군사재판 후 더블린에서 처형된 인원은 14명이며 케이스먼트를 포함하면 16명. 15명은 더블린 14명과 코크의 토머스 켄트를 합친 수로 볼 수 있어 허용 범위임). 'that mood'가 대조를 알려 주고, Consequently는 시간 순서 때문에 그럴듯해 보여 함정 역할을 하므로 medium 수준에 맞음.

problem.passage:
In August 1947, the British boundary commission led by lawyer Cyril Radcliffe, a man who had never before visited India, drew the lines dividing Punjab and Bengal between the new states of India and Pakistan in roughly five weeks. Because the final maps were not published until two days after independence ______ millions of Hindus, Muslims, and Sikhs living near the new borders did not know which country they belonged to, and the resulting panic fueled communal violence that displaced an estimated fifteen million people.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In August 1947, the British boundary commission led by lawyer Cyril Radcliffe, a man who had never before visited India, drew the lines dividing Punjab and Bengal between the new states of India and Pakistan in roughly five weeks. Because the final maps were not published until two days after independence ______ millions of Hindus, Muslims, and Sikhs living near the new borders did not know which country they belonged to, and the resulting panic fueled communal violence that displaced an estimated fifteen million people.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 문장은 종속절 "Because the final maps ... had been declared"로 시작하고, 주절 "millions of Hindus ... did not know"가 그 뒤에 이어진다. 앞에 오는 부사절과 주절 사이는 쉼표로 구분하므로 D가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론과 C의 콜론은 앞부분이 독립절이어야 쓸 수 있는데, 앞부분은 Because로 시작하는 불완전한 절이다. B는 쉼표+and로 두 독립절을 잇는 형식처럼 보이지만, 그렇게 하면 Because절이 주절과 끊어져 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: This sentence opens with a dependent clause, "Because the final maps ... had been declared," and the main clause, "millions of Hindus ... did not know," follows it. When an introductory adverbial clause comes before the main clause, you separate the two with a comma, so D is correct. A (semicolon) and C (colon) both need a complete independent clause before the mark, but the text before the blank begins with "Because," so it isn't one. B uses comma plus "and," the pattern for joining two independent clauses, but adding "and" here cuts the Because clause off from its main clause, and the sentence falls apart.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞은 "Because the final maps were not published until two days after independence had been declared"라는 종속절(부사절)이고, 뒤는 주절 "millions ... did not know"이므로 쉼표(D)가 유일하게 올바름. A(세미콜론)·C(콜론)는 앞부분이 독립절이어야 하므로 오류, B(쉼표+and)는 종속절과 주절 사이에 등위접속사를 넣어 비문이 됨. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 정확, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 사실관계(Radcliffe 인도 미방문, 약 5주 작업, 1947년 8월 17일 발표=독립 2일 후, 약 1,500만 명 이주)도 통상 서술과 일치. 난이도: 긴 종속절 안에 "until ... had been declared"가 끼어 있어 훑어 읽으면 독립절로 오인해 A/C/B를 고를 수 있고, 정독하면 Because 식별 후 쉼표 규칙 적용이라는 두 단계로 명확히 풀림. 표준 SAT medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 문두 부사절 뒤 주절 경계 문제. 앞 부분이 길어서 독립절로 착각하기 쉽기 때문에 세미콜론·콜론·쉼표+and 오답이 모두 그럴듯함. 역사적 사실(Radcliffe의 인도 방문 경험 없음, 약 5주, 독립 이틀 뒤 8월 17일 공개, 약 1,500만 명 이주)은 일반적으로 인용되는 수치와 일치함.

problem.passage:
Historians often describe the Korean War as one of the first proxy conflicts of the Cold War. North Korea, armed and advised by the Soviet Union, invaded the South in June 1950, and the United States, acting under a United Nations mandate, quickly sent troops to defend the government in Seoul. The fighting, which ended in an armistice in July 1953 rather than in a formal peace ______ left the peninsula divided near the same line where the war had begun.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Historians often describe the Korean War as one of the first proxy conflicts of the Cold War. North Korea, armed and advised by the Soviet Union, invaded the South in June 1950, and the United States, acting under a United Nations mandate, quickly sent troops to defend the government in Seoul. The fighting, which ended in an armistice in July 1953 rather than in a formal peace ______ left the peninsula divided near the same line where the war had begun.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The fighting"이고 본동사는 "left"이며, 그 사이의 "which ended ... formal peace treaty"는 쉼표로 열린 비제한적 관계절이다. 따라서 관계절을 닫는 쉼표가 필요하므로 A가 정답이다. B의 세미콜론은 주어와 본동사를 떼어 놓아 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. C는 여는 쉼표만 있고 닫는 쉼표가 없어 삽입절의 끝이 표시되지 않는다. D는 "and left"가 관계절 안의 두 번째 동사가 되어 버려 주어 "The fighting"에 본동사가 남지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is "The fighting," and its main verb is "left." Between them sits a nonessential relative clause, "which ended ... formal peace treaty," and it opens with a comma. That clause needs a closing comma too, so A is correct. B is wrong because a semicolon would split the subject from its verb, and the words before it can't stand alone as an independent clause. C is wrong because it leaves out the closing comma, so nothing marks where the clause ends. D is wrong because "and left" turns "left" into a second verb inside the relative clause, which leaves "The fighting" with no main verb.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The fighting"과 본동사 "left" 사이의 비제한적 관계절(which ended ... treaty)을 닫는 쉼표가 필요하므로 A가 유일한 정답. B(세미콜론)는 주어-동사 분리, C는 닫는 쉼표 누락, D는 "and left"가 관계절 내부 동사가 되어 본동사 부재. 한국전쟁 사실관계(1950년 6월 침공, 1953년 7월 정전협정, UN 결의 하 미군 파병, 개전선 부근 분단)도 정확. 한·영 해설 모두 선택지 참조와 결론이 일치하며 자연스러움. 긴 삽입절 끝을 찾아 주어-동사 구조를 확인해야 하는 두 단계 판단으로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 사실관계(1950년 6월 침공, 1953년 7월 정전, 38선 부근 분단)가 정확하다. 관계절 안에 "rather than" 구가 들어 있어 닫는 쉼표가 들어갈 자리를 찾으려면 정독해야 하므로 medium에 맞는다.

problem.passage:

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Imre Nagy, a reform-minded communist who had been forced out of power by Hungary's hard-line leadership the previous year, was reinstated as prime minister in the first days of the 1956 uprising______ he announced Hungary's withdrawal from the Warsaw Pact, a decision that helped prompt Soviet tanks to roll back into Budapest on November 4.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Imre Nagy ... was reinstated ... uprising"은 긴 동격구가 들어 있어도 그 자체로 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 "he announced ..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있고, 도입 부사구 "within days" 뒤의 쉼표도 맞으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 두 절 사이에 아무 문장부호도 없어 run-on 문장이 된다. D는 관계대명사 "which"를 넣었지만 뒤에 주어 "he"가 이미 있어 관계절이 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank, "Imre Nagy ... was reinstated ... uprising," is a complete independent clause even though it contains a long appositive. The part after it, "he announced ...," is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, and the comma after the introductory phrase "within days" is correct, so B is the answer. A joins the two clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses, so it is a run-on sentence. D adds "which," but the clause after it already has the subject "he," so the relative clause doesn't work grammatically.

quality.seed: history and civics — Hungarian Revolution 1956 and anti-Soviet uprising crushed by Warsaw Pact tank intervention

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격구를 포함한 완전한 독립절("Imre Nagy ... was reinstated ... uprising"), 뒤는 "he announced ..." 독립절이므로 세미콜론으로 연결하는 B가 유일하게 올바름. A는 comma splice, C는 run-on, D는 "which" 뒤에 주어 "he"가 중복되어 비문. 역사적 사실(1955년 실각, 1956년 10월 24일 총리 복귀, 11월 1일 바르샤바조약기구 탈퇴 선언, 11월 4일 소련군 재진입)도 정확. 긴 동격구로 독립절 판단을 흐리게 하고 "within days" 쉼표로 A를 그럴듯하게 만들어 medium에 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 역사 사실 확인: 1955년 4월 실각, 1956년 10월 24일 복귀, 11월 1일 바르샤바 조약 탈퇴 선언, 11월 4일 소련 재개입. 모두 정확함. 긴 동격구 때문에 주절의 범위를 판단하기 어려워 중간 난이도에 맞음.

Militarily, the offensive was costly for the attackers, who failed to hold most of the positions they ______ the sheer scale of the assault, which included a brief breach of the US embassy compound in Saigon, contradicted official American assurances that the enemy was nearly defeated and deepened public doubts about the war.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In late January 1968, during the Lunar New Year holiday known as Tet, North Vietnamese and Viet Cong forces launched coordinated attacks on more than one hundred cities and towns across South Vietnam. Militarily, the offensive was costly for the attackers, who failed to hold most of the positions they ______ the sheer scale of the assault, which included a brief breach of the US embassy compound in Saigon, contradicted official American assurances that the enemy was nearly defeated and deepened public doubts about the war.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Militarily ... seized'와 뒤 'the sheer scale ... contradicted ... doubts'는 각각 독립절이므로 경계에 세미콜론이 필요하고, 'however'는 뒤 절에 속하는 접속부사로 'politically, however,'처럼 앞뒤를 쉼표로 감싸야 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 연결한 comma splice이다. B는 세미콜론을 however 뒤에 두어 'politically, however'가 앞 절에 붙게 되어 의미상 대조(군사적/정치적) 구조가 무너진다. C는 경계는 맞지만 however 뒤 쉼표가 빠져 삽입 요소가 주어 앞에서 제대로 분리되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank ("Militarily ... seized") and the text after it ("the sheer scale ... deepened public doubts about the war") are both independent clauses, so a semicolon has to mark the boundary between them. "However" is a conjunctive adverb that belongs to the second clause, and together with "politically" it is an introductory element, so it needs a comma after it: "politically, however," — that makes D correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. B puts the semicolon after "however," which attaches "politically, however" to the first clause and breaks the military-versus-political contrast. C places the boundary correctly but leaves out the comma after "however," so the introductory element isn't set off from the subject.

quality.seed: history and civics — Tet Offensive 1968 Vietnam and coordinated North Vietnamese surprise attack shifting American public opinion

hardJudge.note: 두 독립절(Militarily... seized / the sheer scale... doubts) 경계에 세미콜론, 접속부사 'however'를 쉼표로 감싼 D가 유일하게 올바름. A·B는 comma splice, C는 however 뒤 쉼표 누락으로 'however the sheer scale...'이 부사절처럼 읽혀 부적절. 테트 공세(1968년 1월 말, 100여 도시, 사이공 미 대사관 구내 일시 침입) 사실 정확. 세미콜론 위치 판단 + however 쉼표 처리의 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합하며, A·C는 부분적으로 그럴듯하고 B도 말이 되는 오답 구성.

advisory.note: D 정답이 맞다. 앞뒤가 모두 독립절이라 경계에 세미콜론이 필요하고, 뒤 절 앞에 나오는 'politically, however,'는 쉼표로 분리해야 한다. B와 C는 각각 일부만 맞아서 비교해야 배제되므로 medium 난이도에 맞는다. 테트 공세에 대한 서술도 사실과 일치한다.

problem.passage:

Mass media played a central role in the killing. Radio Télévision Libre des Mille Collines (RTLM), a privately owned station that repeatedly called Tutsi "cockroaches" and read out the names and locations of people to be hunted down by militia members ______ became one of the most notorious tools of the violence. Years later, the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda convicted several of the station's founders of inciting genocide.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: During the 1994 genocide in Rwanda, Hutu extremists killed an estimated 800,000 people, most of them members of the Tutsi minority, in about one hundred days. Mass media played a central role in the killing. Radio Télévision Libre des Mille Collines (RTLM), a privately owned station that repeatedly called Tutsi "cockroaches" and read out the names and locations of people to be hunted down by militia members ______ became one of the most notorious tools of the violence. Years later, the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda convicted several of the station's founders of inciting genocide.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "Radio Télévision Libre des Mille Collines (RTLM)"이고 동사는 "became"이다. 그 사이의 "a privately owned station that ... militia members"는 쉼표로 시작된 비필수 동격구이므로 같은 부호인 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론은 두 독립절 사이에만 쓰는데, 여기서는 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞뒤 모두 완전한 절이 되지 않는다. C의 대시도 삽입구를 닫을 수는 있지만, 쉼표로 시작한 삽입구를 대시로 닫으면 부호가 맞지 않는다. D는 동격구를 닫지 않아 "militia members became"처럼 읽혀 militia members가 became의 주어인 것처럼 문장 구조가 잘못 해석된다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is "Radio Télévision Libre des Mille Collines (RTLM)," and its verb is "became." The phrase in between, "a privately owned station that ... militia members," is a nonessential appositive that opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma too. That makes B correct. A doesn't work because a semicolon belongs only between two independent clauses, and here it would cut the subject off from its verb, so neither side is a complete clause. C is tempting because a dash can close an interruption, but an interruption that opens with a comma can't close with a dash, since the punctuation has to match. D leaves the appositive open, so the sentence reads as "militia members became," as if the militia members were the subject of "became," and that misreads the sentence's structure.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "RTLM"와 동사 "became" 사이의 비필수 동격구가 쉼표로 열렸으므로 쉼표로 닫는 B가 정답임을 직접 확인. A는 독립절 두 개가 없어 불가, C는 부호 불일치, D는 주어-동사 구조 오독 유발. 해설(한/영) 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. RTLM·ICTR 미디어 재판(설립자 선동죄 유죄) 등 사실 관계 정확. 긴 삽입구 속에서 주어-동사를 추적하고 여는 부호와 짝을 맞추는 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 긴 동격구(관계절 포함)를 닫는 쉼표를 찾는 표준 문항이다. 삽입구가 길어서 'militia members became'으로 잘못 읽힐 함정이 있고, 대시와 세미콜론도 그럴듯한 오답이다. 사실관계도 대체로 정확하다(ICTR Media 사건에서 RTLM 창립자 Nahimana와 Barayagwiza가 유죄 판결을 받음). 다만 'several'은 약간 넓은 표현이다.
