The catalysts developed by Karl Ziegler and Giulio Natta changed this outcome: by binding each incoming monomer in a fixed orientation at the metal center, they ______ the arrangement of the methyl groups, producing isotactic chains whose regular structure allowed them to pack into a rigid, crystalline plastic suitable for industrial use.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Before the 1950s, attempts to polymerize propylene yielded a sticky, rubbery mass in which the methyl groups along the chain pointed in random directions. The catalysts developed by Karl Ziegler and Giulio Natta changed this outcome: by binding each incoming monomer in a fixed orientation at the metal center, they ______ the arrangement of the methyl groups, producing isotactic chains whose regular structure allowed them to pack into a rigid, crystalline plastic suitable for industrial use.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 촉매가 단량체를 고정된 방향으로 결합시켜 메틸기 배열을 규칙적으로 만들었다고 설명하므로, 배열을 '결정했다/지정했다'는 뜻의 B가 정답이다. A는 촉매가 반응을 빠르게 한다는 일반 상식과 맞아 보이지만, 지문의 핵심은 속도가 아니라 배열의 규칙성이다. D는 배열에 변화를 주었다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 무작위 상태를 규칙적으로 바꾼 것이므로 '다양화했다'는 정반대다. C는 배열을 숨겼다는 뜻으로, 구조가 드러나 결정성을 낳았다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the catalysts bound each monomer in a fixed orientation, which turned random methyl placement into a regular isotactic pattern, so B ("dictated") fits: the catalysts determined the arrangement. A looks tempting because catalysts usually speed up reactions, but the sentence is about how orderly the structure is, not how fast the reaction runs. D seems possible because the catalysts did change the arrangement, but they made it more uniform, which is the opposite of diversifying it. C means hiding the arrangement, and nothing in the text is about hiding it; the point is that the catalysts produced a regular structure.

hardJudge.note: 검산: "by binding each incoming monomer in a fixed orientation" → 메틸기 배열을 '결정/지정'했다는 B가 유일하게 논리적. 무작위→규칙적 전환이므로 D(diversified)는 정반대, C(concealed)는 문맥 무관, A(accelerated)는 촉매=속도라는 상식에 기대는 매력적 오답이나 "배열을 가속했다"는 문맥과 어긋남. 과학적 사실(Ziegler–Natta 촉매, 이소택틱 폴리프로필렌의 결정성, 1950년대 이전 아택틱 고무상 생성물) 정확. 한·영 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 난이도: 메커니즘 문장(고정 방향 결합)과 결과(규칙 구조)를 연결해야 하고 A·D가 부분적 근거를 가지므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: Ziegler-Natta 촉매의 입체규칙성 설명이 사실과 맞음. A는 촉매 상식, D는 '변화'라는 부분 근거로 매력적 오답 역할을 하고, C도 말은 됨. medium에 적합함.

problem.passage:

Because of this periodic structure, light within a certain band of wavelengths cannot travel through the material and is reflected back. Researchers note that this mechanism makes the color unusually ______: whereas pigments gradually break down under sunlight, a structural color persists as long as the lattice itself remains intact, which explains why specimens collected more than a century ago still gleam in museum drawers.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

Because of this periodic structure, light within a certain band of wavelengths cannot travel through the material and is reflected back. Researchers note that this mechanism makes the color unusually ______: whereas pigments gradually break down under sunlight, a structural color persists as long as the lattice itself remains intact, which explains why specimens collected more than a century ago still gleam in museum drawers.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 뒤 콜론 이하에서 색소는 햇빛에 분해되지만 구조색은 격자가 유지되는 한 지속되고, 백 년 된 표본도 여전히 빛난다고 설명하므로 '오래 지속되는'을 뜻하는 C가 정답이다. A는 반짝이는 색이라는 묘사와 어울리지만 시간에 따른 지속성이라는 핵심 대비를 담지 못한다. B는 구조색이 시야각에 따라 변한다는 배경지식과 연결될 수 있으나 지문은 변하지 않고 지속됨을 강조하므로 반대 방향이다. D는 빛이 반사된다는 앞 문장과 표면적으로 일치하지만, 빈칸 뒤의 근거인 분해 대 지속의 대비를 설명하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The colon after the blank sets up the explanation: pigments break down under sunlight, but structural color lasts as long as the lattice survives, so century-old specimens still gleam. That points to C, meaning long-lasting. A fits the shiny appearance, but it doesn't capture the contrast about lasting over time. B may remind you that iridescent color shifts with viewing angle, but the text stresses that the color stays the same, which is the opposite idea. D echoes the earlier statement that light is reflected, but it doesn't match the reasoning that follows the blank, which compares breaking down with lasting.

hardJudge.note: 콜론 이하 '색소는 분해 vs 구조색은 격자가 유지되는 한 지속, 백 년 된 표본도 여전히 빛남'이 '오래 지속되는'(durable)을 명확히 뒷받침하므로 정답 C 타당. advisory.note: 콜론 뒤의 분해 대 지속 대비가 durable을 명확히 뒷받침함. vivid와 reflective는 앞 맥락(gleam, reflected)과 부분적으로 맞아 유인력이 있고, variable은 지문 방향과 반대임. 난이도 medium에 맞음.

problem.passage:
In electrospinning, a high voltage draws a charged polymer solution from a needle into a thin jet that stretches and dries into nanofibers. Materials engineer Priya Raman found that the voltage and the flow rate cannot be tuned independently: raising the voltage thins the fibers only if the flow rate is lowered at the same time, since excess solution otherwise thickens the jet faster than the electric field can stretch it. Because of this interdependence, Raman argues that the two settings must be ______ rather than optimized one at a time.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In electrospinning, a high voltage draws a charged polymer solution from a needle into a thin jet that stretches and dries into nanofibers. Materials engineer Priya Raman found that the voltage and the flow rate cannot be tuned independently: raising the voltage thins the fibers only if the flow rate is lowered at the same time, since excess solution otherwise thickens the jet faster than the electric field can stretch it. Because of this interdependence, Raman argues that the two settings must be ______ rather than optimized one at a time.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 전압과 유량이 서로 영향을 주므로 따로따로 조정할 수 없다고 말하고, 빈칸은 "하나씩 최적화하는 것"과 대비되는 말이어야 하므로 두 값을 함께 맞춘다는 뜻의 A(coordinated)가 정답이다. B(maximized)는 전압을 높이는 내용과 일부 맞아 보이지만, 지문에서는 유량을 낮춰야 한다고 하므로 두 값을 모두 최대로 올리는 것은 맞지 않는다. C(standardized)는 정해진 설정값이라는 뜻이어서 두 값이 서로에 맞춰 함께 바뀐다는 핵심을 담지 못한다. D(isolated)는 따로 다룬다는 뜻으로, 지문이 부정하는 "하나씩 최적화"와 같은 의미가 되어 버린다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says voltage and flow rate depend on each other, and the blank has to contrast with "optimized one at a time." That means the two settings must be adjusted together, so choice A (coordinated) is the answer. Choice B (maximized) can look right because the passage mentions raising the voltage, but the flow rate actually has to be lowered, so pushing both settings to their highest values doesn't work. Choice C (standardized) means fixed, agreed-upon values, which misses the point that each setting must change in response to the other. Choice D (isolated) means handling the settings separately, which is exactly the one-at-a-time approach the passage rejects.

Food scientists have found that this transformation is highly sensitive to the rate of heating: when the temperature climbs too quickly, granules on the outside of a mixture can burst before those in the center have swollen at all. For this reason, recipes that depend on a smooth, uniform sauce often call for heat that is ______, allowing every granule to pass through the same stages at roughly the same time.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 온도가 너무 빨리 오르면 바깥 입자가 먼저 터져 불균일해진다고 설명하므로, 해결책은 천천히 올라가는 열, 즉 B 'gradual'이다. A 'intense'는 열이 강하다는 뜻으로, 지문이 문제로 지적한 급격한 가열을 오히려 부추긴다. C 'brief'는 짧은 시간을 뜻해 열이 오르는 속도와 무관하고, 모든 입자가 단계를 거칠 시간을 주지도 못한다. D 'constant'는 일정함이라는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 일정하게 높은 열은 여전히 빠른 온도 상승을 일으킬 수 있으며 지문의 핵심인 '상승 속도'를 정확히 짚지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says that when the temperature rises too quickly, outer granules burst before inner ones swell, so the fix is heat that rises slowly. That makes B, "gradual," the answer. A, "intense," means strong heat, which would make the rapid heating problem worse. C, "brief," describes how long the heat lasts, not how fast the temperature rises, and it wouldn't give every granule time to go through each stage. D, "constant," sounds reasonable because it suggests steadiness, but steady high heat can still raise the temperature fast, so it misses the text's point about the rate of heating.

The process works only if the applied pressure exceeds the seawater's osmotic pressure, the natural tendency of water to move toward the saltier side. As fresh water leaves, the brine left behind grows more concentrated, so its osmotic pressure rises. Engineers therefore note that the required pump pressure does not stay fixed during operation; instead, it must ______ as recovery increases, or the flow of purified water will slow and eventually stop.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

problem.explanation: 농축수의 삼투압이 계속 올라가므로, 물이 계속 흐르려면 가해지는 압력도 함께 증가해야 한다. 따라서 '점점 높아지다'를 뜻하는 C(escalate)가 정답이다. A(fluctuate)는 압력이 고정되지 않는다는 점과는 맞지만, 오르내림을 뜻해 한 방향으로 꾸준히 증가한다는 의미를 정확히 담지 못한다. B(stabilize)는 압력이 고정되지 않는다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. D(reverse)는 물의 흐름 방향과 관련 있어 보이지만, 압력의 방향을 바꾸면 담수화 원리 자체가 무너진다.
problem.explanationEn: The brine's osmotic pressure keeps rising, so the applied pressure has to keep climbing to stay above it. That makes C (escalate), meaning "increase steadily," the right answer. A (fluctuate) does fit the idea that the pressure isn't fixed, but it means going up and down, not a steady one-way increase. B (stabilize) contradicts the statement that the pressure does not stay fixed. D (reverse) might seem connected to which way the water flows, but reversing the pressure would undo the desalination process entirely.

Materials scientist Lena Okafor notes that this speed does more than save time: because the powder spends so little time hot, SPS can ______ grain growth, allowing engineers to produce dense ceramic composites whose fine-grained structure gives them unusual toughness.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

So the blank needs a word meaning "hold back," which is D. A may tempt you because the passage stresses speed, but accelerating grain growth would contradict the fine-grained result. B and C sound reasonable in a lab setting, but the passage gives no reason why brief heating would reveal or measure grain growth, and neither word explains why the structure stays fine.

problem.passage:
When a circuit board heats up and cools down repeatedly, the copper pads and the silicon chip expand and contract by different amounts, putting stress on the tiny solder joints that connect them. Materials engineer Priya Raman found that a single cycle almost never causes visible damage. Instead, each cycle adds a little strain to the solder's grain structure, and over thousands of cycles the effect ______: microscopic voids gradually join together until a crack forms and the electrical connection fails.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: When a circuit board heats up and cools down repeatedly, the copper pads and the silicon chip expand and contract by different amounts, putting stress on the tiny solder joints that connect them. Materials engineer Priya Raman found that a single cycle almost never causes visible damage. Instead, each cycle adds a little strain to the solder's grain structure, and over thousands of cycles the effect ______: microscopic voids gradually join together until a crack forms and the electrical connection fails.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 한 번의 사이클로는 손상이 없지만 각 사이클이 '조금씩' 변형을 더해 수천 번 후 균열이 생긴다고 설명하므로, 작은 효과가 쌓인다는 뜻의 B(accumulates)가 정답이다. C(intensifies)는 효과가 커진다는 점에서 부분적으로 맞지만, 각 사이클의 강도가 세진다는 의미여서 작은 손상이 더해진다는 '누적'의 핵심을 정확히 담지 못한다. D(disperses)는 미세 공극이 '흩어진다'는 연상과 연결될 수 있으나, 공극이 서로 합쳐진다는 내용과 정반대이다. A(reverses)는 냉각 시 수축하는 상황을 떠올리게 하지만, 손상이 결국 고장으로 이어진다는 흐름과 모순된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says one cycle almost never causes damage, but each cycle adds a little strain, and after thousands of cycles a crack forms. That describes small effects building up over time, so B (accumulates) is correct. C (intensifies) is partly right because the damage does grow, but it suggests each cycle gets stronger, which misses the key idea of small amounts adding up. D (disperses) might call to mind the voids being spread out, but the text says the voids join together, which is the opposite. A (reverses) might fit the idea of cooling undoing expansion, but it contradicts the point that the damage ends in failure.

hardJudge.note: 'each cycle adds a little strain' + 'over thousands of cycles'가 누적(accumulates)을 명확히 지시함. C(intensifies)는 강한 매력 오답으로 비교 판단이 필요하고, D는 'microscopic voids' 연상, A는 열팽창·수축 연상으로 그럴듯함. 한·영 해설 결론과 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 열 사이클에 의한 솔더 피로 균열(공극 합체→균열) 서술은 공학적으로 타당.

advisory.note: "each cycle adds a little strain"는 누적을 강하게 가리키고, intensifies는 그럴듯한 오답으로 정확도를 따져야 배제된다. A와 D는 쉽게 배제되는 편이지만 medium 난이도로는 적절하다. 열피로 관련 사실도 정확하다.

By reducing the background flow that usually carries all particles along together, the coating ______ small differences in particle motion that would otherwise go unnoticed.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

Engineers have used this property in dampers that protect buildings from earthquakes. Because the strength of the magnetic field can be adjusted continuously, the damper's resistance is not fixed at one level; sensors detect the ground's motion, and a controller ______ the fluid's viscosity from moment to moment, stiffening it during strong shaking and loosening it during milder tremors.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

A fits the stiffening part, but it doesn't fit the loosening during mild tremors. B means keeping viscosity unchanged, which goes against the idea that resistance is not fixed. C does suggest change, but it means simply flipping the viscosity to its opposite, not fine-tuning it to how strong the shaking is.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Friction-stir welding (FSW) was developed at The Welding Institute in the United Kingdom in 1991.
- In FSW, a rotating tool with a shoulder and a pin is plunged into the seam between two metal plates.
- Friction from the spinning tool softens the metal to roughly 80 percent of its melting point without actually melting it.
- The tool stirs the softened metal from both plates together, forming a solid bond as it cools.
- Conventional fusion welding melts aluminum alloys, which can create porosity and cracks that weaken aircraft joints.

The student wants to explain why friction-stir welding is suited to aircraft construction. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options: Because friction-stir welding joins aluminum without melting it, it avoids the porosity and cracks of fusion welding, allowing some manufacturers to replace thousands of fuselage rivets.
Because friction-stir welding uses a rotating tool with a shoulder and a pin, it can be plunged into the seam between two metal plates, including aluminum ones.
Because friction-stir welding was developed at The Welding Institute in 1991, it has been studied for decades by manufacturers of many kinds of metal products.

B accurately describes the tool but never says why that matters for aircraft. C gives only the origin date and adds a claim about decades of study that isn't in the notes, with no link to aircraft. D explains how the process softens and stirs metal, but it doesn't connect this to any advantage in aircraft construction.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Precision optical lenses, such as those in telescopes and lithography systems, require surfaces smooth to within a few nanometers.
- Conventional mechanical polishing removes glass by abrasion: hard particles scratch away material, which can leave microscopic subsurface cracks.
- Tribochemical polishing uses softer particles, such as cerium oxide, that chemically bond with the glass surface during rubbing.
- In tribochemical polishing, the bonded surface atoms are then carried away by the particles, removing material roughly one molecular layer at a time.
- Because it relies on chemical bonding rather than scratching, tribochemical polishing leaves far less subsurface damage than abrasive polishing.

The student wants to contrast how the two polishing methods take material off a glass surface. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In a magnetic material, the spins of electrons tend to line up along certain preferred crystal directions, called "easy axes."
- Magnetocrystalline anisotropy is the energy cost of turning those spins away from an easy axis.
- Neodymium-iron-boron (Nd2Fe14B) has a very strong anisotropy, so its spins strongly resist being turned.
- As a result, Nd2Fe14B has high coercivity: a strong opposing field is needed to demagnetize it, making it useful for permanent magnets in electric motors.
- Soft iron has a weak anisotropy, so its spins turn easily, and it loses its magnetization in a weak opposing field.

The student wants to explain why one material keeps its magnetization better than the other. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

problem.passage:
In electroplating, metal ions dissolved in a bath are reduced at a cathode, where they deposit as a thin metal coating. Manufacturers of jewelry and circuit boards have long assumed that the smoothness of a coating depends mainly on how much metal is deposited overall. Materials chemist Lena Hwang proposes a different explanation: smoothness is determined chiefly by the earliest stage of plating, when ions first form tiny clusters, or nuclei, on the bare cathode surface. According to Hwang, when many nuclei form at once and are spread densely across the surface, they merge into an even layer, but when only a few nuclei form, each grows into a separate bump that remains visible even after much more metal has been added.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Hwang's proposal?
problem.stimulus: In electroplating, metal ions dissolved in a bath are reduced at a cathode, where they deposit as a thin metal coating. Manufacturers of jewelry and circuit boards have long assumed that the smoothness of a coating depends mainly on how much metal is deposited overall. Materials chemist Lena Hwang proposes a different explanation: smoothness is determined chiefly by the earliest stage of plating, when ions first form tiny clusters, or nuclei, on the bare cathode surface. According to Hwang, when many nuclei form at once and are spread densely across the surface, they merge into an even layer, but when only a few nuclei form, each grows into a separate bump that remains visible even after much more metal has been added.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Hwang's proposal?
options: Coatings that received the largest total amount of deposited metal were generally smoother than coatings that received smaller amounts, regardless of conditions during the first seconds of plating.
Cathodes on which nuclei formed densely in the first seconds of plating took slightly longer to reach a given coating thickness than cathodes on which nuclei formed sparsely.

Coatings of equal total thickness differed sharply in smoothness, and the smoothest ones were those whose cathodes had shown the highest number of nuclei per unit area in the first seconds of plating.
Circuit board coatings plated with copper were rougher on average than jewelry coatings plated with gold, even though both were plated to a similar final thickness.
problem.explanation: Hwang의 주장은 증착된 금속의 총량이 아니라 초기 핵 밀도가 매끄러움을 결정한다는 것이다. C는 총 두께를 같게 통제한 상태에서 매끄러움이 초기 핵 밀도와 함께 달라졌음을 보여 주므로 이 주장을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 총량을 중시하는 기존 가정을 지지하므로 Hwang의 주장을 오히려 약화한다. B는 핵 밀도를 다루지만 매끄러움이 아니라 도금 속도에 관한 내용이다. D는 같은 두께에서 매끄러움이 차이 난다는 점을 보여 주지만, 그 차이를 핵 형성과 연결하지 않고 금속 종류의 차이로만 설명한다.
problem.explanationEn: Hwang argues that coating smoothness depends mainly on how densely nuclei form at the start, not on the total amount of metal deposited. C keeps the total thickness the same and shows that smoothness tracked early nucleus density, so it directly supports her proposal. A supports the traditional total-amount view, which works against Hwang. B does mention nucleus density, but it links density to plating speed, not to smoothness. D shows that coatings of similar thickness can differ in smoothness, but it never connects that difference to nucleation. Instead, it only points to a difference between metals.

problem.passage:
Photochromic eyeglass lenses darken outdoors because they contain spiro compounds such as spirooxazines. When ultraviolet light strikes one of these molecules, a bond in its ring structure breaks and the molecule unfolds into a flat, colored form called a merocyanine. Indoors, away from UV light, the molecule closes again and the lens clears. Users have long noticed that these lenses stay noticeably lighter on hot summer days than on cold winter days, even in equally bright sunlight. Chemist Lena Haviland proposes that this happens because heat speeds up the closing reaction: at higher temperatures, colored molecules snap back to the colorless form faster, so fewer of them are in the colored form at any one moment, even though UV light opens new molecules at the same rate.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Haviland's hypothesis?
problem.stimulus: Photochromic eyeglass lenses darken outdoors because they contain spiro compounds such as spirooxazines. When ultraviolet light strikes one of these molecules, a bond in its ring structure breaks and the molecule unfolds into a flat, colored form called a merocyanine. Indoors, away from UV light, the molecule closes again and the lens clears. Users have long noticed that these lenses stay noticeably lighter on hot summer days than on cold winter days, even in equally bright sunlight. Chemist Lena Haviland proposes that this happens because heat speeds up the closing reaction: at higher temperatures, colored molecules snap back to the colorless form faster, so fewer of them are in the colored form at any one moment, even though UV light opens new molecules at the same rate.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Haviland's hypothesis?
options: Under steady UV exposure, lenses held at 35°C and lenses held at 5°C reached the same maximum darkness, but the 35°C lenses took longer to get there.
When lenses were kept in darkness at a single temperature, the colored form returned to the colorless form at a steady rate that depended on how many colored molecules were present.
Under steady UV exposure, lenses held at 35°C absorbed far less ultraviolet light than lenses held at 5°C, so fewer molecules were opened in the warm lenses.
When UV light was switched off, lenses held at 35°C cleared several times faster than lenses held at 5°C, while both sets of lenses absorbed UV light at the same rate.
problem.explanation: Haviland의 가설은 두 부분으로 되어 있다. 열이 닫힘(탈색) 반응을 빠르게 하고, UV에 의한 열림 속도는 온도와 관계없이 같다는 것이다. D는 따뜻한 렌즈가 더 빨리 투명해지면서 UV 흡수량은 같았다는 결과이므로 두 부분을 모두 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 최대 어두움이 같았다고 하므로 따뜻한 날 렌즈가 더 밝다는 현상 자체와 맞지 않는다. B는 닫힘 반응을 설명하지만 온도를 비교하지 않는다. C는 열림 쪽 차이로 현상을 설명하므로 열림 속도가 같다는 가설의 전제와 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn: Haviland's hypothesis has two parts: heat speeds up the closing (fading) reaction, and UV opens molecules at the same rate no matter the temperature. D shows that warm lenses cleared faster while both sets absorbed UV equally, so it directly supports both parts. A says the maximum darkness was the same, which doesn't even match the observation that lenses stay lighter on hot days. B describes the closing reaction but never compares temperatures. C explains the effect through a difference in opening, which goes against the hypothesis's claim that the opening rate stays the same.

advisory.note: D는 온도에 따른 닫힘 속도와 같은 UV 흡수라는 두 요소를 모두 뒷받침한다. 오답들은 각각 그럴듯한 함정이다(A는 온도 비교, B는 닫힘 반응, C는 온도와 흡수 차이를 다룸). 다만 D는 키워드 대응만으로 비교적 쉽게 찾을 수 있다. 그래도 중간 난이도 범위 안이다.

problem.passage:
When helium-4 is cooled below about 2.17 kelvins, it becomes a superfluid that can flow through extremely narrow channels without any measurable friction. Early cryogenic engineers assumed that a liquid with such strange behavior would be too unpredictable to use in practical equipment and treated it as a laboratory curiosity. In practice, however, superfluid helium's ability to carry heat away with remarkable efficiency has made it ______ in systems that cool the superconducting magnets of large particle accelerators, where engineers now rely on it to keep conditions steady.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: When helium-4 is cooled below about 2.17 kelvins, it becomes a superfluid that can flow through extremely narrow channels without any measurable friction. Early cryogenic engineers assumed that a liquid with such strange behavior would be too unpredictable to use in practical equipment and treated it as a laboratory curiosity. In practice, however, superfluid helium's ability to carry heat away with remarkable efficiency has made it ______ in systems that cool the superconducting magnets of large particle accelerators, where engineers now rely on it to keep conditions steady.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation:
정답 A(indispensable, 없어서는 안 될). 'however' 뒤 문장을 보면 초유체 헬륨이 열을 매우 효율적으로 운반하고, 엔지니어들이 지금은 조건을 안정적으로 유지하는 데 '의존한다(rely on)'고 되어 있다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '실용성이 없다'는 통념과 정반대인 '필수적인'이 들어가야 한다.
B(impractical, 비실용적인): 반박당한 초기 엔지니어들의 생각을 그대로 옮긴 말이라 전환어 'however'와 맞지 않는다.
C(somewhat unreliable, 다소 신뢰할 수 없는): 전환어를 놓치고 통념과 같은 방향으로 강도만 약하게 한 표현이다. 'rely on'과 충돌한다.
D(luminous, 빛나는): 열 운반이나 실용성과 상관없는 제3의 의미다.
problem.explanationEn:
The answer is A, "indispensable." After "In practice, however," the text says superfluid helium carries heat away very efficiently and that engineers now rely on it to keep conditions steady. That reverses the early belief that it was too unpredictable to be practical, so the blank needs a word meaning "essential."
B, "impractical," just repeats the early engineers' belief, which the word "however" overturns.
C, "somewhat unreliable," misses the shift and keeps the old view, only in a weaker form. It also contradicts "rely on."
D, "luminous," means "glowing." It has nothing to do with heat transfer or usefulness.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 'however' 이후 'remarkable efficiency', 'rely on it to keep conditions steady'로 유일하게 지지됨. 사실관계(He-4 람다점 ≈2.17K, 입자가속기 초전도자석 냉각에 초유체 헬륨 사용) 정확. 체크리스트 4 미충족: C 'somewhat unreliable'은 정답 방향의 강도 변형이 아니라 B와 같은 통념 방향의 약화 표현이어서 3번과 중복되고, 정답 방향에서 강도만 다른 매력적 오답(예: 'marginally useful' 류)이 없음. D 'luminous'는 문맥 무관한 명백한 오답이라 변별력 낮음. 전환 구조는 분명하나 negation layer·확신도 조정 등 추가 사고 요구는 약해 hard 중 하위권.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 옳다. 사실관계도 맞다(람다점 약 2.17 K, LHC 자석은 초유체 헬륨으로 냉각). 체크리스트 4번은 충족하지 못했다. C는 통념 방향의 약한 표현일 뿐이고, 정답과 같은 방향이면서 강도만 다른 오답(예: useful, helpful)이 없어 정밀도를 가르는 변별이 없다. D는 무관한 단어라 바로 제외된다. 'however' 뒤에 'rely on', 'remarkable efficiency'가 직접 나와 정답이 곧바로 정해지므로 전형적인 medium 수준의 통념 반전 문항이다. hard 특성은 충족하지 못한다.

problem.passage:
Zeolites are crystalline aluminosilicates filled with uniform, molecule-sized pores, and textbooks often call them "molecular sieves": in this account, they separate gases by letting small molecules through and blocking larger ones. For the industrial production of oxygen from air, however, this tidy image ______ how the process actually works. Oxygen and nitrogen molecules differ in size by only a fraction of an angstrom, and the zeolites used in air-separation plants hold on to nitrogen more strongly because nitrogen's larger quadrupole moment interacts strongly with the metal cations lining the pores, not because nitrogen is too large to enter.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Zeolites are crystalline aluminosilicates filled with uniform, molecule-sized pores, and textbooks often call them "molecular sieves": in this account, they separate gases by letting small molecules through and blocking larger ones. For the industrial production of oxygen from air, however, this tidy image ______ how the process actually works. Oxygen and nitrogen molecules differ in size by only a fraction of an angstrom, and the zeolites used in air-separation plants hold on to nitrogen more strongly because nitrogen's larger quadrupole moment interacts strongly with the metal cations lining the pores, not because nitrogen is too large to enter.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation:
지문은 두 단계로 되어 있다. 첫 단계는 제올라이트를 크기로 걸러내는 '체'로 보는 교과서식 설명을 소개하고, 둘째 단계는 'however'로 시작해 그 설명을 반박한다. 산소와 질소는 크기가 거의 같고, 실제 분리는 질소의 사중극자 모멘트와 양이온 사이의 상호작용으로 일어난다. 그러므로 빈칸에는 그 깔끔한 이미지가 실제 원리를 '가린다'는 반박의 동사가 들어가야 하며, 정답은 C 'obscures'이다.
A 'illustrates'(보여 주다)는 첫 단계의 설명적 흐름에는 어울린다. 하지만 'however'로 시작하는 반박과 뒤따르는 반대 근거와는 모순된다.
B 'addresses'(다루다)는 중립적인 단어여서 그 이미지가 실제 원리와 어긋난다는 반박의 기능을 전달하지 못한다.
D 'erroneous'(잘못된)는 의미상으로는 반박에 가깝지만 형용사다. 'this tidy image ___ how the process works' 자리에는 목적어를 받는 동사가 필요하므로 문법적으로 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
The text has two stages. First, it presents the textbook picture of zeolites as size-based sieves. Then, starting with "however," it argues against that picture: oxygen and nitrogen are nearly the same size, and the real separation comes from nitrogen's quadrupole moment interacting with the cations in the pores. So the blank needs a verb that pushes back on the picture, saying it hides the real mechanism. That makes "obscures" (C) the correct answer.
- **A ("illustrates")** fits the descriptive first stage. But it contradicts the "however" and the evidence against the picture that follows.
- **B ("addresses")** is neutral. It doesn't say that the image misleads, so it can't do the job of a rebuttal.
- **D ("erroneous")** is close in meaning, but it's an adjective. The blank must be a verb that takes "how the process actually works" as its object.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 교과서식 '분자체' 설명(1단계)과 'however'로 시작하는 반박(2단계)으로 명확히 나뉘며, 빈칸은 2단계 첫 문장에 위치한다. 정답 'obscures'는 깔끔한 이미지가 실제 원리(크기 차이 미미, 사중극자-양이온 상호작용에 의한 질소 선택 흡착)를 가린다는 반박 기능에 부합. A 'illustrates'는 1단계에 어울리는 오답, D 'erroneous'는 의미는 근접하나 형용사로 품사가 어긋나는 오답, B 'addresses'는 중립어로 반박 기능 미충족. 과학적 사실(O2/N2 운동 직경 3.46 vs 3.64 Å, PSA 공정에서 질소 사중극자 모멘트에 의한 선택 흡착)도 정확. 해설은 정답과 오답 배제 논리를 일관되게 뒷받침. 정답 도출에는 'however' 단서, 크기 유사성 증거, 흡착 메커니즘 설명을 종합해 통념을 뒤집는 관계어를 추론해야 하므로 medium 이상의 사고를 요구한다.

advisory.note: 'however' 하나만으로 대조 방향이 바로 드러나고, D는 품사만 봐도 탈락하며, B는 중립어라 쉽게 지울 수 있다. 통념을 반박하는 구조는 있지만 그 반박이 명시적으로 신호되어 있어 역전 관계를 따로 추론할 필요가 없다. 난이도는 주로 과학 용어(사중극자 모멘트, 양이온)에서 나오므로 전형적인 medium 수준이다. 사실관계(O2와 N2의 크기 차이가 1 Å 미만, 질소의 사중극자 모멘트와 양이온의 상호작용에 의한 흡착)는 정확하다.

problem.passage:
Lens makers often finish glass surfaces with tribochemical polishing, in which a slurry of fine particles rubs against the glass while water in the slurry chemically softens the topmost layer of atoms. Engineers at one optics company tested this process on two identical batches of lenses. Both batches were polished with the same particles, pressure, and time, but the first batch was polished in a completely dry chamber, while the second was polished with water added. Under a microscope, the lenses in the first batch still showed tiny raised bumps, called asperities, that had been bent but not removed, whereas the lenses in the second batch were smooth at the atomic scale. Because water was the only difference between the two batches, the engineers concluded that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Lens makers often finish glass surfaces with tribochemical polishing, in which a slurry of fine particles rubs against the glass while water in the slurry chemically softens the topmost layer of atoms. Engineers at one optics company tested this process on two identical batches of lenses. Both batches were polished with the same particles, pressure, and time, but the first batch was polished in a completely dry chamber, while the second was polished with water added. Under a microscope, the lenses in the first batch still showed tiny raised bumps, called asperities, that had been bent but not removed, whereas the lenses in the second batch were smooth at the atomic scale. Because water was the only difference between the two batches, the engineers concluded that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the polishing particles, rather than the water, were mainly responsible for removing the asperities from the second batch.
the dry chamber caused the asperities to form on the lenses in the first batch during polishing.
increasing the pressure in the dry chamber would have made the first batch just as smooth as the second batch.
the chemical action of water was needed for the asperities to be removed rather than merely bent.
problem.explanation: 두 묶음은 입자·압력·시간이 같고 물의 유무만 달랐으며, 물이 없을 때는 돌기가 휘기만 하고 물이 있을 때만 제거되었다. 따라서 물의 화학 작용이 돌기 제거에 필요하다는 D가 정답이다. A는 두 묶음에서 입자가 같았으므로 결과 차이를 설명하지 못한다. B는 돌기가 연마 중 생겼다는 근거가 없으며, 지문은 돌기가 '제거되지 않았다'고만 한다. C는 압력이 실험에서 바뀌지 않았으므로 압력의 효과를 결론 내릴 수 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The two batches had the same particles, pressure, and time; the only difference was water. Without water, the asperities were only bent, and with water they were removed, so D is correct: the water's chemical action was needed for removal. A doesn't work because the particles were the same in both batches, so they can't explain why the results differed. B claims the dry chamber created the asperities, but the text only says they weren't removed. C makes a claim about pressure, which was never changed in the test, so the engineers couldn't conclude anything about it.

hardJudge.note: 통제 실험(물만 다름)에서 결과 차이의 원인을 유일한 변수로 귀속시키는 한 단계 추론. 단서("Because water was the only difference")가 직접 제시되어 easy에 적합. 오답 A(입자 귀속), B(원인·결과 혼동), C(검증되지 않은 변수) 모두 전형적 오개념으로 그럴듯하며 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제 가능. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치. tribochemical polishing 서술은 실제 개념(화학기계적 연마)과 부합하며 사실 오류 없음. 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 단일 변수 통제 실험 추론으로 한 단계 추론임. 오답들은 전형적 오개념(같은 입자에 원인 돌리기, 생성과 비제거 혼동, 바꾸지 않은 변수로 결론 내리기)이라 easy 목표에 맞음.

problem.passage:
To coat solar cells with thin silicon films, manufacturers often use plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD). In this process, an electric field turns a gas such as silane into a plasma that contains highly reactive fragments called radicals. These radicals land on the cell's surface and bond there, building the film layer by layer. Engineers at one factory found that the film grew only where radicals reached the surface; areas shielded from the plasma by a metal clamp stayed bare. This suggests that if a section of a solar panel is blocked so that no radicals can reach it during PECVD, ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: To coat solar cells with thin silicon films, manufacturers often use plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD). In this process, an electric field turns a gas such as silane into a plasma that contains highly reactive fragments called radicals. These radicals land on the cell's surface and bond there, building the film layer by layer. Engineers at one factory found that the film grew only where radicals reached the surface; areas shielded from the plasma by a metal clamp stayed bare. This suggests that if a section of a solar panel is blocked so that no radicals can reach it during PECVD, ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: that section will likely end up without a silicon film.
that section will likely end up with a thicker silicon film than other areas.
that section will likely end up with a film made of metal from the clamp.
that section will likely end up coated once the silane gas cools.
problem.explanation: 지문은 라디칼이 표면에 닿아 결합해야만 막이 자라며, 클램프로 가려진 부분은 맨 표면으로 남았다고 말한다. 따라서 라디칼이 닿지 못하는 부분에는 실리콘 막이 생기지 않는다는 A가 정답이다. B는 가려진 부분에 막이 오히려 두껍게 생긴다고 하여 지문의 관찰과 반대이다. C는 클램프의 금속이 막을 이룬다고 하지만 지문에 그런 근거가 없다. D는 가스가 식으면 막이 생긴다고 하지만, 지문에서 막을 만드는 것은 냉각이 아니라 라디칼이다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says the film forms only when radicals reach the surface and bond there, and the areas covered by the clamp stayed bare. So a section that no radicals can reach should end up with no silicon film, which makes A the answer. B says the blocked section gets a thicker film, which is the opposite of what the engineers saw. C says the film would be made of metal from the clamp, but nothing in the passage supports that. D says the section gets coated once the gas cools, but in the passage the film comes from radicals, not from the gas cooling.

hardJudge.note: 지문이 "막은 라디칼이 닿은 곳에서만 자랐고 가려진 부분은 맨 표면으로 남았다"고 직접 진술하므로, 라디칼이 차단된 구역에 막이 없다는 A가 한 단계 추론으로 도출된다. B는 관찰과 정반대, C는 지문에 근거 없음(클램프는 차폐물일 뿐), D는 냉각이 아닌 라디칼이 막을 만든다는 지문 내용과 충돌하여 모두 배제 가능하되 비전문가에게는 그럴듯하다. PECVD·실란·라디칼 설명은 과학적으로 타당하다. 한국어·영어 해설은 글자 참조와 결론이 일치하고 영어는 자연스러우며 한글 혼입 없음. 선택지 4개 평행 구조, 정답 표기 정상.

advisory.note: 지문의 관찰(가려진 부분은 맨 표면으로 남음)을 그대로 적용하면 되는 한 단계 추론이다. 오답들도 각각 반대 방향, 근거 없는 금속 막, 원인을 잘못 짚은 냉각이라 전형적인 오개념에 해당한다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Engineers often attach blocks of zinc to underwater steel pipelines. Because zinc corrodes more easily than steel, it gives up its electrons first and slowly wears away instead of the pipe. For this reason, some engineers claim that once zinc anodes are installed, a pipeline is protected for its entire working life and needs no further attention.

Text 2
Zinc anodes do shield steel pipelines, but only while the zinc lasts. As the anodes dissolve, they shrink, and when they are used up the steel itself begins to corrode. Divers and remote vehicles must therefore inspect pipelines regularly and replace worn anodes before they disappear completely.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim made by some engineers in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Engineers often attach blocks of zinc to underwater steel pipelines. Because zinc corrodes more easily than steel, it gives up its electrons first and slowly wears away instead of the pipe. For this reason, some engineers claim that once zinc anodes are installed, a pipeline is protected for its entire working life and needs no further attention.

That means the author of Text 2 would object to the claim, which makes B the answer. A is wrong because zinc corrodes more easily than steel, not more slowly. C ignores Text 2's point that the steel corrodes once the zinc is used up, and D is wrong because Text 2 says zinc does protect steel.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Early refracting telescopes had a stubborn flaw. Because glass bends blue light more strongly than red light, a single lens brings different colors to focus at slightly different distances. Many seventeenth-century astronomers concluded that this colored blurring could never be removed from any telescope that used lenses.

Text 2

problem.explanationEn: In Text 1, many astronomers concluded that the colored blurring in lens telescopes could never be removed. Text 2 explains that Dollond combined crown and flint glass so the second lens canceled most of the color spreading, which shows that conclusion was wrong, so C is correct. A is wrong because Text 2 describes a fix, so it would not agree the problem was permanent. B is wrong because Text 2 never blames craftsmanship; it accepts that glass bends colors differently. D is wrong because Text 2 treats sharper images as an important gain rather than saying the blurring didn't matter.

problem.passage:
Many impact-resistant composites contain polymer layers that absorb energy through viscoelastic behavior: when deformed, their long molecular chains slide and rearrange, converting some of the impact energy into heat. This dissipation is greatest near the polymer's glass transition temperature (Tg), the point at which the material shifts from a rigid, glassy state to a softer, rubbery one. Importantly, Tg is not fixed. The faster a polymer is deformed, the less time its chains have to rearrange, so the material behaves as though its Tg were higher. Materials engineer Priya Venkataraman tested a polymer whose Tg, measured under slow loading, is about 40°C below room temperature. In slow bending tests at room temperature, the polymer dissipated little energy, but under high-speed impact at the same temperature, it dissipated far more. These results suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Many impact-resistant composites contain polymer layers that absorb energy through viscoelastic behavior: when deformed, their long molecular chains slide and rearrange, converting some of the impact energy into heat. This dissipation is greatest near the polymer's glass transition temperature (Tg), the point at which the material shifts from a rigid, glassy state to a softer, rubbery one. Importantly, Tg is not fixed. The faster a polymer is deformed, the less time its chains have to rearrange, so the material behaves as though its Tg were higher. Materials engineer Priya Venkataraman tested a polymer whose Tg, measured under slow loading, is about 40°C below room temperature. In slow bending tests at room temperature, the polymer dissipated little energy, but under high-speed impact at the same temperature, it dissipated far more. These results suggest that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the polymer's slow-loading Tg must have been measured incorrectly, since its energy dissipation at room temperature should not vary with loading speed.
the polymer dissipates more energy under impact mainly because high-speed deformation heats it above its slow-loading Tg.
the polymer would dissipate even more energy in slow bending tests if those tests were conducted at a temperature well above room temperature.
the rapid deformation of an impact raised the polymer's effective Tg close to room temperature, placing the material in its range of greatest dissipation.
problem.explanation: 지문은 변형 속도가 빠를수록 유효 Tg가 올라가고, 에너지 소산은 Tg 근처에서 가장 크다고 말한다. 느린 하중에서 Tg는 실온보다 40°C 낮아 실온에서 소산이 적었지만, 충격 시 유효 Tg가 실온 근처로 올라가 소산이 커졌다고 보는 D가 두 정보를 연결한 결론이다. A는 Tg가 고정되지 않는다는 지문 내용과 모순된다. B는 열 발생을 언급하지만, 이 폴리머는 실온에서 이미 느린 하중 기준 Tg보다 높은 온도에 있으므로 원인을 설명하지 못한다. C는 온도를 올리면 Tg에서 더 멀어지므로 소산이 오히려 줄어들 것이라 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says faster deformation raises a polymer's effective Tg and that dissipation peaks near Tg. With slow loading, the Tg sits 40°C below room temperature, so dissipation was low; a fast impact would push the effective Tg up toward room temperature, which explains the much higher dissipation, so D is correct. A contradicts the passage's point that Tg is not fixed. B mentions heating, but at room temperature the polymer is already above its slow-loading Tg, so heating it further can't explain the result. C gets the direction wrong: raising the temperature would move the material even farther from its slow-loading Tg, so dissipation should go down, not up.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 느린 하중 Tg = 실온−40°C → 실온에서 Tg와 멀어 소산 적음. 빠른 변형 → 유효 Tg 상승 → 실온에 근접 → 소산 최대 영역. D가 유일하게 두 정보(속도에 따른 Tg 상승 + Tg 근처 소산 최대)를 연결함. A는 "Tg는 고정되지 않는다"와 모순, B는 이미 Tg 위에 있어 가열은 Tg에서 더 멀어지게 하므로 설명 불가, C는 온도 상승이 Tg에서 더 멀어지게 하므로 방향 오류. 시간-온도 중첩 원리와 부합해 과학적 사실 오류 없음. 해설 한·영 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 오답 B·C는 지문 일부(열 발생, 고무상이 더 부드러움)에 근거해 비교 필요 → medium 적합.

advisory.note: D는 '변형 속도↑ → 유효 Tg↑'와 '소산은 Tg 근처에서 최대'라는 두 정보를 연결한 결론이다. B는 열 언급, C는 온도 변화라는 그럴듯한 근거를 갖고 있어 오답으로서 매력이 있다. 다만 A는 지문과 대놓고 모순되어 쉽게 배제된다. medium 난이도에 적합하다.

The sentence after the blank gives what happens because of that change: the walls reflect more sunlight and let in less heat. That is a cause-and-effect relationship, so D is correct. A introduces an example, but the second sentence is a consequence, not an example. B signals a contrast or something unexpected, but a white surface reflecting sunlight is exactly what you would expect. C adds a similar but separate point, while the second sentence follows directly from the first.

problem.explanation: 목표는 에너지 저장 부품 설계자에게 이 소재가 매력적인 이유를 설명하는 것이다. D는 가볍고 전기를 잘 통한다는 특성을 슈퍼커패시터 전극 시험과 연결하여 목표를 달성한다. A는 소재의 구성만 설명할 뿐 에너지 저장과 무관하다. B는 연구 기록에 관한 사실로 에너지 저장 용도를 언급하지 않는다. C는 무게와 탄성을 말하지만 전기 전도성이나 에너지 저장과 연결하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The goal is to explain why graphene aerogel appeals to engineers building energy-storage parts. D does this by linking the material's light weight and good conductivity to its testing as a supercapacitor electrode. A only describes what the material is made of and never mentions energy storage. B reports a research record about lightness but says nothing about storing energy. C mentions that it is airy and springy, but it doesn't connect these traits to electricity or energy storage.

quality.seed: technology and engineering — Graphene aerogel mechanical strength and electrical conductivity enabling lightweight structural supercapacitor electrode materials

hardJudge.note: 정답 D는 노트의 '가벼움'·'전기 전도성'·'슈퍼커패시터 전극 시험'을 결합해 에너지 저장 설계자에게 매력적인 이유를 직접 설명한다. A(구성), B(2013 기록), C(공기·탄성)는 모두 노트에 근거하지만 에너지 저장 용도와 연결하지 않아 배제된다. 해설은 한·영 모두 글자 참조와 결론이 일치하며 자연스럽다. 노트 내용(Zhejiang University 2013 graphene aerogel, 슈퍼커패시터 전극 연구)은 사실과 부합한다. 단서가 노트에 직접 드러나고 한 단계 추론으로 풀리므로 easy에 적합하다.

advisory.note: D만 에너지 저장(슈퍼커패시터)을 언급하므로 단일 단서로 풀린다. 오답들은 메모의 다른 사실을 그대로 옮긴 전형적 오답이다. 2013년 저장대 기록(밀도 약 0.16 mg/cm³, 헬륨보다 가벼움)은 실제로 보고된 사실이다.

problem.passage:

problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Reverse osmosis is a process used in many desalination plants to turn seawater into drinking water.
- In reverse osmosis, pumps push seawater against a thin membrane at high pressure.
- The membrane is semipermeable: water molecules can pass through it, but most dissolved salt ions cannot.
- Modern membranes can block more than 99 percent of the salt in seawater.
- The Sorek plant in Israel, opened in 2013, is one of the largest reverse osmosis plants in the world.
problem.question: The student wants to explain how the membrane separates fresh water from salt. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Because the membrane lets water molecules through while stopping most dissolved salt ions, the water on the far side is nearly salt-free.
Because the Sorek plant opened in Israel in 2013, it has become one of the largest reverse osmosis plants in the world.
Because many desalination plants use reverse osmosis, seawater can be turned into drinking water in many places.
Because the membrane lets salt ions through while stopping most water molecules, the salt can be collected on the far side.
problem.explanation: 목표는 막이 담수와 소금을 어떻게 분리하는지 설명하는 것이며, 이는 반투과성 막에 관한 세 번째 메모와 직접 대응한다. A는 물 분자는 통과하고 염 이온은 막힌다는 메모를 정확히 활용하므로 정답이다. B는 소렉 플랜트에 관한 사실만 전달할 뿐 분리 원리를 설명하지 않는다. C는 역삼투가 널리 쓰인다는 점만 말하고 막의 작동 방식은 설명하지 않는다. D는 물과 염 이온의 역할을 뒤바꿔 메모와 어긋나는 부정확한 진술이다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to explain how the membrane separates fresh water from salt, and the third note speaks to that directly. A is correct because it uses that note accurately: water molecules pass through the membrane, but most salt ions don't. B only gives facts about the Sorek plant and never explains how the separation happens. C points out that reverse osmosis is widely used but doesn't say how the membrane works. D swaps the roles of water and salt ions, so it contradicts the notes.

quality.seed: technology and engineering — Reverse osmosis membrane semipermeable barrier and salt ion rejection in desalination plant freshwater production

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 세 번째 메모(반투과성 막: 물 통과, 염 이온 차단)를 정확히 반영하여 목표를 달성한다. B·C는 목표(분리 원리 설명)와 무관한 정보, D는 메모 내용을 뒤집은 진술로 배제된다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일한 결론과 선택지 참조를 갖고 모순이 없다. 다만 사소한 참고: 실제 SAT 수사적 종합 문항은 오답도 대개 메모와 사실적으로 일치하는 진술로 구성되는데 D는 메모를 반대로 뒤집은 '부정확 진술' 유형이며, B는 "2013년 개장했기 때문에 가장 큰 플랜트가 되었다"는 인과가 다소 억지스럽다. 그럼에도 easy 난이도의 전형적 오개념 오답으로 기능하므로 적합 판정.

advisory.note: B는 개업 연도와 규모 사이에 인과관계를 억지로 붙였지만, 목표와 무관한 오답이라 문제가 되지 않는다. D는 메모의 내용을 뒤집은 전형적인 오개념 선택지다. 쉬운 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Perovskite solar cells owe much of their promise to a flexible crystal lattice: by substituting bromide ions for some of the iodide ions in that lattice, researchers can widen the material's bandgap and shift which colors of light it absorbs. The ability of these thin films, which are often less than a micrometer thick, to absorb light across precisely chosen wavelengths ______ engineers to stack perovskite layers atop conventional silicon cells, capturing energy that silicon alone would miss.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Perovskite solar cells owe much of their promise to a flexible crystal lattice: by substituting bromide ions for some of the iodide ions in that lattice, researchers can widen the material's bandgap and shift which colors of light it absorbs. The ability of these thin films, which are often less than a micrometer thick, to absorb light across precisely chosen wavelengths ______ engineers to stack perovskite layers atop conventional silicon cells, capturing energy that silicon alone would miss.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The ability'이고, 'of these thin films...'와 'to absorb light across precisely chosen wavelengths'는 그 주어를 꾸미는 수식어이다. 따라서 단수 정동사인 D 'allows'가 와야 한다. A와 C는 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'wavelengths'나 'films'에 맞춘 복수 동사여서 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다. B는 분사 'allowing'이라 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 문장이 되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The ability," and both "of these thin films..." and "to absorb light across precisely chosen wavelengths" are modifiers describing it. So the blank needs a singular finite verb, which is D, "allows." A and C are plural verbs that agree with the nearby plural nouns "wavelengths" or "films" instead of the actual subject. B is the participle "allowing," which leaves the sentence with no main verb, so it isn't a complete sentence.

quality.seed: technology and engineering — Photovoltaic perovskite crystal structure and bandgap tuning enhancing light absorption efficiency in thin-film solar cells

hardJudge.note: 주어 'The ability'(단수)와 동사 사이에 'films', 'wavelengths' 등 복수 명사와 관계절이 끼어 있어 두 단계 판단(주어 식별 + 수 일치) 필요. D 'allows'만 단수 정동사로 정답 확인. A·C는 인접 복수 명사에 끌리는 함정, B는 정동사 결여 함정으로 오답 설계 적절. 해설 한·영 일치, 과학적 서술(브로마이드 치환으로 밴드갭 확대, 실리콘 탠덤) 사실에 부합.

advisory.note: 주어 'The ability'와 동사 사이에 삽입절과 to부정사구가 있어 복수 명사(films, wavelengths)로 수 일치를 유도하는 전형적인 medium 문항이다. 정답 D는 맞다. 다만 오답 중 '부분적으로 맞는 근거'가 있는 것은 사실상 A와 C 두 개뿐이고, B는 정동사가 아니어서 쉽게 배제된다.

problem.passage:
Engineers have begun printing flat sheets of shape-memory polymer that can fold themselves into three-dimensional structures. The sheets, which are stretched into a temporary shape while warm and then cooled so that the strain in each hinge region is locked in place, ______ toward their original geometry when reheated, bending along pre-programmed creases much as paper does in the hands of an origami artist.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Engineers have begun printing flat sheets of shape-memory polymer that can fold themselves into three-dimensional structures. The sheets, which are stretched into a temporary shape while warm and then cooled so that the strain in each hinge region is locked in place, ______ toward their original geometry when reheated, bending along pre-programmed creases much as paper does in the hands of an origami artist.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 주어 "The sheets"는 긴 관계절(which ... locked in place) 뒤에서 본동사를 필요로 하므로, 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사 C "recover"가 정답이다. A "recovering"과 D "having recovered"는 분사라서 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다. B "recovers"는 정동사이긴 하지만 단수형이다. 빈칸 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "place"나 "region", "strain"과 잘못 일치시킨 것이다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject "The sheets" is separated from its verb by a long relative clause (which ... locked in place), and the sentence still needs a main verb. C, "recover," is a finite plural verb that agrees with "sheets," so C is correct. A, "recovering," and D, "having recovered," are participles, so they would leave the sentence without a main verb. B, "recovers," is a finite verb, but it's singular. It wrongly agrees with nearby singular nouns like "strain," "region," or "place" instead of the actual subject.

quality.seed: technology and engineering — Shape-memory polymer thermal recovery and pre-programmed deformation enabling self-folding origami-inspired structures

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The sheets"가 긴 관계절(which ... locked in place)로 본동사와 분리된 구조. 빈칸은 문장의 유일한 본동사 자리이므로 정동사가 필요하고, 복수 주어와 일치하는 C "recover"가 유일한 정답. A·D는 비정동사(분사)로 본동사 부재, B는 인접 단수 명사(place/region/strain)에 끌린 오답으로 매력적. 한·영 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조이며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 형상기억고분자 자가접힘 소재는 실제 연구 분야로 사실 오류 없음. 긴 삽입절 + 수 일치의 두 단계 판단을 요구해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 주어와 동사 사이에 긴 관계절이 끼어 있는 수 일치 문항이다. 정동사가 필요한지 판단한 뒤 수 일치를 확인하는 두 단계가 필요하다. 바로 앞의 단수 명사 때문에 B가 유력한 오답으로 작동하므로 medium 수준에 맞다.

problem.passage:

The coating, a layer of silica nanoparticles bonded to fluorine-free polymer chains that together mimic the leaf's rough, water-shedding surface, ______ droplets to roll away while carrying off dust and dirt as well.

problem.stimulus: Inspired by the microscopic bumps and waxy nanostructures that cause water to bead and roll off lotus leaves, materials engineers have developed superhydrophobic coatings for rain jacket fabrics. The coating, a layer of silica nanoparticles bonded to fluorine-free polymer chains that together mimic the leaf's rough, water-shedding surface, ______ droplets to roll away while carrying off dust and dirt as well.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "The coating"이고, 콤마 사이의 긴 동격구(a layer ... surface)는 주어를 꾸미는 삽입어구일 뿐이므로 문장에는 단수 주어에 맞는 정동사가 필요하다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사(polymer chains, nanoparticles)에 끌려 복수형으로 맞춘 것이어서 주어-동사 일치가 틀린다. C와 D는 분사 형태여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되므로 완전한 문장이 되지 못한다. D는 완료형이어서 그럴듯해 보이지만 마찬가지로 정동사가 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The coating." The long phrase set off by commas (a layer ... surface) is just an appositive describing that subject, so the sentence still needs a main verb that agrees with a singular subject. That makes A correct. B is a main verb, but it's plural because it matches the nearby plural nouns ("polymer chains," "nanoparticles"), so the subject and verb don't agree. C and D are participles, which would leave the sentence with no main verb, so it wouldn't be a complete sentence. D may sound right because it's a perfect form, but it isn't a main verb either.

quality.seed: technology and engineering — Superhydrophobic textile coating lotus leaf mimicry and water repellent treatment applied to rain jacket fabrics

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The coating"(단수) + 긴 동격 삽입구 뒤에 정동사 필요 → A "causes"가 유일하게 맞음. B는 인접 복수명사(nanoparticles, polymer chains)에 의한 근접 일치 오답, C/D는 비정형 동사로 정동사 부재. 한/영 해설 모두 정답·글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음, 자연스러움. 연꽃잎 초소수성(lotus effect) 서술은 사실에 부합. 삽입구 길이와 복수명사 유인으로 두 단계 판단(주어 식별 + 정동사 여부)이 요구되어 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 긴 동격구가 주어와 동사 사이를 떼어 놓고, 동사 바로 앞에 복수 명사(surface 앞의 chains)가 있어 오답을 유도한다. 주어 찾기와 정동사 필요성 확인의 두 단계를 거쳐야 하는 전형적인 medium 문항이다. 정답은 A로 확정된다.

A와 D는 정동사이긴 하지만, 빈칸 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'temperatures'나 'grains'에 수를 맞춘 복수형이어서 단수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C 'allowing'은 분사라서 정동사가 아니므로, 이것을 넣으면 주절에 동사가 없어 문장이 성립하지 않는다.

The clause "which ... temperatures" just interrupts the sentence between the subject and its verb. So the sentence needs a singular finite verb, which makes B, "allows," the correct answer. A and D are finite verbs, but they're plural: they match the nearby plural nouns "temperatures" or "grains" instead of the actual subject. C, "allowing," is a participle, not a finite verb, so with C the main clause would have no verb and the sentence wouldn't be complete.

quality.seed: technology and engineering — Spark plasma sintering rapid consolidation and grain refinement in tungsten carbide tool bit manufacturing

hardJudge.note: 주어 'This rapid heating'(단수) + 긴 관계절 삽입 후 단수 정동사 'allows' 필요. 빈칸 앞 복수 명사(temperatures, grains)가 A/D를 유인하는 구조이고 C는 비정동사 오답으로, 표준 중간 난이도 주어-동사 일치 문항에 부합. 해설 한/영 모두 정확·일관하며 SPS 관련 내용도 사실에 부합.

advisory.note: 긴 관계절이 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어 근접 복수명사에 끌리는 오답을 유도하는 전형적인 medium 문항이다. SPS 관련 내용도 사실에 맞다.

problem.stimulus: In a conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) machine, DNA samples sit in plastic tubes inside a heavy metal block that must be repeatedly heated and cooled, and because the block itself is so massive, each temperature shift takes close to a minute. Microfluidic PCR devices avoid this delay: a few microliters of sample are pushed through hair-thin channels that pass back and forth over zones held at fixed temperatures, so only the tiny volume of liquid changes temperature, and it does so in about a second. ______ a full set of thirty amplification cycles, which typically takes more than an hour on a benchtop machine, can be completed on a palm-sized chip in under ten minutes.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 미세유체 장치에서 액체 온도가 약 1초 만에 바뀐다는 원인을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 결과로 전체 30회 증폭이 10분 안에 끝난다는 점을 말하므로 결과를 나타내는 C가 정답이다. problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the blank gives a cause: in a microfluidic device, the liquid changes temperature in about a second. A may look tempting because the passage does compare old and new devices, but that comparison already happened in the previous sentence, and the final sentence follows from that sentence instead of contrasting with it. B introduces something unexpected, but a shorter run time is exactly what you'd expect after faster temperature shifts. A looks like it adds one more trait, but the next sentence doesn't continue the list of strengths; it goes the opposite way. B might pull you in because the next sentence mentions "the same strong ionic attractions," but slow charging isn't a result of advantages like the wide temperature range. C is wrong because the next sentence isn't an example of the strengths described before it.

With no voltage applied, the molecules form a gentle helix that rotates incoming light by 90 degrees, so the light passes through the second filter and the pixel appears bright. ______ when a voltage is applied across the cell, the molecules tilt to align with the electric field, the helix unwinds, and the light reaches the second filter unrotated, where it is blocked, leaving the pixel dark.

The next sentence describes the opposite case: with voltage applied, the helix unwinds and the pixel goes dark. That contrast makes B correct. A might look tempting because the second sentence contains a chain of causes, but the dark state with voltage is not a result of the bright state described before it. C would make the second sentence an example of the first, when it actually describes a different condition with a different outcome. D says the two states are alike, but bright and dark are opposites.

hardJudge.note: 두 조건(무전압=밝음 / 전압=어두움)의 대조 관계를 파악해야 하며, A는 뒤 문장 내부의 인과 연쇄 때문에 훑어 읽으면 고르기 쉬운 매력적 오답이다. C·D는 상대적으로 약하지만 말이 된다. TN-LCD 동작 설명은 과학적으로 정확하고, 한·영 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침한다.

problem.stimulus: Ferrofluids, liquids in which nanoscale iron oxide particles are suspended, behave like ordinary oils until a magnet approaches. When a field is applied, the particles align along the field lines and the fluid stiffens almost instantly______ it relaxes just as quickly, allowing the lens to glide back into place with submicron accuracy.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "the particles align ... almost instantly"와 뒤 "it relaxes just as quickly"는 각각 독립절이므로 경계에 세미콜론이 필요하고, 두 번째 절 앞의 도입 종속절 "when the field is removed" 뒤에는 쉼표를 찍어 주절과 구분하는 것이 관례이다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 두 독립절을 쉼표로만 잇는 콤마 스플라이스이며, A는 삽입구처럼 보이게 쉼표를 붙였지만 경계 문제를 해결하지 못한다. B는 세미콜론은 맞지만 도입 종속절 뒤 쉼표가 빠져 "removed it"이 이어 읽혀 의미가 혼동된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank ("the particles align ... almost instantly") and the text after it ("it relaxes just as quickly") are both independent clauses, so a semicolon is needed between them. The second clause also opens with the dependent clause "when the field is removed," which should be followed by a comma to set it apart from the main clause. That makes C correct. A and D join two independent clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice; A's extra comma makes the phrase look like an aside, but it still leaves the clause boundary unmarked. B uses the semicolon correctly but leaves out the comma after the introductory clause, so "removed it" runs together and becomes confusing.

hardJudge.note: 정답 C는 옳다(독립절 경계 세미콜론 + 도입 종속절 뒤 쉼표). A·D는 콤마 스플라이스로 명확히 배제된다. 다만 B와 C의 차이가 도입 종속절 뒤 쉼표 유무뿐이라 실제 SAT에서는 잘 쓰지 않는 미세한 구분이며, B를 '틀렸다'고 단정하기엔 논쟁 여지가 있다. 해설은 정답과 일치하고 한·영 해설도 결론·글자 참조가 동일하다. 지문의 과학적 내용(자성유체의 자기장 반응, 광학 위치결정 스테이지 활용)은 사실에 부합한다.

advisory.note: 두 단계 판단이 필요한 문항이다. 먼저 독립절 사이의 경계에 세미콜론이 와야 하고, 이어서 도입 종속절 뒤에 쉼표가 와야 한다. 각 오답에도 부분적으로 맞는 요소가 있어 medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.stimulus: Engineers developing compostable food packaging have turned to nanocellulose, a material made of plant-derived fibers only a few nanometers wide. When these fibers are dispersed through a biodegradable polymer matrix such as polylactic acid, the composite gains stiffness without losing its ability to break down in industrial compost. The fibers' tendency to clump during mixing, a problem that weakens the finished film in unpredictable ______ researchers to coat each fiber with a thin surface treatment before blending.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 주어는 "The fibers' tendency to clump during mixing"이고 동사는 "has led"이다. 그 사이의 "a problem that ... ways"는 쉼표로 시작한 비필수 동격 삽입구이므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 세미콜론은 주어와 동사를 갈라 놓아 앞뒤 어느 쪽도 독립절이 되지 못한다. C는 삽입구를 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 "ways"가 주어처럼 읽히고, D는 "and"가 주어의 유일한 동사 앞에 붙어 있어 이어 줄 대상이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject is "The fibers' tendency to clump during mixing," and its verb is "has led." The phrase in between, "a problem that ... ways," is a nonessential appositive that opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma too. That makes A correct. B puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, so neither side can stand as an independent clause. C leaves out the closing comma, which makes "ways" look like the subject, and D puts "and" in front of the subject's only verb, so there is nothing for it to connect.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 주어 "The fibers' tendency to clump during mixing" + 비필수 동격구 "a problem that ... ways" + 동사 "has led". 여는 쉼표에 대응하는 닫는 쉼표가 필요하므로 A가 유일하게 옳음. B(세미콜론은 독립절 분리용), C(닫는 쉼표 누락), D(단일 동사 앞 and로 연결 대상 없음) 모두 배제 근거 타당. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 긴 주어와 삽입구 경계를 파악해야 하므로 medium 적합. 지문은 독창적 서술로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 동격 삽입구를 닫는 쉼표 문제다. 주어와 동사를 찾은 뒤 삽입구의 경계를 확인하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. C는 'in unpredictable ways has led'처럼 자연스럽게 읽혀 훑어 읽으면 고르기 쉬운 오답이고, B와 D도 그럴듯해 보인다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

Before deposition begins, the tool is bombarded with argon ions, a cleaning step that strips away surface oxides and roughens the substrate at the nanoscale ______ the coating that follows anchors itself far more firmly than it would to an untreated surface.

problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격 수식어(a cleaning step that...)가 붙어 있지만 'the tool is bombarded'라는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'the coating ... anchors itself'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 접속부사 as a result로 잇는 경우에는 그 앞에 세미콜론, 뒤에 쉼표를 써야 하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 두 절 사이에 아무 경계 부호가 없어 run-on 문장이 된다. D는 'resulting in' 뒤에 명사구가 와야 하는데 완전한 절(the coating ... anchors)이 와서 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Even though a long appositive (a cleaning step that...) comes before the blank, the text before it is still an independent clause built on "the tool is bombarded." The text after the blank, "the coating ... anchors itself," is also an independent clause. When you join two independent clauses with the conjunctive adverb "as a result," you need a semicolon before it and a comma after it, so B is correct. A joins the two clauses with only commas, which makes a comma splice. C puts no boundary punctuation between the clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence. D doesn't work because "resulting in" has to be followed by a noun phrase, not a full clause like "the coating ... anchors."

advisory.note: 빈칸 앞 동격 수식어 때문에 앞 절이 독립절인지 판단하기 어렵고, 오답 A와 D도 그럴듯해 보인다. 학생은 절 경계를 확인한 뒤 접속부사 구두점 규칙을 적용하는 두 단계를 거쳐야 하므로 medium 난이도에 맞다. PVD와 아르곤 이온 세정에 관한 내용도 사실과 맞다.

problem.passage:
Liquid air energy storage plants cool air until it condenses, store it in insulated tanks, and later let it boil and expand to drive turbines. Early prototypes wasted much of the cold released during that boiling, but engineers at one pilot facility in northern England captured it in beds of gravel and reused it to chill incoming air during the next charging cycle. This recovery did not eliminate the need for compressors and refrigeration, but it ______ the electricity they consumed, raising the plant's round-trip efficiency by roughly a third.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Liquid air energy storage plants cool air until it condenses, store it in insulated tanks, and later let it boil and expand to drive turbines. Early prototypes wasted much of the cold released during that boiling, but engineers at one pilot facility in northern England captured it in beds of gravel and reused it to chill incoming air during the next charging cycle. This recovery did not eliminate the need for compressors and refrigeration, but it ______ the electricity they consumed, raising the plant's round-trip efficiency by roughly a third.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 재활용한 냉기가 압축기·냉동 장치를 없애지는 못했지만 효율을 높였다는 대조 구조이므로, 그 장치들이 쓰는 전력을 '줄였다'는 뜻의 B(curtailed)가 맞다. C(replaced)는 전력을 대체했다는 뜻이 되어 '필요를 없애지 못했다'는 앞 절과 충돌한다. D(redirected)는 냉기가 다른 곳에 쓰였다는 점과 표면적으로 연결되지만, 전력 사용 방향을 바꾼다고 효율이 오르는 것은 아니므로 감소라는 핵심을 놓친다. A(concealed)는 전력 소비를 숨겼다는 뜻으로, 실제 효율 향상과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence sets up a contrast: the recovered cold didn't remove the need for compressors and refrigeration, but it still raised efficiency. So the cold must have reduced the electricity those machines used, which makes B (curtailed) the answer. C (replaced) would mean the electricity was substituted entirely, and that clashes with the statement that the machines were still needed. D (redirected) might seem to fit because the cold was put to new use, but changing where electricity goes wouldn't raise efficiency, so it misses the idea of a reduction. A (concealed) means hiding the consumption, which doesn't match a real gain in efficiency.

hardJudge.note: 'did not eliminate... but it ___ the electricity... raising efficiency' 구조상 '줄였다'가 유일하게 논리적이며 B(curtailed)가 정답. C(replaced)는 앞 절과 모순, D(redirected)는 재활용 맥락과 표면적으로 연결되어 비교가 필요한 매력적 오답, A도 문장 자체는 성립. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 선택지 글자와 결론이 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 실제 Highview Power 파일럿은 Slough(남부)였으나 지문은 특정 시설을 명시하지 않은 일반화된 서술이라 유의미한 사실 오류로 보지 않음. 저작권 의심 없음. 대조 구조 파악 + 효율 상승 결과와의 연결이라는 두 단계 판단이 요구되어 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 대조 구조(did not eliminate ~ but)와 효율 상승이라는 문맥을 함께 봐야 해서 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. replaced와 redirected는 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답이다. 영국 Highview 파일럿 시설의 자갈층 냉열 회수는 사실과 대체로 부합한다.

problem.passage:
Engineers designing holographic displays often rely on diffractive optical elements, thin films etched with microscopic interference patterns that bend incoming light to reconstruct a three-dimensional image. These elements are highly wavelength selective: a pattern recorded for green laser light diffracts green light efficiently but redirects red or blue light only weakly and at the wrong angles. For this reason, a display that must reproduce full color cannot simply ______ a single element; instead, designers stack separate layers, each tuned to one of the three laser wavelengths, so that every color is reconstructed in the correct position.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Engineers designing holographic displays often rely on diffractive optical elements, thin films etched with microscopic interference patterns that bend incoming light to reconstruct a three-dimensional image. These elements are highly wavelength selective: a pattern recorded for green laser light diffracts green light efficiently but redirects red or blue light only weakly and at the wrong angles. For this reason, a display that must reproduce full color cannot simply ______ a single element; instead, designers stack separate layers, each tuned to one of the three laser wavelengths, so that every color is reconstructed in the correct position.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문에서 소자 하나는 한 파장만 효율적으로 회절시키므로, 풀컬러 디스플레이는 단일 소자에 '의존할' 수 없고 대신 여러 층을 쌓는다고 했다. 따라서 'instead'와 대조를 이루는 C가 정답이다. A는 보정이라는 공학적 맥락에 어울려 보이지만, 문제는 보정이 아니라 단일 소자로는 세 색을 감당할 수 없다는 점이다. B는 제작을 뜻하는데, 단일 소자를 만드는 것 자체가 불가능하다는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 빛과 관련되어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 단일 소자에 빛을 비추는 것 자체는 가능하며 지문이 문제 삼는 핵심이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says each element diffracts only one wavelength efficiently, so a full-color display can't rely on a single element and instead stacks several layers. That contrast with "instead" makes C the answer. A sounds right in an engineering context, but the problem isn't adjusting the element; one element just can't handle three colors. B means making the element, and the passage never says a single element can't be made. D fits the topic of light, but shining light on one element is possible, and that isn't the problem the passage describes.

A(calibrate)·B(fabricate)는 공학 맥락상 부분적 타당성이 있어 비교가 필요하고, D(illuminate)도 빛 주제와 연결되어 말이 됨. 회절 광학 소자의 파장 선택성 및 RGB 적층 구조 서술은 사실에 부합. 한·영 해설 모두 C를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 선택지 중 C만 두 단어 구이지만 '단어 또는 구' 유형상 허용 범위.

advisory.note: 파장 선택성 → 단일 소자 불충분 → instead 대조 확인의 두 단계 추론이 필요함. calibrate/illuminate가 그럴듯한 오답 역할을 함. 중간 난이도에 적합.

problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- A McKibben actuator is a type of pneumatic artificial muscle first developed in the 1950s for use in orthotic devices.
- It consists of an inflatable rubber bladder surrounded by a sleeve of braided nylon fibers.
- When compressed air fills the bladder, the braided sleeve widens and shortens, pulling on whatever is attached to its ends.
- Biological muscle tissue also shortens and thickens as it contracts, which is why engineers say the actuator mimics muscle.
- Unlike biological muscle, which can shorten by roughly 40 percent of its resting length, a typical McKibben actuator shortens by only about 25 percent.
problem.question: The student wants to point out a limitation of the device relative to the tissue it imitates. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Like biological muscle tissue, a McKibben actuator shortens and thickens as it contracts, pulling on whatever is attached to its ends.
A McKibben actuator, first developed in the 1950s for orthotic devices, shortens by about 25 percent when compressed air fills its rubber bladder.
Because its braided nylon sleeve widens and shortens when air fills the bladder, a McKibben actuator behaves much as biological muscle tissue does.
Although a McKibben actuator contracts in a musclelike way, it shortens by only about 25 percent of its length, whereas biological muscle can shorten by roughly 40 percent.
problem.explanation: 목표는 이 장치가 모방하는 생체 근육보다 못한 점(한계)을 지적하는 것이다. D는 액추에이터의 수축률(약 25%)과 생체 근육의 수축률(약 40%)을 대비해 한계를 분명히 보여 준다. A와 C는 정확한 메모를 쓰지만 둘의 유사점만 강조해 한계를 드러내지 못한다. B는 25%라는 수치를 언급하지만 근육의 40%와 비교하지 않아 그것이 한계인지 알 수 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to show a way the device falls short of the muscle tissue it copies. D does this by contrasting the actuator's roughly 25 percent shortening with muscle's roughly 40 percent. A and C use accurate notes but only point out similarities, so they don't show any limitation. B gives the 25 percent figure but never compares it with muscle, so you can't tell from that sentence that it's a shortcoming.

hardJudge.note: D만이 액추에이터 25%와 근육 40%를 직접 대비해 '모방 대상 대비 한계'라는 목표를 충족. A·C는 유사점만, B는 수치만 제시해 비교가 없음. 오답 B가 부분 근거를 가져 비교 판단이 필요하므로 medium 적합. 해설 한·영 일치, 메모와 사실 부합.

advisory.note: B는 수치는 있지만 비교가 없어 부분적으로만 맞는 매력적 오답이고, A와 C는 유사점만 말한다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다. 다만 메모의 '25%'를 B·D가 그대로 쓰며 '휴지 길이 대비'라는 점은 생략되어 있는데, 이는 문제가 되지 않는다.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Cutting tools used in metal machining wear down from friction and heat at the point where the tool meets the workpiece.
- Physical vapor deposition (PVD) is a process in which a hard material, such as titanium aluminum nitride, is vaporized in a vacuum chamber and condensed onto a tool as a thin film.
- Plasma-assisted PVD bombards the tool surface with ionized gas before and during coating, which cleans the surface and helps the film bond more tightly.
- In a 2019 trial, uncoated carbide drills lasted an average of 410 holes in hardened steel before needing replacement.
- Identical drills given a plasma-assisted PVD coating lasted an average of 1,150 holes under the same conditions.

The student wants to emphasize how much the treatment affected the drills' service life. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Cutting tools used in metal machining wear down from friction and heat at the point where the tool meets the workpiece.
- Physical vapor deposition (PVD) is a process in which a hard material, such as titanium aluminum nitride, is vaporized in a vacuum chamber and condensed onto a tool as a thin film.
- Plasma-assisted PVD bombards the tool surface with ionized gas before and during coating, which cleans the surface and helps the film bond more tightly.
- In a 2019 trial, uncoated carbide drills lasted an average of 410 holes in hardened steel before needing replacement.
- Identical drills given a plasma-assisted PVD coating lasted an average of 1,150 holes under the same conditions.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize how much the treatment affected the drills' service life. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In plasma-assisted PVD, ionized gas strikes the tool surface before and during coating, cleaning it so that the titanium aluminum nitride film bonds more tightly.
In a 2019 trial, carbide drills given a plasma-assisted PVD coating lasted an average of 1,150 holes in hardened steel before needing replacement.
In a 2019 trial, drills with a plasma-assisted PVD coating lasted an average of 1,150 holes in hardened steel, nearly triple the 410 holes managed by identical uncoated drills.
In a 2019 trial, uncoated carbide drills, which wear down from friction and heat, lasted an average of 410 holes in hardened steel before needing replacement.
problem.explanation: 목표는 처리(코팅)가 드릴 수명에 미친 영향의 크기를 강조하는 것이므로, 코팅된 드릴과 코팅되지 않은 드릴의 수치를 함께 비교해야 한다. C는 1,150개와 410개를 나란히 제시하고 '거의 세 배'라고 차이를 밝혀 목표를 달성한다. A는 코팅이 더 잘 붙는 원리를 설명할 뿐 수명 변화는 보여주지 않는다. B는 코팅된 드릴의 수치만 있어 비교 기준이 없으므로 영향의 크기를 알 수 없다. D는 코팅되지 않은 드릴의 수치만 제시해 처리의 효과를 보여주지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to emphasize how much the coating changed the drills' service life, so you need both numbers side by side. C does this: it gives 1,150 holes against 410 holes and describes the gap as nearly triple. A explains how the plasma helps the coating bond, but it says nothing about how long the drills lasted. B gives only the coated drills' result, so there's nothing to compare it with, and you can't tell how big the effect was. D gives only the uncoated drills' result, so it doesn't show what the treatment did.

hardJudge.note: 1,150/410 ≈ 2.8이므로 '거의 세 배' 표현은 정확함. C만이 두 수치를 비교해 영향의 크기를 보여주며, B·D는 각각 한쪽 수치만 제시해 부분적으로 관련 있는 오답, A는 원리 설명으로 그럴듯한 오답. 한·영 해설 모두 C를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치. 표준 SAT medium 수준에 부합.
